# DataFusion Advanced — 13) Nested data support

Style target follows the uploaded advanced-reference pattern. 

## 13.0 Nested-data mental model

```text id="tq8tg3"
Arrow / DataFusion nested types
  ├─ ARRAY / LIST
  │   ├─ variable-length list values
  │   ├─ element type + element nullability
  │   └─ SQL / Expr list functions
  ├─ STRUCT
  │   ├─ named child fields
  │   ├─ child type + child nullability
  │   └─ field access / struct functions / unnest(struct)
  ├─ MAP
  │   ├─ key-value nested representation
  │   ├─ unique non-null keys for make_map
  │   └─ map functions + element access
  └─ Parquet / Arrow nested IO
      ├─ read support
      ├─ write support
      └─ field access + pruning opportunities
```

DataFusion’s feature matrix explicitly lists nested type support for `ARRAY`/`LIST` and `STRUCT`, including read support, write support, field access using `col['field']` and `col[1]`, array functions, struct functions, and Postgres JSON operators such as `->` and `->>`. It also lists Parquet support for primitive and nested types. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

---

## 13.1 Value case: why nested types matter

| Workload                    | Nested-data value                                                                        |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| event logs                  | keep `attributes`, `tags`, `context`, `device`, `geo` in columnar nested form            |
| semi-structured ingestion   | avoid premature JSON-string parsing at every query                                       |
| lakehouse Parquet           | preserve nested schemas from Spark/Arrow/Delta/Iceberg-style producers                   |
| vector search / ML features | arrays/lists for embeddings and dense numeric feature vectors                            |
| API payload analysis        | structs/maps model object-like payloads                                                  |
| telemetry                   | arrays for repeated labels, structs for grouped sensor fields                            |
| projection/pushdown         | access only needed nested leaves where engine/source supports it                         |
| generated SQL               | `col['field']`, array functions, and struct construction reduce UDF/custom-code pressure |

Operational principle:

```text id="yoa0tx"
Prefer native Arrow nested columns over opaque JSON strings when:
  - fields are queried repeatedly
  - schemas are known or semi-stable
  - Parquet/Arrow IO is available
  - type-aware filters/projections matter
```

---

## 13.2 Type vocabulary

| SQL / user term        | Arrow/DataFusion type concept    | Notes                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `ARRAY<T>` / `LIST<T>` | Arrow list-like array            | variable-length list values; list may be null; elements may be null                                          |
| fixed-size array       | Arrow fixed-size list            | each list has fixed length; useful for embeddings/vectors                                                    |
| `STRUCT<a:T,b:U>`      | Arrow `Struct`                   | named child arrays; struct value itself can be null                                                          |
| `MAP<K,V>` / map-like  | Arrow `Map` / map functions      | key-value nested representation; map-construction functions require non-null unique keys in documented cases |
| JSON-like object       | usually `STRUCT` or `MAP`        | choose struct for known fields, map for dynamic keys                                                         |
| JSON array             | usually `LIST`                   | list element type must be compatible/coercible                                                               |
| top-level table row    | `RecordBatch` row across columns | not the same as a struct column, though convertible in some Arrow APIs                                       |

Arrow’s Rust `StructArray` docs describe struct arrays as arrays of structs whose children are represented by separate arrays; they also distinguish `StructArray` from `RecordBatch`: both are collections of same-length arrays, but `StructArray` can be nested and can have top-level nulls, while `RecordBatch` has top-level schema metadata and cannot represent a whole-row null. ([Docs.rs][2])

---

## 13.3 `ARRAY` / `LIST` construction in SQL

### Literal arrays

```sql id="qlj1j6"
SELECT [1, 2, 3] AS ints;

SELECT ['red', 'green', 'blue'] AS colors;

SELECT [1, NULL, 3] AS nullable_ints;
```

### Function construction

```sql id="2wrseb"
SELECT make_array(1, 2, 3) AS ints;

SELECT make_list('a', 'b', 'c') AS strings;

SELECT range(0, 10) AS zero_to_nine;

SELECT generate_series(1, 10, 3) AS series;
```

DataFusion’s array-function catalog includes `make_array`, `make_list`, `range`, `generate_series`, many `array_*` and `list_*` aliases, vector functions, and shape/access functions. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### Arrays of structs

```sql id="bh67ge"
SELECT [
  {name: 'alice', age: 30},
  {name: 'bob', age: 25}
] AS users;
```

### Nested arrays

```sql id="a1htmq"
SELECT [
  [1, 2],
  [3, 4],
  [5, NULL]
] AS matrix_like;
```

Agent rules:

```text id="21fai8"
Array elements must have a compatible unified type.
Use explicit casts when element type inference is ambiguous.
Use arrays for repeated homogeneous values.
Use arrays of structs for repeated records.
Use maps for dynamic key-value bags.
Avoid unbounded array expansion without LIMIT / cardinality controls.
```

---

## 13.4 `ARRAY` / `LIST` Rust construction

### Arrow list builder

```rust id="4c05ss"
use std::sync::Arc;

use datafusion::arrow::{
    array::{ArrayRef, Int32Builder, ListBuilder},
    datatypes::{DataType, Field, Schema},
    record_batch::RecordBatch,
};

let mut builder = ListBuilder::new(Int32Builder::new());

// [1, 2]
builder.values().append_value(1);
builder.values().append_value(2);
builder.append(true);

// NULL list
builder.append(false);

// [] empty but non-null list
builder.append(true);

// [3, NULL]
builder.values().append_value(3);
builder.values().append_null();
builder.append(true);

let list_array: ArrayRef = Arc::new(builder.finish());

let schema = Arc::new(Schema::new(vec![
    Field::new(
        "values",
        DataType::List(Arc::new(Field::new_list_field(DataType::Int32, true))),
        true,
    ),
]));

let batch = RecordBatch::try_new(schema, vec![list_array])?;
```

Arrow’s Rust builder docs show `ListBuilder::new(Int32Builder::new())`, appending child values, then appending list validity; the example produces `[[1, 2], null, [], [3, null]]`. ([Docs.rs][4])

### List representation note

`ListArray` is an alias for `GenericListArray<i32>`, and Arrow’s generic list array stores variable-size lists using offsets into a child values array; `LargeListArray` uses `i64` offsets. ([Docs.rs][5])

Agent rules:

```text id="0r9800"
Use ListBuilder for nested list construction.
Call builder.values() to append element values.
Call builder.append(true/false) to finish each parent list slot.
Remember [] and NULL list are different.
Use DataType::List(FieldRef(element_field)).
Use datafusion::arrow re-exports to avoid Arrow-version mismatch.
```

---

## 13.5 Array/list access and functions

### Bracket access

```sql id="q6jeub"
SELECT
  tags[1] AS first_tag,
  embedding[3] AS third_component
FROM events;
```

DataFusion’s feature page explicitly lists nested field access with `col[1]` for nested values. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

### Element extraction functions

```sql id="85mk7h"
SELECT
  array_element(tags, 1) AS tag_1,
  array_extract(tags, 1) AS tag_1_alt,
  array_position(tags, 'vip') AS vip_pos,
  array_positions(tags, 'vip') AS vip_positions
FROM users;
```

The array-function index includes element access and position functions such as `array_element`, `array_extract`, `array_position`, `array_positions`, and `array_indexof`. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### Membership and overlap

```sql id="7rrx2m"
SELECT
  array_contains(tags, 'vip') AS has_vip,
  array_has_all(tags, ['vip', 'paid']) AS has_all_required,
  array_has_any(tags, ['fraud', 'blocked']) AS has_any_risk,
  arrays_overlap(tags, ['promo', 'beta']) AS overlaps_marketing
FROM users;
```

### Shape / cardinality

```sql id="kwk145"
SELECT
  array_length(tags) AS tag_count,
  cardinality(tags) AS tag_cardinality,
  array_dims(matrix_like) AS dims,
  array_ndims(matrix_like) AS rank,
  array_empty(tags) AS no_tags
FROM events;
```

### Transform / cleanup

```sql id="4vm3ge"
SELECT
  array_compact(tags) AS tags_no_nulls,
  array_distinct(tags) AS unique_tags,
  array_sort(tags) AS sorted_tags,
  array_reverse(tags) AS reversed_tags,
  array_slice(tags, 1, 3) AS first_three,
  array_join(tags, ',') AS tags_csv
FROM events;
```

### Set-like operations

```sql id="a16hdj"
SELECT
  array_union(tags_a, tags_b) AS all_tags,
  array_intersect(tags_a, tags_b) AS common_tags,
  array_except(tags_a, tags_b) AS only_a
FROM profiles;
```

### Vector math

```sql id="rjha2w"
SELECT
  dot_product(query_embedding, doc_embedding) AS dot,
  cosine_distance(query_embedding, doc_embedding) AS cosine_dist,
  array_normalize(embedding) AS unit_embedding
FROM vectors;
```

The array-function catalog includes set-like functions, vector functions, shape functions, mutation-like transformations, and list aliases such as `list_*`; use the exact function name set of the pinned DataFusion version. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

Agent rules:

```text id="6gfjym"
Use array_length/cardinality before unnest to estimate explosion.
Use array_contains/has_any/has_all for tag predicates.
Use vector functions only on numeric arrays with compatible lengths.
Normalize array order before equality/snapshot comparisons if order is not semantic.
Prefer list_* aliases only if house style is LIST; otherwise standardize on array_*.
```

---

## 13.6 `STRUCT` construction in SQL

### Struct literal

```sql id="ln6ssa"
SELECT {name: 'Alice', age: 30} AS person;
```

### `named_struct`

```sql id="rjfe95"
SELECT
  named_struct('lat', lat, 'lon', lon) AS point
FROM events;
```

`named_struct` returns an Arrow struct using name/input-expression pairs; field names must be constant strings, and inputs can be constants, columns, functions, arithmetic, or string expressions. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### `struct` / `row`

```sql id="xgo6za"
SELECT
  struct(user_id AS id, email AS email, country AS country) AS user_obj
FROM users;

SELECT
  row(a, b) AS row_struct
FROM t;
```

The `struct` function converts expressions into one struct column and uses aliases for field names where provided; `row` is documented as an alias. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### Agent rules

```text id="o49t3o"
Use STRUCT for fixed known fields.
Use named_struct when names are constant-string arguments.
Use struct(expr AS field_name, ...) for readable SQL.
Use row only when positional/generated field names are acceptable.
Avoid duplicate field names.
Alias the resulting struct column.
```

---

## 13.7 Struct Rust construction

```rust id="nboh0q"
use std::sync::Arc;

use datafusion::arrow::{
    array::{ArrayRef, BooleanArray, Int32Array, StructArray},
    datatypes::{DataType, Field},
};

let flag: ArrayRef = Arc::new(BooleanArray::from(vec![false, true, true]));
let score: ArrayRef = Arc::new(Int32Array::from(vec![10, 20, 30]));

let struct_array = StructArray::from(vec![
    (
        Arc::new(Field::new("flag", DataType::Boolean, false)),
        flag,
    ),
    (
        Arc::new(Field::new("score", DataType::Int32, false)),
        score,
    ),
]);

assert_eq!(struct_array.len(), 3);
```

Arrow’s `StructArray` docs show construction from a vector of `(Field, ArrayRef)` pairs; each child field is represented by a separate array, and child arrays must have equal length. ([Docs.rs][2])

Agent rules:

```text id="yvhlq6"
StructArray child arrays must have equal length.
Struct field order exists physically, but DataFusion struct coercion is often name-based.
A struct value may be NULL even if child arrays have values.
RecordBatch cannot represent a top-level null row; StructArray can.
Use StructArray for nested object columns, not for whole tables unless converting deliberately.
```

---

## 13.8 Struct field access

### Bracket access

```sql id="oab45t"
SELECT
  person['name'] AS name,
  person['age'] AS age
FROM people;
```

DataFusion’s `get_field` docs state that most users invoke it indirectly with field access syntax such as `my_struct_col['field_name']`, which becomes `get_field(my_struct_col, 'field_name')`. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### Nested field access

```sql id="u5fgka"
SELECT
  profile['address']['city'] AS city,
  profile['address']['zip'] AS zip
FROM users;
```

Nested access such as `my_struct['a']['b']` is optimized into a single `get_field(my_struct, 'a', 'b')` call, and `get_field` supports multiple field-name arguments for nested access. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### Explicit `get_field`

```sql id="qw8qgl"
SELECT
  get_field(profile, 'address', 'city') AS city
FROM users;
```

### Arrow schema inspection + access

```sql id="2dtawt"
SELECT
  arrow_field(profile) AS profile_field,
  arrow_field(profile)['data_type'] AS profile_type
FROM users
LIMIT 1;
```

`arrow_field` returns a struct containing Arrow field information including name, data type, nullability, and metadata, and its own result can be accessed with bracket syntax, as shown by `arrow_field(1)['data_type']`. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### Agent rules

```text id="x9wivn"
Use col['field'] for static field names.
Use get_field(col, dynamic_name_expr) when field name is dynamic.
Use chained bracket syntax for readability.
Use get_field(col, 'a', 'b') in generated SQL for normalized nested access.
Field names are strings; quote/escape field names carefully.
```

---

## 13.9 Map-like fields

### Map construction

```sql id="sbqo7i"
SELECT MAP('type', 'click') AS attrs;

SELECT MAP { 'type': 'click', 'source': 'web' } AS attrs;

SELECT MAKE_MAP(['POST', 'HEAD'], [41, 33]) AS method_counts;
```

DataFusion map functions include `map`, `make_map`, `map_entries`, `map_extract`, `map_keys`, and `map_values`; `make_map` creates a map from two lists, and each key must be unique and non-null. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### Map extraction

```sql id="nkqx9m"
SELECT
  map_extract(attrs, 'type') AS type_value,
  element_at(attrs, 'source') AS source_value,
  map_keys(attrs) AS keys,
  map_values(attrs) AS values,
  map_entries(attrs) AS entries
FROM events;
```

`element_at` is documented as an alias of `map_extract`. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### Agent rules

```text id="m4yods"
Use STRUCT for known fixed fields.
Use MAP for dynamic keys.
Keys must be unique and non-null for make_map.
Map value types should be compatible/coercible.
For frequent filters on known fields, prefer STRUCT columns over MAP.
```

---

## 13.10 Postgres JSON-style operators

### Feature claim and usage stance

DataFusion’s feature page lists support for Postgres JSON operators such as `->` and `->>` under nested/struct support. Treat these as syntactic conveniences for nested object access and scalar/text extraction, and verify exact behavior under the pinned DataFusion version because operator semantics depend on input type and SQL parser/planner behavior. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

### Representative patterns

```sql id="a56moh"
SELECT
  payload -> 'user' AS user_obj,
  payload -> 'user' -> 'id' AS user_id_value,
  payload ->> 'event_type' AS event_type_text
FROM events;
```

### Agent rules

```text id="4wj1z9"
Prefer bracket/get_field for Arrow STRUCT/MAP access in generated DataFusion-native SQL.
Use -> / ->> when Postgres-style compatibility is a product requirement.
Golden-test -> vs ->> output types with arrow_typeof.
Do not assume JSON-string parsing semantics for Arrow STRUCT columns without tests.
```

---

## 13.11 `unnest`: row/column expansion

### Array/map expansion

```sql id="6wde1x"
SELECT
  user_id,
  unnest(tags) AS tag
FROM users;
```

`unnest` expands an array or map into rows; its input can be a constant, column, function, or combination of array operators. ([Apache DataFusion][6])

### Struct expansion

```sql id="mimqiv"
SELECT
  unnest(struct_column)
FROM foov;
```

`unnest(struct)` expands a struct’s fields into individual columns, and each field can be accessed via names like `"<table>.<struct>.<field>"`; the docs show `unnest(struct_column)` producing separate columns for fields `a` and `b`. ([Apache DataFusion][6])

### Generate rows from arrays

```sql id="24t754"
SELECT unnest(make_array(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)) AS n;

SELECT unnest(range(0, 10)) AS n;
```

DataFusion’s special-function examples show both `unnest(make_array(...))` and `unnest(range(0, 10))`. ([Apache DataFusion][6])

### Agent rules

```text id="e6f4me"
Array/map unnest changes row cardinality.
Struct unnest changes column shape.
Always alias unnested outputs.
Pre-filter and project before unnest when possible.
Estimate cardinality before unnesting high-cardinality arrays.
Use LIMIT in exploratory unnest queries.
```

---

## 13.12 Struct coercion and field mapping

### Name-based mapping

DataFusion uses name-based field mapping when coercing struct types across operations; when combining structs from different sources, fields are matched by name rather than by position. This applies to array literal construction with struct elements, arrays constructed from struct columns, `UNION`/`UNION ALL` with structs, and other documented coercion paths. ([Apache DataFusion][7])

### Field reordering example

```sql id="k1w10b"
SELECT [{a: 1, b: 2}, {b: 3, a: 4}];
```

Documented result intent:

```text id="u01971"
[{"a": 1, "b": 2}, {"a": 4, "b": 3}]
```

### Union example

```sql id="mvdbkn"
SELECT {a: 1, b: 2} AS s
UNION ALL
SELECT {b: 3, a: 4} AS s;
```

Documented result intent:

```text id="wcxbr5"
field names matched across branches;
second row becomes {a: 4, b: 3}
```

### Agent rules

```text id="bopkn6"
Struct field names are semantic.
Do not rely on field position for struct coercion.
Use consistent field names across UNION branches and array literals.
Use explicit aliases inside struct(...) to enforce names.
When a field can be NULL-only in one branch, cast or construct a typed NULL.
```

---

## 13.13 Nested Parquet / Arrow reading

### Parquet external table

```sql id="7xpi2z"
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE events
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://bucket/events/';
```

DataFusion’s feature page lists Parquet primitive and nested type support; the CLI data-source docs state Parquet schema information is derived automatically, directory paths must end in `/`, all files inside a Parquet directory must be valid Parquet with compatible schemas, and wildcards are not supported—use directory roots instead. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

### Query nested Parquet fields

```sql id="d5hl7n"
SELECT
  payload['user']['id'] AS user_id,
  payload['geo']['country'] AS country,
  tags[1] AS first_tag
FROM events
WHERE payload['event_type'] = 'click';
```

### Hive partition + nested fields

```sql id="1zuxqr"
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE events
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://bucket/events/';

SELECT
  event_date,
  payload['user']['id'] AS user_id
FROM events
WHERE event_date = DATE '2026-05-22';
```

If a directory uses Hive-compliant partition paths, DataFusion CLI docs say partition columns are automatically parsed and incorporated into the schema and data, enabling filters on those columns. ([Apache DataFusion][8])

### Agent rules

```text id="v78u40"
Prefer Parquet/Arrow for nested data.
Use directory roots, not wildcards.
Ensure files in a directory have compatible schemas.
Use bracket/get_field access for nested leaves.
Use arrow_typeof / DESCRIBE for schema verification.
Partition by top-level low-cardinality fields; keep nested payload fields for event detail.
```

---

## 13.14 Nested Parquet / Arrow writing

### SQL export

```sql id="7j7d1b"
COPY (
  SELECT
    user_id,
    struct(region AS region, country AS country) AS geo,
    make_array('vip', 'paid') AS tags,
    named_struct('score', score, 'rank', rank) AS metrics
  FROM users
)
TO 's3://bucket/curated/users/'
STORED AS PARQUET;
```

### DataFrame Parquet write

```rust id="irfgva"
use datafusion::dataframe::DataFrameWriteOptions;
use datafusion::prelude::*;

ctx.sql(
    "SELECT
       user_id,
       struct(region AS region, country AS country) AS geo,
       make_array('vip', 'paid') AS tags
     FROM users"
)
.await?
.write_parquet(
    "out/users_nested.parquet",
    DataFrameWriteOptions::new(),
    None,
)
.await?;
```

DataFusion’s feature page lists write support for nested `ARRAY`/`LIST` and `STRUCT`, and its DataFrame API exposes eager Parquet writing with `write_parquet` behind the Parquet feature. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

### Agent rules

```text id="s1czkb"
Use Parquet for durable nested analytic datasets.
Use explicit struct field aliases before writing.
Avoid schema drift across output partitions/files.
Test downstream reader compatibility for maps, lists, and deep structs.
For partitioned writes, keep partition columns simple top-level scalars.
```

---

## 13.15 Nested field introspection

### `arrow_typeof`

```sql id="y1b5fv"
SELECT
  arrow_typeof(payload) AS payload_type,
  arrow_typeof(payload['user']) AS user_type,
  arrow_typeof(payload['user']['id']) AS user_id_type,
  arrow_typeof(tags) AS tags_type,
  arrow_typeof(tags[1]) AS tag_type
FROM events
LIMIT 1;
```

`arrow_typeof` returns the underlying Arrow data type name of an expression. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### `arrow_field`

```sql id="zi7rgc"
SELECT
  arrow_field(payload) AS payload_field,
  arrow_field(payload['user']) AS user_field,
  arrow_field(payload['user'])['data_type'] AS user_arrow_type
FROM events
LIMIT 1;
```

`arrow_field` returns a struct containing Arrow field information, including name, data type, nullability, and metadata. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### `arrow_metadata`

```sql id="k63rhv"
SELECT
  arrow_metadata(payload) AS payload_metadata
FROM events
LIMIT 1;
```

Agent rules:

```text id="y1gijc"
Use arrow_typeof to snapshot nested output types.
Use arrow_field to inspect names/nullability/metadata.
Use DESCRIBE for table-level schema, arrow_* functions for expression-level nested types.
```

---

## 13.16 Rust DataFrame / Expr access patterns

### SQL-expression route

```rust id="6pry7l"
let df = ctx.sql(
    "SELECT payload['user']['id'] AS user_id, tags[1] AS first_tag FROM events"
).await?;
```

### DataFrame expression-string route

```rust id="a9y8fr"
let df = ctx.table("events").await?
    .select_exprs(&[
        "payload['user']['id'] AS user_id",
        "tags[1] AS first_tag",
    ])?;
```

`select_exprs` parses SQL expression strings and is useful when DataFusion’s SQL nested syntax is desired inside a DataFrame pipeline; for untrusted inputs, validate/schema-check or construct expressions programmatically. DataFrame methods accept logical expressions, and the expression API supports fluent `Expr` construction for programmatic plans. ([Apache DataFusion][9])

### Python API note for `get_field` semantics

The Python API documentation states `get_field(expr, name)` extracts a field from a struct or map by name; when the field name is static, bracket syntax `expr["field"]` is a convenient shorthand, and `get_field` is useful for dynamic expressions. This matches the SQL `get_field` semantics documented in the scalar-function reference. ([Apache DataFusion][10])

Agent rules:

```text id="9cjvae"
For Rust codegen:
  - use SQL/select_exprs for exact nested SQL syntax when acceptable
  - use function helpers when available in pinned Rust API
  - validate all dynamic field names against schema or allowed keys
```

---

## 13.17 Nested-data performance considerations

### Projection and filter placement

```sql id="qdvi4b"
SELECT
  payload['user']['id'] AS user_id
FROM events
WHERE payload['event_type'] = 'click';
```

Nested field access is represented by `get_field`; DataFusion’s expression placement documentation identifies `get_field` as a cheap expression that can be pushed toward leaf nodes, which helps reduce data early at low compute cost. ([Docs.rs][11])

### Parquet nested pruning

DataFusion’s feature matrix lists Parquet support for nested types, row group/data page pruning, bloom-filter pruning, and predicate pushdown support details; practical pruning of nested leaves depends on file statistics, schema, query shape, and DataFusion version. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

Agent performance rules:

```text id="41fcsb"
Project only needed nested leaves.
Filter on nested leaves as early as possible.
Prefer Parquet with useful statistics for large nested datasets.
Avoid SELECT payload when only payload['a']['b'] is needed.
Avoid unnest before filtering if a predicate can be applied pre-unnest.
Benchmark nested filters under pinned DataFusion version.
```

---

## 13.18 Nested-data schema design

### Struct vs map vs array

| Shape               | Use                                                 | Avoid when                         |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `STRUCT`            | known fields, stable schema, frequent field filters | keys are dynamic/unbounded         |
| `MAP`               | dynamic key-value attributes, sparse metadata       | keys become hot predicates         |
| `LIST<T>`           | repeated homogeneous values                         | element types vary widely          |
| `LIST<STRUCT<...>>` | repeated records/events per row                     | expected to explode frequently     |
| `STRUCT<LIST<...>>` | object with repeated fields                         | list semantics belong at top level |
| JSON string         | raw archival, rare queries, unknown schema          | fields queried often               |

Agent schema rules:

```text id="7mcx6g"
Hot filters should be typed fields, not JSON text.
Fixed keys -> STRUCT.
Dynamic keys -> MAP.
Repeated values -> LIST.
Repeated records -> LIST<STRUCT>.
Embeddings -> fixed-size list if length is invariant; normal list if length can vary.
```

---

## 13.19 Generated SQL patterns

### Struct projection normalization

```sql id="eqy2ui"
SELECT
  event_id,
  payload['user']['id'] AS user_id,
  payload['user']['email'] AS user_email,
  payload['geo']['country'] AS country
FROM events;
```

### Reconstruct nested output

```sql id="sx4kwe"
SELECT
  event_id,
  named_struct(
    'id', payload['user']['id'],
    'email', payload['user']['email']
  ) AS user,
  named_struct(
    'country', payload['geo']['country'],
    'city', payload['geo']['city']
  ) AS geo
FROM events;
```

### Array filtering

```sql id="82zsgp"
SELECT
  user_id,
  tags
FROM users
WHERE array_contains(tags, 'vip');
```

### Array explode

```sql id="394pfc"
SELECT
  user_id,
  unnest(tags) AS tag
FROM users
WHERE array_length(tags) > 0;
```

### Map lookup

```sql id="ajecjm"
SELECT
  event_id,
  element_at(attrs, 'source') AS source
FROM events;
```

---

## 13.20 Null semantics and missing fields

Nested data can have null at multiple levels:

```text id="j35fg1"
struct_col is NULL
struct_col['field'] is NULL
struct_col['field'] does not exist
list_col is NULL
list_col is empty []
list_col[1] is NULL
map_col is NULL
map key missing
map key exists with NULL value
```

Agent handling rules:

```sql id="36asif"
SELECT
  coalesce(payload['user']['id'], 'unknown') AS user_id_safe,
  array_length(tags) AS tag_count,
  tags IS NULL AS tags_is_null,
  array_empty(tags) AS tags_is_empty
FROM events;
```

```text id="al2nvv"
Distinguish NULL list from empty list.
Distinguish missing map key from key with NULL value only if function semantics expose it and tests confirm.
Use coalesce for defaulting extracted fields.
Use arrow_field/arrow_typeof to verify expression schema, not to infer business null semantics.
```

---

## 13.21 Version and compatibility notes

Nested support is a fast-evolving part of DataFusion. The official feature page advertises nested read/write, field access, array/struct functions, and Postgres JSON operators; the scalar-function docs document `get_field`, many array/list/map/struct functions, and `unnest`; the struct-coercion guide documents name-based mapping. Use pinned crate/docs plus golden tests for any product-facing nested behavior. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

Test matrix:

```text id="v16dfk"
[ ] array literal type inference
[ ] list element access index behavior
[ ] struct field access
[ ] nested struct field access
[ ] map construction and lookup
[ ] missing field/key behavior
[ ] null struct/list/map behavior
[ ] unnest(array) row multiplication
[ ] unnest(struct) column expansion
[ ] struct union field-name mapping
[ ] read nested Parquet
[ ] write nested Parquet
[ ] arrow_typeof snapshots for nested expressions
[ ] Postgres -> / ->> operator output types
```

---

## 13.22 Deployment advisory

```text id="d8lnso"
Data lake:
  use Parquet for nested durable datasets
  maintain compatible schemas across files
  avoid wildcard locations; use directory roots
  expose top-level partition columns for pruning

SQL service:
  allow nested field access but limit unnest/cardinality explosion
  validate dynamic field names
  restrict Postgres JSON operators if semantics are not part of contract
  add query row/byte limits

ETL:
  parse raw JSON into typed STRUCT/LIST/MAP early if fields are queried repeatedly
  cast/normalize nested field types explicitly
  reconstruct nested output with named_struct / struct / map functions

ML/vector:
  store embeddings as numeric arrays/fixed-size lists where possible
  validate length before dot_product/cosine_distance
  avoid unnesting embeddings for similarity scoring
```

---

## 13.23 Anti-pattern inventory

* Storing hot query fields as opaque JSON strings.
* Using `SELECT payload` when only `payload['a']['b']` is needed.
* Unnesting arrays before applying filters that could be pushed earlier.
* Treating `[]` and `NULL` list as equivalent.
* Relying on struct field position instead of field name.
* Using MAP for stable, frequently-filtered fields.
* Generating Postgres `->` / `->>` operators without pinned-version type tests.
* Assuming wildcard Parquet locations work; DataFusion docs recommend directory roots instead. ([Apache DataFusion][8])
* Writing nested datasets with inconsistent schemas across files.
* Using high-cardinality nested fields as partition directories.
* Forgetting that `unnest(struct)` expands columns while `unnest(array)` expands rows.
* Building `StructArray` with mismatched child lengths.
* Building nested arrays with direct low-level buffers before mastering builders.
* Assuming nested Parquet pruning is identical across DataFusion versions.

---

## 13.24 Agent checklist

```text id="mnapwe"
[ ] Choose shape: STRUCT vs MAP vs LIST vs LIST<STRUCT>.
[ ] Use bracket access: col['field'], col[1].
[ ] Use get_field for normalized/dynamic field access.
[ ] Use named_struct / struct / row for struct construction.
[ ] Use map / make_map for dynamic key-value data.
[ ] Use array_* / list_* functions for array operations.
[ ] Use unnest only when row or column expansion is intended.
[ ] Use arrow_typeof / arrow_field for nested schema audits.
[ ] Prefer Parquet/Arrow for nested read/write.
[ ] Use directory roots and compatible schemas for nested Parquet.
[ ] Test struct coercion field-name behavior across UNION/arrays.
[ ] Validate NULL vs empty vs missing semantics.
[ ] Alias extracted fields and constructed structs.
[ ] Add LIMIT/cardinality controls around unnest.
[ ] Pin DataFusion version before relying on -> / ->> semantics.
```

# DataFusion Advanced — 14) Data sources and file formats

Style target follows the uploaded advanced-reference pattern. 

## 14.0 Source model: three entry surfaces

```text id="l5rmfl"
DataFrame direct read:
  ctx.read_csv / read_parquet / read_json / read_avro / read_arrow
    → anonymous DataFrame

Catalog registration:
  ctx.register_csv / register_parquet / register_json / register_avro / register_arrow
  CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE ...
    → named TableProvider
    → SQL / ctx.table access

Direct path SQL:
  SELECT * FROM 'path-or-url'
    → DynamicFileCatalog / URL table path
    → security-sensitive in embedded apps
```

DataFusion’s built-in table provider layer includes `ListingTable`, which reads one or more Parquet, JSON, CSV, or Avro files from local or remote directories, supports Hive-style partitioning, optional compression, remote object stores, metadata caching, and related file-listing behavior. DataFusion also includes `MemTable` for in-memory `RecordBatch`es and `StreamingTable` for potentially unbounded inputs. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 14.1 Built-in format matrix

| Format          | Direct DataFrame API              | Register API           | SQL DDL `STORED AS`       | Feature notes             | Best use                                              |
| --------------- | --------------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| CSV             | `ctx.read_csv`                    | `ctx.register_csv`     | `CSV`                     | default/common            | human-readable ingestion, interchange, small data     |
| Parquet         | `ctx.read_parquet`                | `ctx.register_parquet` | `PARQUET`                 | `parquet` feature         | analytics lake, typed/nested/compressed columnar data |
| JSON            | `ctx.read_json`                   | `ctx.register_json`    | `JSON`                    | default/common            | semi-structured interchange, logs                     |
| Avro            | `ctx.read_avro`                   | `ctx.register_avro`    | `AVRO`                    | `avro` feature            | Avro ecosystems, schema-bearing row data              |
| Arrow IPC       | `ctx.read_arrow`                  | `ctx.register_arrow`   | `ARROW`                   | default/common            | Arrow-native interchange, fast local columnar data    |
| in-memory Arrow | `ctx.read_batch` / `read_batches` | `ctx.register_batch`   | not file DDL              | no file path              | tests, adapters, generated data                       |
| custom source   | `ctx.read_table`                  | `ctx.register_table`   | custom/provider dependent | implement `TableProvider` | databases, APIs, proprietary storage                  |

`CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE` currently accepts file types `CSV`, `ARROW`, `PARQUET`, `AVRO`, and `JSON`, and `LOCATION` may point to a local path or object-store path containing a file or a directory of partitioned files. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

## 14.2 DataFrame direct-read APIs

### CSV

```rust id="8xk84e"
use datafusion::prelude::*;

let ctx = SessionContext::new();

let df = ctx
    .read_csv("data/events.csv", CsvReadOptions::new())
    .await?;
```

### Multiple CSV files as one DataFrame

```rust id="4q1tzf"
let df = ctx
    .read_csv(
        vec![
            "data/events-part-000.csv",
            "data/events-part-001.csv",
        ],
        CsvReadOptions::new(),
    )
    .await?;
```

`read_csv` creates a DataFrame for a CSV data source; the current docs show both single-file and multi-file calls, and note that `read_table` with `ListingTable` gives more control for complex file layouts. ([Docs.rs][3])

### Parquet

```rust id="oglikr"
let df = ctx
    .read_parquet("data/facts/", ParquetReadOptions::default())
    .await?;
```

`read_parquet` creates a DataFrame for a Parquet source and is feature-gated on `parquet`; by default, statistics are collected when reading Parquet files, which can slow DataFrame creation while accelerating later filtered queries. ([Docs.rs][3])

### JSON

```rust id="xqlk52"
let df = ctx
    .read_json("data/events.json", JsonReadOptions::default())
    .await?;
```

`read_json` creates a DataFrame for a JSON data source; for more control, the docs point to `read_table` with `ListingTable`. ([Docs.rs][3])

### Avro

```rust id="f3pwkq"
let df = ctx
    .read_avro("data/events.avro", AvroReadOptions::default())
    .await?;
```

`read_avro` and `register_avro` are available only with the `avro` crate feature and create/register DataFrames/tables for Avro data sources. ([Docs.rs][3])

### Arrow IPC

```rust id="9xim94"
let df = ctx
    .read_arrow("data/events.arrow", ArrowReadOptions::default())
    .await?;
```

`read_arrow` creates a DataFrame for an Arrow data source, and `register_arrow` registers an Arrow file as a SQL table. ([Docs.rs][3])

---

## 14.3 Registration APIs: named tables for SQL

```rust id="ldsqg0"
ctx.register_csv("events_csv", "data/events.csv", CsvReadOptions::new()).await?;
ctx.register_parquet("facts", "data/facts/", ParquetReadOptions::default()).await?;
ctx.register_json("events_json", "data/events.json", JsonReadOptions::default()).await?;
ctx.register_avro("events_avro", "data/events.avro", AvroReadOptions::default()).await?;
ctx.register_arrow("events_arrow", "data/events.arrow", ArrowReadOptions::default()).await?;

let df = ctx.sql("SELECT count(*) FROM facts").await?;
```

`register_csv`, `register_json`, `register_parquet`, `register_avro`, and `register_arrow` make files available as SQL tables; `register_parquet` and `register_avro` are feature-gated on `parquet` and `avro` respectively. ([Docs.rs][3])

Agent rule:

```text id="xxwzj5"
read_*       = anonymous DataFrame source
register_*   = named table for SQL / ctx.table
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE = SQL catalog registration
read_table/register_table = custom or complex provider path
```

---

## 14.4 `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE`: SQL registration path

### Generic syntax

```sql id="o8nfsq"
CREATE [UNBOUNDED] EXTERNAL TABLE
[ IF NOT EXISTS ]
<table_name> [ (<column_definition>) ]
STORED AS <file_type>
[ PARTITIONED BY (<column_list>) ]
[ WITH ORDER (<ordered_column_list>) ]
[ OPTIONS (<key_value_list>) ]
LOCATION <literal>;
```

DataFusion documents `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE` as registering a local or remote location as a named queryable table; supported file types are `CSV`, `ARROW`, `PARQUET`, `AVRO`, and `JSON`. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

### Parquet external table

```sql id="5k1eu0"
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE taxi
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION '/mnt/nyctaxi/tripdata.parquet';
```

For Parquet, schema information is derived automatically, and DataFusion may read file metadata/statistics during table creation unless `datafusion.execution.collect_statistics` is disabled. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

### CSV external table with inferred schema

```sql id="1jehw9"
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE events
STORED AS CSV
LOCATION '/data/events.csv'
OPTIONS ('has_header' 'true');
```

CSV schemas are inferred by scanning a subset of the file unless an explicit schema is supplied. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

### CSV external table with explicit schema

```sql id="k5gtet"
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE events (
  event_id VARCHAR NOT NULL,
  user_id VARCHAR,
  amount DOUBLE,
  event_date DATE
)
STORED AS CSV
LOCATION '/data/events.csv'
OPTIONS ('has_header' 'true');
```

DataFusion supports manual schema specification in `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE`; use it for production CSV/JSON contracts instead of relying on inference. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

## 14.5 Direct path querying

### CLI / SQL examples

```sql id="xw8cm0"
SELECT * FROM 'data.csv';

SELECT count(*)
FROM 'https://datasets.example.org/hits_1.parquet';

SELECT count(*)
FROM 's3://bucket/path/to/parquet_directory/';
```

The CLI docs show direct querying by enclosing a file, directory, or remote location in single quotes; they explicitly show a CSV file query, an HTTP(S) Parquet query, and S3/GCS-style remote paths. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

### Embedded Rust: explicit enablement

```rust id="4kcfu2"
use datafusion::prelude::*;

let ctx = SessionContext::new()
    .enable_url_table();

let batches = ctx
    .sql(
        "SELECT a, MIN(b)
         FROM 'tests/data/example.csv' AS example
         GROUP BY a
         LIMIT 100",
    )
    .await?
    .collect()
    .await?;
```

`enable_url_table()` permits SQL access to local files such as `SELECT * FROM 'my_file.parquet'`; the docs call this security-sensitive and say it should only be enabled for systems that intentionally permit SQL to access the filesystem directly. ([Docs.rs][3])

Agent rule:

```text id="yx2oil"
Public / multi-tenant SQL:
  avoid enable_url_table()
  register allowed tables explicitly
  restrict paths through catalog/object-store policy

Local CLI / trusted notebook:
  direct quoted paths are convenient
```

---

## 14.6 Local files, directories, and multiple files

### Single file

```sql id="hwuv3g"
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE hits
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 'hits.parquet';
```

### Directory

```sql id="ohha1n"
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE taxi
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION '/mnt/nyctaxi/';
```

The CLI docs state that directory paths for Parquet should end in `/`; otherwise DataFusion treats the path as a file rather than a directory. All files inside the directory must be valid Parquet files with compatible schemas. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

### Multiple files with Rust API

```rust id="1wvb1w"
let df = ctx
    .read_csv(
        vec![
            "data/part-000.csv",
            "data/part-001.csv",
            "data/part-002.csv",
        ],
        CsvReadOptions::new(),
    )
    .await?;
```

`DataFilePaths` lets methods such as `read_csv` and `read_avro` accept either a single file or multiple files. ([Docs.rs][5])

---

## 14.7 Wildcards: avoid / unsupported in CLI docs

```sql id="n91uyn"
-- Do not generate:
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 'gs://bucket/*.parquet';
```

```sql id="8v9kfi"
-- Preferred:
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 'gs://bucket/my_table/';
```

DataFusion CLI docs state that wildcards are not supported and recommend specifying a directory path directly so DataFusion reads all compatible files under that directory; this design avoids storage-backend-specific wildcard behavior across local filesystems, S3, GCS, and other stores. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

---

## 14.8 Hive-style partitions

### Layout

```text id="jxh7es"
s3://bucket/my_table/a=1/b=100/file1.parquet
s3://bucket/my_table/a=2/b=200/file2.parquet
```

### SQL

```sql id="qqckct"
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE my_table
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://bucket/my_table/';

SELECT count(*)
FROM my_table
WHERE b = 200;
```

DataFusion automatically parses Hive-compliant partition directories and incorporates partition columns/values into table schema/data when a directory path has Hive-style structure. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

### Explicit partition declaration

```sql id="2aqjbe"
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE taxi
STORED AS PARQUET
PARTITIONED BY (year, month)
LOCATION '/mnt/nyctaxi';
```

DataFusion’s DDL docs show `PARTITIONED BY` for Hive-style partition pruning. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Agent rules:

```text id="z9uewi"
Partition path format: col=value/col=value/file
Use low/moderate-cardinality partition keys.
Prefer top-level scalar partition columns.
Do not use high-cardinality UUID/session IDs as partition directories.
Directory schema must be compatible across files.
```

---

## 14.9 Schema inference vs explicit schemas

| Format          | Inference behavior                                          | Production stance                        |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Parquet         | schema from file metadata; no schema needed in DDL          | usually infer; validate with `DESCRIBE`  |
| Arrow           | schema stored in Arrow IPC                                  | infer/verify                             |
| Avro            | schema-bearing format                                       | infer/verify; feature-gated              |
| CSV             | inferred by scanning subset unless explicit schema supplied | explicit schema strongly preferred       |
| JSON            | schema inferred or option-driven depending path/options     | explicit schema preferred where possible |
| directories     | inferred/merged from compatible files                       | require compatibility tests              |
| Hive partitions | partition columns parsed from paths                         | validate partition type/string behavior  |

For CSV, DataFusion’s docs say schema is inferred from a subset of the file; CSV option `SCHEMA_INFER_MAX_REC` controls how many records are scanned, and if set to `0`, inference is disabled and fields are inferred as `Utf8`. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Schema audit:

```sql id="54z7sy"
DESCRIBE events;

SELECT
  arrow_typeof(event_id) AS event_id_type,
  arrow_typeof(event_date) AS event_date_type
FROM events
LIMIT 1;
```

---

## 14.10 CSV format

### SQL registration

```sql id="fnmg1a"
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE t (
  col1 VARCHAR,
  col2 INT,
  col3 BOOLEAN
)
STORED AS CSV
LOCATION '/tmp/foo/'
OPTIONS (
  'DELIMITER' '|',
  'HAS_HEADER' 'true',
  'NEWLINES_IN_VALUES' 'true',
  'NULL_VALUE' ''
);
```

DataFusion CSV options include compression, header handling, delimiter, quote, terminator, escape, double-quote behavior, newlines in values, date/time/timestamp formats, null value, null regex, schema-inference record count, and comment character. Unsupported CSV options raise errors. ([Apache DataFusion][6])

### Rust direct read

```rust id="p9rp63"
let df = ctx
    .read_csv("data/events.csv", CsvReadOptions::new().has_header(true))
    .await?;
```

### Compressed CSV

```sql id="mrrnut"
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test
STORED AS CSV
COMPRESSION TYPE GZIP
LOCATION '/path/to/aggregate_simple.csv.gz'
OPTIONS ('has_header' 'true');
```

DataFusion DDL docs show compressed CSV registration using `COMPRESSION TYPE GZIP`. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Agent rules:

```text id="71aawl"
CSV = interoperability, not optimal analytics storage.
Always set HAS_HEADER deliberately.
Always set delimiter/null behavior deliberately for production.
Use explicit schema for production.
Use Parquet after ingestion/cleaning for repeated analytics.
```

## 14.11 Parquet format

### SQL registration

```sql id="s5jvbf"
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE facts
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://bucket/facts/';
```

### Rust direct read

```rust id="nraxo6"
let df = ctx
    .read_parquet("s3://bucket/facts/", ParquetReadOptions::default())
    .await?;
```

### Parquet read/write option examples

```sql id="2nuf26"
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE facts
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://bucket/facts/'
OPTIONS (
  'pruning' 'true',
  'enable_page_index' 'true',
  'pushdown_filters' 'false',
  'skip_metadata' 'true',
  'schema_force_view_types' 'true'
);
```

Parquet options include compression, encoding, dictionary encoding, statistics, bloom-filter settings, row-group size, page index, row-group pruning, metadata-size hint, pushdown filters, filter reordering, metadata skipping, forcing view types, binary-as-string behavior, data page sizing, dictionary page sizing, write batch size, writer version, and Arrow metadata controls. ([Apache DataFusion][6])

Agent rules:

```text id="q6pbc6"
Parquet = default production analytics format.
Use directory roots for lake tables.
Keep schemas compatible across files.
Use statistics/pruning/page-index options deliberately.
Disable collect_statistics during registration if startup latency matters.
Use explicit object-store credentials outside SQL when possible.
```

## 14.12 JSON format

### SQL registration

```sql id="gmro0i"
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE t (
  a INT,
  payload VARCHAR

STORED AS JSON
LOCATION '/tmp/foo/'
OPTIONS ('COMPRESSION' 'gzip');
```

JSON options include `COMPRESSION`, with supported values `GZIP`, `BZIP2`, `XZ`, `ZSTD`, and `UNCOMPRESSED`; unsupported JSON options raise errors. ([Apache DataFusion][6])

```rust id="ukq4mq"
    .await?;
```

```text id="n8xr90"
JSON = semi-structured exchange/log format.
```

### SQL registration

```sql id="v1yr60"
STORED AS ARROW
```

```text id="1rclb7"
Arrow IPC = fast columnar interchange.
```

## 14.15 `ListingTable`: advanced file source abstraction

```rust id="12rm03"
// High-level registration API:
ctx.register_listing_table(
    "events",
    "s3://bucket/events/",
    listing_options,
    provided_schema,
    sql_definition,
).await?;
```

`register_listing_table` registers a `ListingTable` that assembles multiple files from locations in an `ObjectStore` into one table; it is async because resolving schema may require file access. ([Docs.rs][3])

Use `ListingTable` / `register_listing_table` when:

```text id="zipd1c"
multiple directories
complex file extension handling
custom ListingOptions
provided_schema needed
custom object-store table layout
large lake datasets
schema resolution should be controlled
```

---

## 14.16 Object stores and remote files

```sql id="it3so3"
SELECT count(*)
FROM 'https://datasets.example.org/hits.parquet';

SELECT count(*)
FROM 's3://my-data-bucket/path/to/table/';

SELECT count(*)
FROM 'gs://bucket/my_table/';
```

DataFusion direct path examples include HTTP(S), S3, and GCS; for S3/GCS, the docs specify using protocol prefixes such as `s3://` or `gs://` and providing credentials through environment variables or the relevant object-store configuration path. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

Rust object-store registration pattern:

```rust id="rl4un8"
use std::sync::Arc;
use datafusion::prelude::*;
use datafusion::object_store::local::LocalFileSystem;
use url::Url;

let ctx = SessionContext::new();

ctx.register_object_store(
    &Url::parse("file:///")?,
    Arc::new(LocalFileSystem::new()),
);
```

`SessionContext::register_object_store` registers an object store for a URL prefix. ([Docs.rs][3])

Agent rules:

```text id="d1yv9x"
Do not inline long-lived credentials in SQL.
Use environment / object-store registry / secret manager.
Separate object-store registries by tenant when credentials differ.
Prefer registered tables over direct path SQL in services.
```

---

## 14.17 Direct path vs registered table vs DataFrame read

| Mode                     | Syntax                          | Pros                          | Risks                            |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| direct quoted path       | `SELECT * FROM 'file.parquet'`  | fastest ad hoc CLI            | filesystem/object-store exposure |
| `ctx.enable_url_table()` | embedded direct path SQL        | convenient trusted local apps | security-sensitive               |
| `ctx.read_*`             | Rust DataFrame path             | typed app control             | anonymous source                 |
| `ctx.register_*`         | named table in `SessionContext` | SQL/table reuse               | catalog lifecycle                |
| `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE`  | SQL registration                | user-visible DDL              | DDL governance/path policy       |
| `ListingTable`           | provider-level control          | complex datasets              | more code/config                 |

`enable_url_table` is explicitly security-sensitive because it permits SQL to access arbitrary local files like `SELECT * FROM 'my_file.parquet'`. ([Docs.rs][3])

---

## 14.18 Format options precedence

```text id="5dqis0"
highest:
  CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE syntax / table-specific options
  COPY option tuples
  session-level config defaults
lowest
```

DataFusion’s format-options docs state that format options can be specified through `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE`, `COPY` option tuples, and session-level config defaults, in decreasing precedence. They also show that table-specific CSV options such as delimiter/header are respected by later `INSERT INTO`. ([Apache DataFusion][6])

Example:

```sql id="drkqjg"
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE my_table(a BIGINT, b BIGINT)
STORED AS CSV
LOCATION '/tmp/my_csv_table/'
OPTIONS (
  NULL_VALUE 'NAN',
  'has_header' 'true',
  'format.delimiter' ';'
);
```

---

## 14.19 Production source-selection policy

| Source shape                   | Recommended format/source              |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------- |
| repeated analytic scans        | Parquet directory                      |
| nested typed data              | Parquet / Arrow                        |
| human-provided import          | CSV with explicit schema               |
| log ingestion                  | JSON → normalize → Parquet             |
| schema-bearing row interchange | Avro                                   |
| Arrow-native pipeline          | Arrow IPC / RecordBatch                |
| service/runtime custom backend | custom `TableProvider`                 |
| one-off CLI query              | quoted direct path                     |
| public SQL endpoint            | registered tables only; no direct path |

## 14.21 Performance advisory by format

```text id="y8q5bx"
CSV:
  slowest parse-heavy path
  no native column pruning in file encoding
  best for interchange/import

JSON:
  flexible but parse-heavy
  best for logs/semi-structured interchange
  normalize hot fields to typed columns

Avro:
  schema-bearing row format
  useful for Avro ecosystems
  not primary analytics scan target

Arrow IPC:
  fast columnar interchange

Parquet:
```

Parquet options include row-group pruning, page-index usage, filter pushdown, metadata-size hints, compression, statistics, and schema-view-type controls; larger row groups can improve compression and scan efficiency but require more memory. ([Apache DataFusion][6])

## 14.22 Rust end-to-end ingestion examples

### CSV → DataFrame → Parquet

```rust id="pz52f9"
use datafusion::dataframe::DataFrameWriteOptions;
use datafusion::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    ctx.read_csv("data/raw/events.csv", CsvReadOptions::new().has_header(true))
        .await?
        .filter(col("event_id").is_not_null())?

            "data/curated/events/",
            DataFrameWriteOptions::new(),

    Ok(())
}
```

### Parquet directory → SQL table

```rust id="zrrrqn"

    "events",

let batches = ctx
    .sql(
        "SELECT event_date, count(*) AS n
         FROM events

    .await?;
```

## 14.23 Security and governance

```text id="1lm5gc"
Public service:
  disable direct path SQL
  do not call enable_url_table()
  use registered tables/catalogs
  apply table/path allowlists
  isolate object stores by tenant
  deny CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE unless governed
  disable DDL with SQLOptions when read-only

Internal CLI:
  direct path SQL is acceptable
  still avoid secrets in SQL logs

ETL jobs:
  prefer Rust read_* / write_* APIs
  register only stable named sources
  validate schemas before writing curated outputs
```

`enable_url_table()` explicitly permits SQL access to arbitrary local files and is documented as security-sensitive. ([Docs.rs][3])

---

## 14.24 Anti-pattern inventory

* Enabling direct quoted path SQL in a public SQL endpoint.
* Using wildcard paths like `s3://bucket/*.parquet`.
* Registering a directory path without a trailing `/` when a directory is intended.
* Mixing incompatible schemas inside one directory table.
* Relying on CSV schema inference for production.
* Treating JSON as a long-term analytics format when hot fields should be typed.
* Reading many tiny files without compaction or listing-cache strategy.
* Inlining cloud credentials in `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE OPTIONS`.
* Assuming Parquet registration has zero metadata cost.
* Disabling Parquet pruning/statistics without measuring.
* Using high-cardinality Hive partitions.
* Forgetting Avro feature flag in minimized builds.
* Assuming direct path SQL and registered-table SQL have identical governance.
* Using `WITH ORDER` metadata without verifying file order.
* Treating `DROP TABLE` as deleting external files.

---

```text id="6k5npr"
[ ] Choose source surface: read_* / register_* / CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE / direct path / ListingTable.
[ ] Choose format: CSV / Parquet / JSON / Avro / Arrow / custom provider.
[ ] Prefer Parquet for production analytics.
[ ] Use explicit schemas for CSV/JSON production ingestion.
[ ] Verify Parquet schema with DESCRIBE / arrow_typeof.
[ ] Use directory roots, not wildcards.
[ ] Ensure directory paths end with `/` when required.
[ ] Ensure all files in a directory have compatible schemas.
[ ] Use Hive partitioning only for bounded-cardinality columns.
[ ] Configure CSV/JSON compression/header/delimiter/null behavior explicitly.
[ ] Tune Parquet options only under pinned-version benchmarks.
[ ] Disable collect_statistics if registration latency matters more than later filter speed.
[ ] Enable `avro` feature before using Avro APIs.
[ ] Use datafusion::arrow imports for Arrow data.
[ ] Do not enable URL table/direct path access in untrusted SQL contexts.
[ ] Register object stores and credentials outside SQL when possible.
```
