## 14.26 Typed per-file extensions: `PartitionedFile.extensions` (DataFusion 54)

DataFusion 54 replaced the single type-erased `Option<Arc<dyn Any>>` extension slot on `PartitionedFile` with a **typed extension map**:

```rust
// datafusion_datasource (re-exported through datafusion::datasource)
pub type FileExtensions = datafusion_common::extensions::Extensions;

pub struct PartitionedFile {
    pub object_meta: ObjectMeta,
    pub partition_values: Vec<ScalarValue>,
    pub range: Option<FileRange>,
    pub statistics: Option<Arc<Statistics>>,
    pub ordering: Option<LexOrdering>,
    pub extensions: FileExtensions,        // typed map, keyed by Rust type
    pub metadata_size_hint: Option<usize>,
    pub table_reference: Option<TableReference>,
}
```

`Extensions` (`datafusion_common::extensions::Extensions`) is a map keyed by concrete Rust `TypeId`: `insert(value)` / `insert_arc(Arc<T>)` store a typed entry (returning the previous entry of that type, if any), `get::<T>()` borrows and `get_arc::<T>()` clones out an entry, `contains::<T>()` tests presence, and `merge(&other)` folds another map in. A deprecated `insert_dyn` supports the old type-erased shim. The same `Extensions` type backs `SessionConfig::extensions` and other extension fields across DataFusion.

On `PartitionedFile`, the convenience surface is:

```rust
use datafusion::datasource::listing::PartitionedFile;
use datafusion::datasource::physical_plan::parquet::ParquetAccessPlan;

#[derive(Debug)]
struct DeltaFileInfo { version: i64, dv_path: Option<String> }

let file = PartitionedFile::new("data/part-0001.parquet", 1024 * 1024)
    // multiple independent typed entries coexist without conflict:
    .with_extension(access_plan)                 // ParquetAccessPlan for row-group/page skipping
    .with_extension(DeltaFileInfo { version: 42, dv_path: None });

// readers/sources retrieve exactly the entry they own, by type:
if let Some(plan) = file.extension::<ParquetAccessPlan>() { /* prune */ }
if let Some(delta) = file.extension::<DeltaFileInfo>() { /* apply deletion vector */ }
```

Why this matters: under 53, one component's extension (for example a table format attaching Delta/semantic file info) clobbered another's (a `ParquetAccessPlan` for scan pruning) because there was a single untyped slot. Under 54, each component keys its data by its own concrete type, so a lakehouse provider and the Parquet source can both annotate the same file. The legacy `with_extensions(Arc<dyn Any + Send + Sync>)` builder is retained as a deprecated shim (it stores the value keyed by its dynamic type); migrate to `with_extension(value)` / `extension::<T>()`.

Agent rules:

```text
Key per-file metadata by a dedicated concrete type you own.
Use with_extension/extension::<T>(); do not use the deprecated with_extensions shim in new code.
Never assume you are the only extension author on a PartitionedFile.
Extensions must be Any + Send + Sync; keep them small and immutable (they clone with the file).
```

[1]: https://docs.rs/datafusion/latest/datafusion/ "datafusion - Rust"
[2]: https://datafusion.apache.org/user-guide/sql/ddl.html "DDL — Apache DataFusion  documentation"
[3]: https://docs.rs/datafusion/latest/datafusion/execution/context/struct.SessionContext.html "SessionContext in datafusion::execution::context - Rust"
[4]: https://datafusion.apache.org/user-guide/cli/datasources.html "Local Files / Directories — Apache DataFusion  documentation"
[5]: https://docs.rs/datafusion/latest/datafusion/execution/context/index.html "datafusion::execution::context - Rust"
[6]: https://datafusion.apache.org/user-guide/sql/format_options.html "Format Options — Apache DataFusion  documentation"


# DataFusion Advanced — 15) Parquet deep dive

Style target follows the uploaded advanced-reference pattern. 

## 15.0 Parquet mental model

```text
Parquet dataset
  ├─ file(s)
  │   ├─ footer metadata
  │   ├─ schema
  │   ├─ row groups
  │   │   ├─ column chunks
  │   │   │   ├─ data pages
  │   │   │   ├─ optional page index
  │   │   │   ├─ optional bloom filter
  │   │   │   └─ min/max/null-count statistics
  │   └─ optional key-value metadata
  ├─ optional Hive partition directories
  └─ DataFusion access path
      read_parquet / register_parquet / CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE
        → ListingTable / ParquetFormat
        → projection pruning
        → row group pruning
        → bloom-filter pruning
        → page-index pruning
        → optional row-level filter pushdown / late materialization
        → Arrow RecordBatch stream
```

DataFusion treats Parquet as the primary high-performance analytical file format: the crate exposes direct DataFrame reads, SQL table registration, and writer paths, while the Parquet reader/writer options surface includes pruning, page-index reading, filter pushdown, compression, row-group sizing, bloom filters, writer version, Arrow metadata, and parallel writer controls. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 15.1 Value case: why Parquet is the default analytics format

| Requirement                        | Parquet / DataFusion value                                                              |
| ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| read few columns from wide data    | projection pushdown reads only referenced column chunks                                 |
| skip irrelevant ranges             | row-group min/max/null stats enable pruning                                             |
| skip pages inside row groups       | page index enables page-level pruning                                                   |
| accelerate equality / `IN` filters | bloom filters can rule out absent values                                                |
| scan nested data                   | Parquet supports nested schemas; DataFusion supports primitive and nested Parquet types |
| reduce storage and I/O             | columnar compression + encoding                                                         |
| lake-style layout                  | directory datasets + Hive partitions                                                    |
| typed SQL over files               | `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE ... STORED AS PARQUET`                                           |
| Rust-native pipelines              | `read_parquet`, `register_parquet`, `write_parquet`                                     |

DataFusion’s Parquet pruning documentation describes a multi-step pruning pipeline: projection pruning, row-group statistics and bloom filters, page statistics, and row-level filter pushdown / late materialization, each reducing bytes read or rows decoded. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

## 15.2 Cargo and feature gating

```toml
[dependencies]
datafusion = { version = "55.0.0", features = ["parquet"] }
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "macros"] }
```

`SessionContext::read_parquet`, `register_parquet`, and `write_parquet` are available only when the `parquet` feature is enabled; the top-level crate’s normal/default build includes broad functionality, but feature-minimized builds must opt in explicitly. ([Docs.rs][1])

Agent rule:

```text
If code references ParquetReadOptions / read_parquet / register_parquet / write_parquet:
  ensure the datafusion parquet feature is enabled.
```

---

## 15.3 Rust read path: `ctx.read_parquet`

### Minimal direct DataFrame read

```rust
use datafusion::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    let df = ctx
        .read_parquet("data/facts.parquet", ParquetReadOptions::default())
        .await?;

    df.show().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```

### Directory dataset

```rust
let df = ctx
    .read_parquet("s3://bucket/lake/facts/", ParquetReadOptions::default())
    .await?;
```

`read_parquet` creates an anonymous `DataFrame` directly from a Parquet source; for more control, the Rust docs direct users toward `read_table` with `ListingTable`. By default, `read_parquet` collects Parquet statistics during DataFrame creation, which can slow initial creation but accelerate filtered queries; the docs point to `datafusion.execution.collect_statistics` for disabling that behavior. ([Docs.rs][1])

### Disable creation-time statistics collection

```rust
use datafusion::prelude::*;

let mut config = SessionConfig::new();
config.set_bool("datafusion.execution.collect_statistics", false)?;

let ctx = SessionContext::new_with_config(config);

let df = ctx
    .read_parquet("s3://bucket/lake/facts/", ParquetReadOptions::default())
    .await?;
```

The config key `datafusion.execution.collect_statistics` controls whether DataFusion collects statistics when first creating a table; it applies to the default `ListingTableProvider` and has no effect after the table is created. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

---

## 15.4 SQL table registration: `register_parquet`

```rust
use datafusion::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    ctx.register_parquet(
        "facts",
        "data/facts.parquet",
        ParquetReadOptions::default(),
    )
    .await?;

    let df = ctx
        .sql(
            "SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total_amount
             FROM facts
             WHERE event_date >= DATE '2026-01-01'
             GROUP BY customer_id",
        )
        .await?;

    df.show().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```

`register_parquet` registers a Parquet file or path as a table that can be referenced from SQL. The Rust docs distinguish it from `read_parquet`: `read_parquet` notes statistics are collected by default, while `register_parquet` notes statistics are not collected by default and points back to `read_parquet` for more detail. ([Docs.rs][1])

Agent distinction:

```text
read_parquet(...)       -> anonymous DataFrame source
register_parquet(...)   -> catalog table name for SQL / ctx.table(...)
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE   -> SQL DDL table registration
```

---

## 15.5 SQL DDL: `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE ... STORED AS PARQUET`

### Single Parquet file

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE taxi
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION '/mnt/nyctaxi/tripdata.parquet';
```

### Parquet directory

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE taxi
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION '/mnt/nyctaxi/';
```

Parquet schema information is derived automatically, and when registering a folder all files inside must be valid Parquet files with compatible schemas. Directory paths must end in `/`; otherwise DataFusion treats the path as a file. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

### S3 / object store

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE facts
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://bucket/path/to/facts/';
```

### DDL with read/write options

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE facts
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://bucket/path/to/facts/'
OPTIONS (
  'pruning' 'true',
  'enable_page_index' 'true',
  'bloom_filter_on_read' 'true',
  'metadata_size_hint' '524288',
  'schema_force_view_types' 'true'
);
```

DataFusion’s format-options system applies to `COPY`, `INSERT INTO`, and `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE`; format options can be specified through `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE`, `COPY` option tuples, and session defaults, in decreasing precedence. Unsupported Parquet options raise errors, while column-specific options for non-existing columns are ignored without error. ([Apache DataFusion][5])

---

## 15.6 Schema inference and compatibility

```text
Parquet file schema
  → Arrow schema
  → DataFusion table schema
  → plus Hive partition columns, if present
```

For partitioned datasets, DataFusion separates file schema from partition columns: the file schema is stored inside Parquet files, while Hive partition values are encoded in directory paths and appended to the full table schema. ([Docs.rs][6])

### Hive partition example

```text
/data/events/event_date=2026-05-22/region=us/file-0.parquet
/data/events/event_date=2026-05-22/region=eu/file-1.parquet
```

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE events
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION '/data/events/';

SELECT count(*)
FROM events
WHERE region = 'us';
```

DataFusion automatically parses Hive-compliant partition directories and incorporates partition columns and values into schema and data when the directory structure follows `col=value` conventions. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

Agent rules:

```text
All files under one Parquet table path must have compatible schemas.
Partition columns are not stored in files; they are derived from paths.
Use DESCRIBE and arrow_typeof audits after registration.
Avoid schema drift across partitions unless a custom schema adapter handles it.
```

---

## 15.7 Directory and path rules

### Preferred

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE facts
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 'gs://bucket/my_table/';
```

### Avoid

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE facts
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 'gs://bucket/*.parquet';
```

DataFusion CLI docs state that wildcards are not supported and recommend registering the directory root directly. This avoids backend-specific wildcard behavior across local filesystems and object stores. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

Agent rules:

```text
Use directory roots, not wildcards.
Ensure directory paths end with `/`.
Keep one logical table per compatible-schema directory.
Use Hive-style partition directories for pruning.
```

---

## 15.8 Parquet scan pruning pipeline

```text
Query:
  SELECT a FROM t WHERE b = 10

Parquet scan optimization:
  1. Projection pruning:
       read only a and b as needed
  2. Row group pruning:
       use row-group min/max/null stats
  3. Bloom filter pruning:
       use bloom filters for equality / IN predicates if present
  4. Page-index pruning:
       use page-level metadata if present
  5. Filter pushdown / late materialization:
       evaluate filters during decode to reduce rows decoded
```

DataFusion’s Parquet blog explains that page-level pruning works after row-group pruning and can skip individual pages inside row groups; it also describes filter pushdown / late materialization as row-level pruning during scanning, distinct from metadata-based row-group/page pruning. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

## 15.9 Projection pushdown

```sql
SELECT
  customer_id,
  amount
FROM facts
WHERE event_date = DATE '2026-05-22';
```

Only referenced columns need to be read from Parquet: projected output columns plus columns required by filters, joins, sorts, and aggregates. DataFusion’s `TableProvider` API explicitly provides projection information to scans so sources such as Parquet can read only the columns actually used by the query. ([Docs.rs][7])

Agent rules:

```text
Avoid SELECT * on wide Parquet.
Project only needed leaves in nested data.
Remember filter-only columns may be needed by the scan even if absent from final projection.
```

---

## 15.10 Row group pruning

### Enable / default

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.pruning = true;
```

### Table-level option

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE facts
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://bucket/facts/'
OPTIONS ('pruning' 'true');
```

`datafusion.execution.parquet.pruning` defaults to `true` and tells the Parquet reader to skip entire row groups using query predicates and min/max metadata stored in the Parquet file; the corresponding table option key is `pruning`. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

Best predicates for pruning:

```sql
WHERE event_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
WHERE id = 123
WHERE region IN ('us', 'eu')
WHERE amount BETWEEN 100 AND 200
```

Weak predicates for pruning:

```sql
WHERE regexp_match(description, 'foo')
WHERE lower(email) = 'x@example.com'
WHERE amount + tax > 100
```

Agent rules:

```text
Row group pruning needs useful row-group statistics.
Sort/cluster data by common filter columns before writing.
Avoid huge row groups if filters are highly selective.
Avoid functions around filter columns when a direct predicate is possible.
```

---

## 15.11 Bloom filter pruning

### Read side

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.bloom_filter_on_read = true;
```

`datafusion.execution.parquet.bloom_filter_on_read` defaults to `true` and instructs DataFusion to use available Parquet bloom filters during reads. Bloom filters are particularly useful for equality and `IN` predicates. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### Write side: global

```sql
COPY facts
TO 's3://bucket/facts_out/'
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  'bloom_filter_on_write' 'true',
  'bloom_filter_fpp' '0.01',
  'bloom_filter_ndv' '100000'
);
```

### Write side: selected columns

```sql
COPY facts
TO 's3://bucket/facts_out/'
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  'bloom_filter_enabled::id' 'true',
  'bloom_filter_enabled::customer_id' 'true',
  'bloom_filter_fpp::id' '0.01',
  'bloom_filter_ndv::id' '1000000'
);
```

Parquet format options include `BLOOM_FILTER_ENABLED`, `BLOOM_FILTER_FPP`, `BLOOM_FILTER_NDV`, and `BLOOM_FILTER_ON_WRITE`; column-specific option keys use `OPTION::COLUMN.NESTED.PATH`. ([Apache DataFusion][5])

Agent rules:

```text
Enable bloom filters for high-value equality / IN lookup columns.
Good columns: id, customer_id, device_id, trace_id, order_id.
Bad columns: boolean flags, very low-cardinality dimensions, frequently-scanned metrics.
Bloom filters cost write time and file size; test read/write tradeoff.
```

---

## 15.12 Page index and page pruning

### Enable / default

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.enable_page_index = true;
```

### Table option

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE facts
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://bucket/facts/'
OPTIONS ('enable_page_index' 'true');
```

`ENABLE_PAGE_INDEX` defaults to `true` and reads Parquet data-page-level metadata, if present, to reduce I/O and decoding; the config setting `datafusion.execution.parquet.enable_page_index` has the same read-side meaning. ([Apache DataFusion][5])

Writer-side supporting options:

```sql
COPY facts
TO 's3://bucket/facts_out/'
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  'statistics_enabled' 'page',
  'column_index_truncate_length' '64'
);
```

`STATISTICS_ENABLED` can be `none`, `chunk`, or `page`, and the default documented value is `page`; `COLUMN_INDEX_TRUNCATE_LENGTH` controls truncation of min/max values in column indexes. ([Apache DataFusion][5])

Agent rules:

```text
Page pruning only helps if files contain page index / page statistics.
Write with statistics_enabled=page for DataFusion-optimized outputs.
Use page pruning for selective predicates inside large row groups.
If files come from other engines, verify page index presence with diagnostics.
```

---

## 15.13 Predicate pushdown / late materialization

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.pushdown_filters = true;
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.reorder_filters = true;
```

`datafusion.execution.parquet.pushdown_filters` defaults to `false`; when enabled, filter expressions are applied during Parquet decoding to reduce rows decoded, and the docs call this optimization “late materialization.” `reorder_filters` also defaults to `false`; when enabled, DataFusion heuristically reorders filters during Parquet decoding. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

Related read-side knobs:

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.force_filter_selections = false;
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.max_predicate_cache_size = '0';
```

`force_filter_selections` forces RowSelections when pushdown filters are enabled; `max_predicate_cache_size` controls memory used to cache predicate evaluation results, with lower values reducing memory but potentially increasing I/O/CPU. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

Agent rules:

```text
pushdown_filters=false is the conservative default.
Enable pushdown_filters only after benchmark coverage.
Enable reorder_filters when multiple filters have very different selectivity/cost.
Regex/string-heavy filters may be expensive; cheap predicates should evaluate first.
Track memory when predicate cache is enabled.
```

---

## 15.14 Metadata size hints and metadata fetching

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.metadata_size_hint = 524288;
```

`metadata_size_hint` tells DataFusion how many bytes at the end of a Parquet file to optimistically fetch for metadata; the default is 512 KiB, which can avoid one I/O request per file when the metadata fits, but if metadata is larger than the hint, two reads are still needed. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

Table option:

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE facts
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://bucket/facts/'
OPTIONS ('metadata_size_hint' '1048576');
```

Agent rules:

```text
Remote object stores: metadata_size_hint can reduce round trips.
Many-column / many-row-group files may need larger hints.
Too large a hint can over-fetch metadata bytes from small files.
Benchmark on real files and object-store latency.
```

---

## 15.15 INT96 timestamp handling

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.coerce_int96 = 'us';
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.coerce_int96_tz = 'UTC';
```

`datafusion.execution.parquet.coerce_int96` is used when Parquet physical `INT96` timestamps should be read at a resolution other than nanoseconds; the docs call out Spark as a system that stores microsecond-resolution timestamps in INT96 to support a larger date range. `coerce_int96_tz` applies an optional timezone when `coerce_int96` is set; `UTC` is recommended when callers need Arrow timestamps to be timezone-aware for Spark `TimestampType`-style semantics. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

Agent rules:

```text
Only set coerce_int96 when reading legacy/Spark-style INT96 files.
Set coerce_int96_tz='UTC' when Spark semantics require timezone-aware Arrow timestamps.
Golden-test timestamp ranges, time zones, and round trips.
Avoid writing new INT96 if modern timestamp encodings are acceptable.
```

---

## 15.16 String / binary read compatibility

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.schema_force_view_types = true;
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.binary_as_string = false;
```

`schema_force_view_types` defaults to `true` and reads Parquet `Utf8`/`LargeUtf8` columns as `Utf8View`, and `Binary`/`LargeBinary` as `BinaryView`; `binary_as_string` defaults to `false` and can read binary columns as strings for legacy writers that failed to set the UTF8 flag. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

Agent rules:

```text
Default string read path may produce Utf8View.
Set binary_as_string only for known legacy files.
Test UDFs against Utf8View/BinaryView if they downcast arrays.
Use arrow_typeof audits after registration.
```

---

## 15.17 Encryption options

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE encrypted_parquet_table
(
  double_field DOUBLE,
  float_field FLOAT
)
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 'pq/'
OPTIONS (
  'format.crypto.file_encryption.encrypt_footer' 'true',
  'format.crypto.file_encryption.footer_key_as_hex' '30313233343536373839303132333435',
  'format.crypto.file_encryption.column_key_as_hex::double_field' '31323334353637383930313233343530',
  'format.crypto.file_encryption.column_key_as_hex::float_field' '31323334353637383930313233343531',
  'format.crypto.file_decryption.footer_key_as_hex' '30313233343536373839303132333435',
  'format.crypto.file_decryption.column_key_as_hex::double_field' '31323334353637383930313233343530',
  'format.crypto.file_decryption.column_key_as_hex::float_field' '31323334353637383930313233343531'
);
```

DataFusion’s CLI datasource docs show Parquet encryption/decryption options in `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE`, with binary keys encoded as hexadecimal strings and column-specific keys using `::column_name` suffixes. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

Hex helper:

```sql
SELECT encode('0123456789012345', 'hex');
```

Agent security rules:

```text
Never log raw encryption keys.
Prefer secret-manager/object-store integration over inline SQL keys.
Redact OPTIONS in audit logs.
Use column-level keys only with clear ownership/rotation policy.
Treat encryption options as table-provider / deployment configuration, not user ad hoc SQL.
```

---

## 15.18 Compression and encoding

### Global compression

```sql
COPY facts
TO 's3://bucket/facts_out/'
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  'compression' 'zstd(3)'
);
```

### Column-specific compression

```sql
COPY facts
TO 's3://bucket/facts_out/'
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  'compression' 'snappy',
  'compression::large_text_col' 'zstd(5)'
);
```

Valid compression values include `uncompressed`, `snappy`, `gzip(level)`, `brotli(level)`, `lz4`, `zstd(level)`, and `lz4_raw`; DataFusion’s documented default is `zstd(3)`, and column-specific overrides use `compression::col`. ([Apache DataFusion][5])

### Encoding and dictionary

```sql
COPY facts
TO 's3://bucket/facts_out/'
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  'encoding::event_date' 'delta_binary_packed',
  'dictionary_enabled::region' 'true',
  'dictionary_enabled::high_cardinality_uuid' 'false'
);
```

Parquet writer options include global/column-specific `ENCODING`, `DICTIONARY_ENABLED`, and supported encodings such as `plain`, `plain_dictionary`, `rle`, `delta_binary_packed`, `delta_length_byte_array`, `delta_byte_array`, `rle_dictionary`, and `byte_stream_split`. ([Apache DataFusion][5])

Agent rules:

```text
Default compression zstd(3) is a strong analytics default.
Use snappy for broad ecosystem compatibility / faster decompression.
Use zstd for storage/I/O efficiency.
Disable dictionary on very high-cardinality columns if it hurts write/read performance.
Use delta encodings for ordered numeric/time-like values after testing.
```

---

## 15.19 Writer version and Arrow metadata

```sql
COPY facts
TO 's3://bucket/facts_out/'
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  'writer_version' '2.0',
  'skip_arrow_metadata' 'false',
  'created_by' 'my-service datafusion 55.0.0',
  'metadata::pipeline' 'daily-facts-v2',
  'metadata::owner' 'analytics-platform'
);
```

`WRITER_VERSION` accepts `1.0` or `2.0` and defaults to `1.0`; `SKIP_ARROW_METADATA` controls writing Arrow schema metadata and defaults to `false`; `CREATED_BY` sets the Parquet file metadata producer string; custom key-value metadata uses `metadata::key_name`. ([Apache DataFusion][5])

Agent rules:

```text
Use writer_version=1.0 for conservative compatibility.
Use writer_version=2.0 only after downstream reader testing.
Keep Arrow metadata unless compatibility requires omitting it.
Use created_by / metadata::* for lineage, not secrets.
```

---

## 15.20 Row group sizing

```sql
COPY facts
TO 's3://bucket/facts_out/'
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  'max_row_group_size' '1048576'
);
```

`MAX_ROW_GROUP_SIZE` sets the maximum rows per row group and defaults to 1,048,576 rows; larger row groups require more writer memory but can improve compression and scan efficiency. ([Apache DataFusion][5])

Decision table:

| Workload                           | Row group guidance                                  |
| ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| large sequential scans             | larger row groups; fewer metadata entries           |
| selective point/range filters      | moderate row groups; useful min/max granularity     |
| many columns / memory tight writer | avoid oversized row groups                          |
| object-store high latency          | avoid excessive tiny row groups/files               |
| page-index-heavy selective scans   | page stats can mitigate large row groups if written |

Agent rules:

```text
Default 1M rows is a reasonable baseline.
Tune row groups with real queries and file statistics.
Do not blindly maximize row group size.
Sort/cluster by common predicates before writing for better row-group pruning.
```

---

## 15.21 Data page and dictionary page sizing

```sql
COPY facts
TO 's3://bucket/facts_out/'
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  'data_pagesize_limit' '1048576',
  'data_page_row_count_limit' '20000',
  'dictionary_page_size_limit' '1048576',
  'write_batch_size' '1024'
);
```

Parquet writer knobs include best-effort data page size, best-effort page row-count limit, dictionary page size limit, and write batch size; documented defaults are 1 MiB data pages, 20,000 rows per data page, 1 MiB dictionary pages, and 1,024 rows per write batch. ([Apache DataFusion][5])

Agent rules:

```text
Smaller pages -> finer-grained page pruning, more metadata overhead.
Larger pages -> better compression, less metadata, coarser pruning.
write_batch_size affects writer memory/throughput behavior.
Change page sizing only with benchmark and downstream-reader tests.
```

---

## 15.22 Parallel writer tuning

```sql
COPY facts
TO 's3://bucket/facts_out/'
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  'allow_single_file_parallelism' 'true',
  'maximum_parallel_row_group_writers' '4',
  'maximum_buffered_record_batches_per_stream' '8'
);
```

`ALLOW_SINGLE_FILE_PARALLELISM` defaults to `true` and enables parallel serialization of columns in a single file; `MAXIMUM_PARALLEL_ROW_GROUP_WRITERS` defaults to `1`; `MAXIMUM_BUFFERED_RECORD_BATCHES_PER_STREAM` defaults to `2`. The config docs note the defaults are tuned for minimum memory in streaming plans, and increasing the row-group writer / buffered-batch values may help when writing large files from already in-memory data if the system has idle cores and can tolerate more memory. ([Apache DataFusion][5])

Output-file-level controls:

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.minimum_parallel_output_files = 4;
SET datafusion.execution.soft_max_rows_per_output_file = 50000000;
SET datafusion.execution.max_buffered_batches_per_output_file = 2;
```

DataFusion’s execution config includes minimum parallel output files, soft maximum rows per output file, and maximum buffered batches per output file; these control output parallelism and buffering at a higher write-output level. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

Agent rules:

```text
Streaming pipeline / memory-tight:
  keep defaults.

Large in-memory export / idle CPU:
  increase maximum_parallel_row_group_writers.
  increase maximum_buffered_record_batches_per_stream.
  monitor peak RSS.

Object-store output:
  prefer multiple output files over one huge file unless downstream requires single file.
  avoid tiny-file explosion with soft_max_rows_per_output_file.
```

---

## 15.23 `write_parquet` from DataFrame

```rust
use datafusion::dataframe::DataFrameWriteOptions;
use datafusion::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    let df = ctx
        .read_parquet("s3://bucket/raw/events/", ParquetReadOptions::default())
        .await?
        .filter(col("event_date").gt_eq(lit("2026-01-01")))?
        .select(vec![
            col("event_id"),
            col("event_date"),
            col("user_id"),
            col("amount"),
        ])?;

    df.write_parquet(
        "s3://bucket/curated/events/",
        DataFrameWriteOptions::new(),
        None,
    )
    .await?;

    Ok(())
}
```

`DataFrame::write_parquet` eagerly executes the DataFrame and writes Parquet file(s); it is available under the `parquet` feature. ([Docs.rs][8])

Partitioned output:

```rust
use datafusion::dataframe::DataFrameWriteOptions;

let options = DataFrameWriteOptions::new()
    .with_partition_by(vec!["event_date".to_string(), "region".to_string()]);

df.write_parquet("s3://bucket/curated/events/", options, None)
    .await?;
```

---

## 15.24 `COPY ... STORED AS PARQUET`

```sql
COPY (
  SELECT
    event_id,
    user_id,
    amount,
    event_date,
    region
  FROM raw_events
  WHERE amount IS NOT NULL
  ORDER BY event_date, event_id
)
TO 's3://bucket/curated/events/'
STORED AS PARQUET
PARTITIONED BY (event_date, region)
OPTIONS (
  'compression' 'zstd(3)',
  'max_row_group_size' '1048576',
  'statistics_enabled' 'page',
  'bloom_filter_enabled::event_id' 'true',
  'bloom_filter_enabled::user_id' 'true',
  'metadata::pipeline' 'curated-events-v1'
);
```

`COPY` can export a query or table to Parquet, can partition output, and can pass Parquet options; the format-options docs explicitly show one Parquet file written per query partition and column-specific overrides such as `compression::column1`. ([Apache DataFusion][5])

---

## 15.25 Parquet diagnostics

### SQL `EXPLAIN`

```sql
EXPLAIN
SELECT event_id
FROM facts
WHERE event_date = DATE '2026-05-22'
  AND user_id = 'u123';
```

### Runtime metrics

```sql
EXPLAIN ANALYZE
SELECT event_id
FROM facts
WHERE event_date = DATE '2026-05-22'
  AND user_id = 'u123';
```

DataFusion’s explain docs state that `EXPLAIN` shows plans without running, `EXPLAIN VERBOSE` includes more planning detail, and `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` runs the query and includes runtime metrics collected by operators. ([Apache DataFusion][9])

### CLI Parquet metadata helper

```sql
SELECT
  path_in_schema,
  row_group_id,
  row_group_num_rows,
  stats_min,
  stats_max,
  total_compressed_size
FROM parquet_metadata('facts.parquet')
WHERE path_in_schema = '"event_date"';
```

The `parquet_metadata` helper is documented as a DataFusion CLI-only diagnostic function, not a default embedded engine function. Use it for file-layout and pruning diagnosis in the CLI; do not assume it exists in a plain `SessionContext` unless registered. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

## 15.26 Production read profiles

### Conservative default

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.pruning = true;
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.enable_page_index = true;
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.bloom_filter_on_read = true;
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.pushdown_filters = false;
```

### More aggressive selective-scan profile

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.pruning = true;
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.enable_page_index = true;
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.bloom_filter_on_read = true;
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.pushdown_filters = true;
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.reorder_filters = true;
```

### Legacy Spark INT96 profile

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.coerce_int96 = 'us';
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.coerce_int96_tz = 'UTC';
```

Agent rule:

```text
Read profile selection must be benchmarked on real Parquet files:
  row group count
  page index availability
  bloom filter availability
  predicate shape
  object-store latency
  batch size / memory limits
```

### Analytics lake default

```sql
COPY facts
TO 's3://bucket/facts/'
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  'compression' 'zstd(3)',
  'statistics_enabled' 'page',
  'max_row_group_size' '1048576',
  'writer_version' '1.0',
  'skip_arrow_metadata' 'false'
);
```

```sql
COPY facts
TO 's3://bucket/facts_snappy/'
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  'compression' 'snappy',

```

TO 's3://bucket/facts_lookup/'
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (

  'statistics_enabled' 'page',

## 15.28 Dataset layout advisory

```text
Good layout:
  /lake/events/event_date=2026-05-22/region=us/part-000.parquet
  /lake/events/event_date=2026-05-22/region=eu/part-001.parquet

Bad layout:
  /lake/events/*.parquet
  /lake/events/user_id=<millions-of-values>/...
  /lake/events/mixed-schema-files/
  /lake/events/no-sort/no-stats/no-page-index/
```

Dataset rules:

```text
Partition by low/moderate-cardinality predicates used in most queries.
Sort/cluster within files by range-filter columns.
Write page statistics for selective scans.
Write bloom filters for high-value equality keys.
Avoid many tiny files.
Avoid massive single-row-group files unless scans are broad.
Keep schemas compatible across files.
Use metadata_size_hint for remote file-footers when needed.
```

---

## 15.29 Security and object-store considerations

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE facts
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  'aws.access_key_id' '******',
  'aws.secret_access_key' '******',
  'aws.region' 'us-east-2'
)
LOCATION 's3://bucket/path/file.parquet';
```

DataFusion CLI docs document explicit S3 credentials in `OPTIONS`, standard AWS environment/config fallback, unsigned public bucket reads, GCS service-account options, and other S3-compatible stores. For production services, prefer object-store registration or environment/secret-manager integration over embedding secrets in SQL text. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

Agent rules:

```text
Do not log SQL containing credentials.
Do not expose CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE to untrusted users without path/credential policy.
Use per-tenant object-store registries for credential isolation.
Disable direct path SQL in public endpoints.
```

---

## 15.30 Version-sensitive / test-required areas

```text
[ ] pushdown_filters performance profile
[ ] reorder_filters behavior
[ ] INT96 timestamp coercion
[ ] Utf8View / BinaryView read schema
[ ] binary_as_string legacy files
[ ] bloom filter write/read interop
[ ] page index presence and read benefit
[ ] writer_version compatibility
[ ] encryption options
[ ] parallel writer memory use
[ ] Hive partition schema types
[ ] remote metadata_size_hint tuning
```

DataFusion’s current docs expose many Parquet knobs with explicit defaults, but practical behavior depends on file layout, writer metadata, object-store latency, query predicates, and pinned DataFusion/Arrow/Parquet versions. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

---

## 15.31 Anti-pattern inventory

* `SELECT *` against wide Parquet files when only a few columns are needed.
* Wildcard Parquet locations instead of directory roots.
* Directory paths without trailing `/`.
* Mixed incompatible schemas under one table directory.
* Very high-cardinality Hive partitions.
* Writing no page stats, then expecting page pruning.
* Expecting bloom-filter pruning when bloom filters were never written.
* Enabling `pushdown_filters` in production without benchmark coverage.
* Disabling `pruning` or `enable_page_index` without a compatibility/performance reason.
* Overlarge row groups for highly selective workloads.
* Tiny row groups / tiny files for broad scan workloads.
* Logging Parquet encryption keys or cloud credentials in SQL.
* Assuming `parquet_metadata()` exists in embedded DataFusion.
* Treating `metadata_size_hint` as universally optimal; it is file/object-store dependent.
* Using INT96 defaults for Spark legacy data without validating timestamp semantics.
* Skipping Arrow metadata without downstream reader compatibility tests.

---

## 15.32 Agent checklist

```text
[ ] Enable DataFusion parquet feature.
[ ] Choose read path: read_parquet / register_parquet / CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE.
[ ] Use ParquetReadOptions::default() for normal Rust reads; move advanced tuning into config/table options when needed.
[ ] Use directory roots with trailing `/`; avoid wildcards.
[ ] Validate schema with DESCRIBE / arrow_typeof / df.schema().
[ ] Validate Hive partition columns and file schema separately.
[ ] Keep pruning=true and enable_page_index=true unless measured otherwise.
[ ] Use bloom_filter_on_read=true when files have bloom filters.
[ ] Write bloom filters only for high-value equality / IN columns.
[ ] Benchmark pushdown_filters and reorder_filters before enabling.
[ ] Tune metadata_size_hint for remote large-metadata files.
[ ] Set coerce_int96/coerce_int96_tz for Spark/legacy INT96 files.
[ ] Choose compression deliberately: zstd(3) default, snappy compatibility.
[ ] Use statistics_enabled=page for DataFusion-optimized outputs.
[ ] Tune max_row_group_size with real query workload and memory constraints.
[ ] Use writer_version=1.0 for conservative compatibility; test 2.0.
[ ] Keep Arrow metadata unless downstream readers require otherwise.
[ ] Tune parallel writers only when CPU is idle and memory budget allows.
[ ] Use staging + atomic publish for overwrite/replace dataset workflows.
```

## 15.33 Parquet changes in DataFusion 54

### Nested leaf-level projection and struct-member filter pushdown

DataFusion 54 pushes **nested projections down to Parquet leaf columns**: selecting `payload.device.id` decodes only the leaf column(s) actually referenced instead of materializing the whole `payload` struct. Filters on struct members (`WHERE payload.device.id = 7`) likewise push down into Parquet decoding, so row-group/page pruning and late materialization apply to nested fields, not just top-level columns. Wide structs where queries touch a few members see the largest wins; no configuration is required — write nested field accesses and let the planner prune.

### Statistics-proven-true filter skipping

Pruning has historically used min/max statistics to skip row groups where a predicate is provably **false**. DataFusion 54 adds the dual: when statistics prove a predicate is **true for every row** in a container (for example `WHERE x > 0` on a row group with `min(x) = 5`), per-row predicate evaluation is skipped for that container entirely. Highly selective *and* highly non-selective filters both get cheaper; no new configuration is involved, but accurate Parquet statistics matter more than before.

### INT96 timezone coercion

`datafusion.execution.parquet.coerce_int96_tz` is new in 54 and complements the existing `coerce_int96` resolution option: it applies an optional timezone to coerced INT96 timestamps (`'UTC'` recommended for Spark `TimestampType` semantics). See §15.15 for the INT96 walkthrough.

### Content-defined chunking (experimental writer feature)

The 54 Parquet writer can use **content-defined chunking (CDC)** for data-page boundaries, which makes page splits content-stable so that unchanged data regions produce byte-identical pages across rewrites (deduplication-friendly for content-addressed storage):

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.parquet.content_defined_chunking.enabled = true;
-- tuning knobs (defaults shown):
--   content_defined_chunking.min_chunk_size = 262144   (256 KiB)
--   content_defined_chunking.max_chunk_size = 1048576  (1 MiB)
--   content_defined_chunking.norm_level = 0            (recommended range [-3, 3])
```

Caveats: CDC is **experimental and disabled by default**, and enabling it **disables parallel Parquet writing** — the writer falls back to serial page production. Do not enable it on hot write paths without benchmarking; it maps to `WriterProperties::content_defined_chunking` in parquet-rs.

### Encryption property conversions are now fallible

The conversions between config-level and parquet-rs encryption properties became `TryFrom`/`TryInto` in 54 (they were infallible `From` in 53): `FileEncryptionProperties::try_from(config_props)?` and `FileDecryptionProperties::try_from(config_props)?` return `Result`, surfacing invalid key/footer configurations as errors at conversion time. Code that used `.into()` must switch to `.try_into()?` and handle the error.

Agent rules:

```text
Use nested field access directly; leaf projection/pushdown is automatic in 54.
Keep Parquet statistics enabled; proven-true skipping depends on them.
Set coerce_int96_tz='UTC' for Spark-written INT96 files needing tz-aware timestamps.
Treat content_defined_chunking as experimental; it disables parallel writes.
Replace .into() with .try_into()? for Parquet encryption property conversions.
```

# DataFusion Advanced — 16) Object stores and remote locations

Style target follows the uploaded advanced-reference pattern. 

## 16.0 Remote-source mental model

```text
SQL / DataFrame path
  → LOCATION / path / URL
  → ObjectStoreRegistry lookup by URL prefix
  → ObjectStore implementation
      file://
      https://
      s3://
      gs://
      oss://
      cos://
      custom://
  → ListingTable / file source
  → schema inference / listing / partition discovery / scan
  → Arrow RecordBatch stream
```

DataFusion’s built-in `ListingTable` reads Parquet, JSON, CSV, or Avro files from one or more local or remote directories, supports Hive-style partitioning, optional compression, directly reading from remote object stores, file metadata caching, and related listing behavior. DataFusion’s `RuntimeEnv` owns an `ObjectStoreRegistry`, which maps URLs to object-store instances used during query execution. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 16.1 Location surfaces

| Surface                 | Syntax / API                                                             | Use                               |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------- |
| direct path SQL         | `SELECT * FROM 's3://bucket/path/'`                                      | trusted CLI/ad hoc                |
| external table SQL      | `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE t STORED AS PARQUET LOCATION 's3://bucket/path/'` | named SQL table                   |
| Rust direct read        | `ctx.read_parquet("s3://bucket/path/", ...)`                             | Rust DataFrame path               |
| Rust table registration | `ctx.register_parquet("t", "s3://bucket/path/", ...)`                    | named table for SQL/DataFrame     |
| object-store registry   | `ctx.register_object_store(url, store)`                                  | custom stores/credentials         |
| listing table           | `ctx.register_listing_table(...)`                                        | advanced multi-file/table control |

DataFusion CLI docs show local/remote files queried directly in single quotes, including local CSV files, local directories, remote HTTPS Parquet files, and S3/GCS-style paths; embedded Rust direct path SQL requires explicitly enabling URL-table access, which DataFusion marks as security-sensitive because it permits SQL to access local files directly. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

## 16.2 `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE` location syntax

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE table_name
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 'scheme://bucket_or_host/path/';
```

Supported location classes documented by DataFusion CLI include local paths, HTTP(S), S3 (`s3://`), GCS (`gs://`), OSS (`oss://`), and COS (`cos://`) through `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE` and/or direct quoted path access. The SQL DDL reference states that `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE` registers a local filesystem or remote object-store location as a named table and accepts `CSV`, `ARROW`, `PARQUET`, `AVRO`, and `JSON` file types. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE hits
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 'https://datasets.example.org/hits_1.parquet';

CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE facts
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://bucket/facts/';

CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE events
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 'gs://bucket/events/';
```

---

## 16.3 HTTP(S)

### Direct SQL path

```sql
SELECT count(*)
FROM 'https://datasets.example.org/path/file.parquet';
```

### External table

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE hits
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 'https://datasets.example.org/path/file.parquet';

SELECT count(*)
FROM hits;
```

DataFusion CLI docs show reading a remote Parquet file via HTTP(S) both directly and as an external table. HTTP(S) is best for public static datasets or controlled endpoints; use explicit object-store registration for authenticated/custom HTTP stores in embedded applications. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Agent rules:

```text
HTTP(S):
  good for public immutable files
  weak for directory-style listing unless the object store supports it
  avoid for private data unless auth layer is explicitly handled
  prefer external table registration for repeated queries
```

---

## 16.4 S3

### Explicit credentials in SQL

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  'aws.access_key_id' '******',
  'aws.secret_access_key' '******',
  'aws.region' 'us-east-2'
)
LOCATION 's3://bucket/path/file.parquet';
```

### Environment credentials

```bash
export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-2
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=******
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=******
```

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://bucket/path/file.parquet';
```

DataFusion CLI supports S3 through `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE` options and standard AWS configuration methods via the AWS config crate. The documented S3 credential precedence is: explicit `OPTIONS`, then standard AWS configuration/environment mechanisms, then unsigned requests if no credentials are specified. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

### Unsigned public S3 bucket

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE nyc_taxi_rides
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://altinity-clickhouse-data/nyc_taxi_rides/data/tripdata_parquet/'
OPTIONS ('aws.skip_signature' 'true');
```

DataFusion documents `aws.SKIP_SIGNATURE true` / `aws.skip_signature` for unsigned public S3 reads; `aws.nosign` is an alias for `skip_signature`, and `AWS_SKIP_SIGNATURE` is the corresponding environment variable. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

### S3 option / environment map

| Environment variable                     | SQL option              | Meaning                  |
| ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`                      | `aws.access_key_id`     | access key               |
| `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`                  | `aws.secret_access_key` | secret key               |
| `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`                     | `aws.region`            | region                   |
| `AWS_ENDPOINT`                           | `aws.endpoint`          | custom endpoint          |
| `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`                      | `aws.token`             | session token            |
| `AWS_SKIP_SIGNATURE`                     | `aws.skip_signature`    | unsigned requests        |
| `AWS_ALLOW_HTTP`                         | none listed             | permit non-TLS HTTP      |
| `AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI` | none listed             | ECS IAM role credentials |

This mapping is documented in the DataFusion CLI data-source guide. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

### Programmatic S3 object store registration

```toml
[dependencies]
datafusion = "55.0.0"
object_store = { version = "0.13", features = ["aws"] }
url = "2"
```

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;

use datafusion::prelude::*;
use object_store::aws::AmazonS3Builder;
use url::Url;

fn register_s3(ctx: &SessionContext) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let s3 = AmazonS3Builder::new()
        .with_region("us-east-2")
        .with_bucket_name("my-bucket")
        .with_access_key_id("...")
        .with_secret_access_key("...")
        .build()
        .map_err(|e| datafusion::error::DataFusionError::External(Box::new(e)))?;

    ctx.register_object_store(
        &Url::parse("s3://my-bucket")?,
        Arc::new(s3),
    );

    Ok(())
}
```

`AmazonS3Builder` is available on the `object_store` crate’s `aws` feature and configures an S3 connection with region, bucket, and credentials. `SessionContext::register_object_store` registers an `ObjectStore` for a URL prefix so DataFusion can resolve matching locations. ([Docs.rs][5])

---

## 16.5 GCS

### SQL credentials via service account path

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  'gcp.service_account_path' '/tmp/gcs.json'
)
LOCATION 'gs://bucket/path/file.parquet';
```

### Environment variable

```bash
export GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT=/tmp/gcs.json
```

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 'gs://bucket/path/file.parquet';
```

DataFusion CLI docs state that Google Cloud Storage data sources require configured connection credentials, show `gcp.service_account_path` in `OPTIONS`, and document `GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` as an environment-variable path for credentials. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

Agent rules:

```text
GCS:
  use gs://bucket/path/
  prefer service account environment / runtime registration in services
  avoid embedding service-account paths in public SQL logs
  use directory roots for datasets
  validate Hive partition discovery on gs:// paths
```

---

## 16.6 OSS — Alibaba Cloud Object Storage Service

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  'aws.access_key_id' '******',
  'aws.secret_access_key' '******',
  'aws.oss.endpoint' 'https://bucket.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com'
)
LOCATION 'oss://bucket/path/file.parquet';
```

DataFusion CLI docs document Alibaba OSS support with `oss://` locations and require connection credentials; supported `OPTIONS` are access key ID, secret access key, and endpoint, with the OSS endpoint format `https://{bucket}.{oss-region-endpoint}`. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Agent rules:

```text
OSS:
  location scheme: oss://bucket/path
  endpoint option: aws.oss.endpoint
  endpoint includes bucket prefix
  treat credentials as S3-compatible options
  isolate tenants by endpoint/bucket/credential policy
```

---

## 16.7 COS — Tencent Cloud Object Storage

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  'aws.access_key_id' '******',
  'aws.secret_access_key' '******',
  'aws.cos.endpoint' 'https://cos.ap-singapore.myqcloud.com'
)
LOCATION 'cos://bucket/path/file.parquet';
```

DataFusion CLI docs document Tencent COS support with `cos://` locations and require credentials; supported `OPTIONS` are access key ID, secret access key, and endpoint, with endpoint format `https://cos.{cos-region-endpoint}`. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Agent rules:

```text
COS:
  location scheme: cos://bucket/path
  endpoint option: aws.cos.endpoint
  endpoint does not include bucket prefix in the same style as OSS
  treat credentials as S3-compatible options
  verify endpoint format under pinned DataFusion/object_store version
```

---

## 16.8 Object store registry

### Runtime-level object-store registry

```text
RuntimeEnv
  memory_pool
  disk_manager
  cache_manager
  object_store_registry
```

`RuntimeEnv` manages execution resources, including memory, disk, cache, and `ObjectStoreRegistry`; the registry maps URLs to object-store instances. ([Docs.rs][6])

### Register object store with `SessionContext`

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;

use datafusion::object_store::local::LocalFileSystem;
use datafusion::prelude::*;
use url::Url;

let ctx = SessionContext::new();

ctx.register_object_store(
    &Url::parse("file://")?,
    Arc::new(LocalFileSystem::new()),
);
```

`SessionContext::register_object_store(url, object_store)` registers an `ObjectStore` for a URL prefix; the docs show registering `LocalFileSystem` for the `file://` prefix. ([Docs.rs][7])

### Register object store with `RuntimeEnv`

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;

use datafusion::execution::runtime_env::RuntimeEnv;
use datafusion::object_store::local::LocalFileSystem;
use url::Url;

let runtime_env = RuntimeEnv::default();

runtime_env.register_object_store(
    &Url::try_from("file://")?,
    Arc::new(LocalFileSystem::new()),
);
```

`RuntimeEnv::register_object_store` registers a custom store for a URL; the docs explicitly mention using this for schemes without built-in support, such as `hdfs://namenode:port/...`, and the method returns any previously registered store for that scheme/prefix. ([Docs.rs][6])

### Runtime builder customization

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;

use datafusion::execution::runtime_env::RuntimeEnvBuilder;
use datafusion::prelude::*;

let runtime = RuntimeEnvBuilder::new()
    .with_object_store_registry(my_registry)
    .build_arc()?;

let state = SessionStateBuilder::new()
    .with_runtime_env(runtime)
    .with_default_features()
    .build();

let ctx = SessionContext::from(state);
```

`RuntimeEnvBuilder::with_object_store_registry` customizes the registry used to get object stores by URL, which is the correct boundary for application-wide remote-storage policy. ([Docs.rs][8])

---

## 16.9 Directory paths over wildcards

### Do not generate

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 'gs://bucket/*.parquet';
```

### Generate

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 'gs://bucket/my_table/';
```

DataFusion CLI docs state that wildcards such as `*.parquet` or recursive wildcard patterns are not supported because wildcard semantics are not universal across storage backends such as S3 and GCS; instead, specify a directory path and DataFusion reads all compatible files in that directory. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Agent rules:

```text
Remote dataset path:
  use directory root
  end directory paths with /
  ensure all files under root are compatible
  avoid glob/wildcard assumptions
  use Hive partition directories for pruning/filtering
```

---

## 16.10 Remote partition discovery

### Object paths

```text
gs://bucket/my_table/a=1/b=100/file1.parquet
gs://bucket/my_table/a=2/b=200/file2.parquet
```

### SQL

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE my_table
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 'gs://bucket/my_table/';

SELECT count(*)
FROM my_table
WHERE b = 200;
```

When a specified directory path has a Hive-compliant partition structure, DataFusion CLI automatically parses and incorporates the Hive columns and values into the table schema and data; the docs show `a=1/b=100` and `a=2/b=200` paths being queried with `WHERE b=200`. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Agent rules:

```text
Remote Hive partitioning:
  layout: col=value/col=value/file
  location points to table root
  partition columns become queryable fields
  filter partition columns for pruning
  keep partition cardinality bounded
  avoid schema conflicts between file columns and partition columns
```

---

## 16.11 Direct path SQL vs registered external table

| Mode                  | Example                                                     | Use                           | Risk                     |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| direct path           | `SELECT * FROM 's3://bucket/table/'`                        | trusted CLI/ad hoc            | ungoverned path exposure |
| external table        | `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE t ... LOCATION 's3://bucket/table/'` | stable SQL object             | DDL governance needed    |
| Rust registry         | `ctx.register_parquet("t", "s3://bucket/table/", ...)`      | application-controlled source | code-managed lifecycle   |
| object-store registry | `ctx.register_object_store(&url, store)`                    | custom credentials/stores     | operational complexity   |

DataFusion CLI docs support direct remote location queries without table registration, while the DDL docs support registering remote locations as external tables. In embedded contexts, direct URL-table access should be enabled only when intentionally allowing SQL path access. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

## 16.12 Credential policy

### SQL `OPTIONS` credentials

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE test
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  'aws.access_key_id' '******',
  'aws.secret_access_key' '******',
  'aws.region' 'us-east-2'
)
LOCATION 's3://bucket/path/file.parquet';
```

### Environment credentials

```bash
export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-2
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=******
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=******
export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=******
```

### Runtime / registry credentials

```rust
// Build provider-specific ObjectStore in code.
// Register store for a URL prefix.
// Keep credentials in app config / secret manager, not SQL text.
ctx.register_object_store(&url, store);
```

DataFusion docs allow credentials in SQL `OPTIONS`, but they also document environment-based credentials and standard SDK/provider resolution; because SQL strings are often logged or visible to users, production services should prefer environment/secret-manager/object-store registry configuration over inline credentials. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Credential precedence for S3 in the CLI is documented as explicit `OPTIONS`, then AWS config/environment mechanisms, then unsigned requests when no credentials are specified. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

## 16.13 Unsigned public buckets

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE public_dataset
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://public-bucket/path/'
OPTIONS ('aws.skip_signature' 'true');
```

DataFusion documents unsigned S3 access using `aws.SKIP_SIGNATURE true`; it also states that if no credentials are specified, the CLI uses unsigned S3 requests, enabling reads from public buckets. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Agent rules:

```text
Unsigned reads:
  good for public datasets
  do not use for private buckets
  prefer explicit skip_signature=true when public-read behavior is intentional
  audit that paths are expected public sources
```

---

## 16.14 Remote object-store performance levers

### Listing and metadata caches

`RuntimeEnvBuilder` exposes object listing and metadata cache controls such as `with_metadata_cache_limit`, `with_object_list_cache_limit`, and `with_object_list_cache_ttl`, and `RuntimeEnv` includes a `cache_manager` for temporary cache data during a session. These are important for remote datasets where listing and footer metadata requests dominate query latency. ([Docs.rs][8])

```rust
use std::time::Duration;
use datafusion::execution::runtime_env::RuntimeEnvBuilder;

let runtime = RuntimeEnvBuilder::new()
    .with_metadata_cache_limit(512 * 1024 * 1024)
    .with_object_list_cache_limit(128 * 1024 * 1024)
    .with_object_list_cache_ttl(Duration::from_secs(300))
    .build_arc()?;
```

Agent rules:

```text
Remote lake datasets:
  cache listings when table roots are stable
  cache metadata when Parquet files are reused
  invalidate/shorten TTL for frequently mutating prefixes
  avoid many tiny files
  prefer partition filters to reduce listing/scan breadth
```

---

## 16.15 Remote layout patterns

### Good

```text
s3://lake/events/event_date=2026-05-22/region=us/part-000.parquet
s3://lake/events/event_date=2026-05-22/region=eu/part-001.parquet
```

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE events
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://lake/events/';

SELECT count(*)
FROM events
WHERE event_date = DATE '2026-05-22'
  AND region = 'us';
```

### Bad

```text
s3://lake/events/*.parquet
s3://lake/events/user_id=<millions-of-values>/...
s3://lake/events/mixed_schema_files/
s3://lake/events/raw_json_blobs_only/
```

DataFusion’s remote path guidance favors directory roots over wildcards and automatically discovers Hive-style partitions in directory names; the Parquet directory rule also requires compatible schemas across files under the folder. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

## 16.16 Security posture by deployment

| Deployment              | Recommended remote-source policy                                                      |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| local CLI               | allow direct quoted paths; credentials through env                                    |
| internal batch job      | direct `read_parquet` / registered tables; credentials through runtime/env            |
| public SQL endpoint     | no direct path SQL; no DDL; registered tables only                                    |
| tenant-isolated service | separate `SessionContext` / `RuntimeEnv` / registry per tenant or credential boundary |
| governed lakehouse      | custom catalog + object-store registry + path allowlist                               |
| diagnostics CLI         | allow cache/metadata inspection; never expose secrets                                 |

DataFusion’s `enable_url_table` is explicitly security-sensitive because it allows SQL such as `SELECT * FROM 'my_file.parquet'` to access local files; the same principle applies to remote paths in untrusted SQL surfaces. ([Docs.rs][7])

---

## 16.17 Rust end-to-end: registered S3 table with read-only SQL

```rust
use datafusion::prelude::*;

pub async fn query_registered_remote_table(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    ctx.register_parquet(
        "events",
        "s3://bucket/events/",
        ParquetReadOptions::default(),
    )
    .await?;

    let options = SQLOptions::new()
        .with_allow_ddl(false)
        .with_allow_dml(false)
        .with_allow_statements(false);

    let df = ctx
        .sql_with_options(
            "SELECT event_date, count(*) AS n
             FROM events
             WHERE event_date >= DATE '2026-01-01'
             GROUP BY event_date
             ORDER BY event_date",
            options,
        )
        .await?;

    df.show().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```

`register_parquet` registers a Parquet source as a named table, while `SQLOptions` can disable DDL, DML, and statement/config SQL when accepting query text from users. ([Docs.rs][7])

---

## 16.18 Rust end-to-end: custom scheme registration

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;

use datafusion::execution::{
    runtime_env::RuntimeEnvBuilder,
    session_state::SessionStateBuilder,
};
use datafusion::prelude::*;
use url::Url;

fn context_with_custom_store(
    scheme_url: Url,
    store: Arc<dyn datafusion::object_store::ObjectStore>,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<SessionContext> {
    let runtime = RuntimeEnvBuilder::new().build_arc()?;
    runtime.register_object_store(&scheme_url, store);

    let state = SessionStateBuilder::new()
        .with_runtime_env(runtime)
        .with_default_features()
        .build();

    Ok(SessionContext::from(state))
}
```

`RuntimeEnv::register_object_store` is designed for custom URL-backed stores, including schemes without built-in support, and `RuntimeEnvBuilder` lets applications supply an object-store registry as part of the execution environment. ([Docs.rs][6])

---

## 16.19 Object-store option matrix

| Store   | URI scheme            | SQL credential/config options                                                                                 | Env vars                                                                                                                            |
| ------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| HTTP(S) | `http://`, `https://` | URL itself; custom auth requires custom store/HTTP config                                                     | app-dependent                                                                                                                       |
| S3      | `s3://`               | `aws.access_key_id`, `aws.secret_access_key`, `aws.region`, `aws.endpoint`, `aws.token`, `aws.skip_signature` | `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`, `AWS_ENDPOINT`, `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`, `AWS_SKIP_SIGNATURE`, etc. |
| GCS     | `gs://`               | `gcp.service_account_path`                                                                                    | `GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`                                                                                                            |
| OSS     | `oss://`              | `aws.access_key_id`, `aws.secret_access_key`, `aws.oss.endpoint`                                              | use configured app/env equivalents                                                                                                  |
| COS     | `cos://`              | `aws.access_key_id`, `aws.secret_access_key`, `aws.cos.endpoint`                                              | use configured app/env equivalents                                                                                                  |

The S3, GCS, OSS, and COS option names above are documented in the DataFusion CLI data-source guide. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

## 16.20 Best-practice deployment advisory

```text
Path governance:
  register known tables
  avoid arbitrary LOCATION from users
  avoid enable_url_table in services
  use catalog allowlists
  constrain object-store prefixes

Credentials:
  prefer env/secret manager/runtime registry
  avoid SQL OPTIONS secrets in logs
  isolate per-tenant credentials
  rotate keys outside SQL

Layout:
  use directory roots
  avoid wildcards
  use Hive partitions for common filters
  keep schemas compatible
  avoid tiny files
  avoid high-cardinality partitions

Performance:
  cache listings/metadata for stable prefixes
  tune cache TTL for mutating datasets
  use Parquet statistics/pruning
  filter partition columns
  project only needed columns

Safety:
  disable DDL/DML/statements for read-only SQL
  redact remote locations if they leak tenant/bucket names
  treat public unsigned buckets as explicit policy, not fallback surprise
```

---

## 16.21 Anti-pattern inventory

* Enabling `enable_url_table()` in a public SQL service.
* Accepting arbitrary `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE ... LOCATION ...` from users.
* Logging SQL that includes access keys or service-account paths.
* Using `gs://bucket/*.parquet` or `s3://bucket/**/*.parquet`.
* Registering directory datasets without trailing `/`.
* Mixing incompatible schemas in one table directory.
* Partitioning by high-cardinality IDs.
* Assuming unsigned S3 access is safe for private data.
* Using inline credentials instead of object-store registry/secret manager.
* Sharing one object-store registry across tenants with different credentials.
* Relying on HTTP(S) URLs for private authenticated data without explicit auth handling.
* Treating S3, GCS, OSS, and COS endpoint formats as interchangeable.
* Leaving listing-cache TTL high for rapidly changing prefixes.
* Forgetting that partition discovery derives values from path strings.

---

## 16.22 Agent checklist

```text
[ ] Choose access mode: direct path / CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE / register_* / custom ObjectStore.
[ ] Avoid direct path SQL for untrusted users.
[ ] Use LOCATION 'scheme://bucket/path/' for remote external tables.
[ ] Use directory roots, not wildcards.
[ ] Ensure directory paths end with `/` when intended as directories.
[ ] Use Hive-style partitions: col=value/col=value/file.
[ ] Verify partition columns appear and filter correctly.
[ ] For S3, choose explicit OPTIONS, env/AWS config, or unsigned policy.
[ ] For public S3, set aws.skip_signature intentionally.
[ ] For GCS, configure gcp.service_account_path or GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT.
[ ] For OSS, use oss:// and aws.oss.endpoint with bucket-qualified endpoint.
[ ] For COS, use cos:// and aws.cos.endpoint with COS endpoint format.
[ ] Register custom object stores through SessionContext or RuntimeEnv.
[ ] Put credentials in runtime/env/secret manager when possible.
[ ] Configure object-list / metadata caches for stable remote datasets.
[ ] Disable DDL/DML/statements when remote paths are not user-governed.
```
