# DataFusion Advanced — 17) Catalogs, schemas, and tables

Style target follows the uploaded advanced-reference pattern. 

## 17.0 Mental model: metadata hierarchy

```text id="u4km6i"
CatalogProviderList
  └─ CatalogProvider               -- catalog / database-like namespace
      └─ SchemaProvider            -- schema namespace
          └─ TableProvider         -- queryable table / view / external source / memory source
              └─ scan(...) -> ExecutionPlan -> RecordBatch stream
```

DataFusion’s catalog hierarchy is explicit: a `CatalogProviderList` contains `CatalogProvider`s, each `CatalogProvider` contains `SchemaProvider`s, and each `SchemaProvider` contains `TableProvider`s. DataFusion ships basic in-memory catalog functionality, but custom catalog implementations are expected for systems backed by local files, remote object storage, metastores, lakehouse catalogs, or governed product metadata. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

---

## 17.1 Value case

| Problem                      | Catalog-layer value                                                                            |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| SQL name resolution          | maps `catalog.schema.table` / `schema.table` / `table` to a `TableProvider`                    |
| metadata governance          | central table/schema existence, ownership, visibility, and schema control                      |
| multi-tenancy                | separate catalogs/schemas per tenant, workspace, org, or security domain                       |
| external storage integration | catalog entry points to Parquet/CSV/JSON/Avro/Arrow/object-store-backed tables                 |
| custom systems               | implement `CatalogProvider`, `SchemaProvider`, `TableProvider` for your database/lakehouse/API |
| DDL integration              | `CREATE TABLE`, `CREATE SCHEMA`, `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE`, `DROP TABLE`, views                  |
| introspection                | `SHOW TABLES`, `SHOW COLUMNS`, `information_schema.*`                                          |
| query planning               | optimizer/planner obtains table schemas, filters, statistics, constraints, scan plans          |

The `CatalogProvider` docs state that DataFusion needs catalog metadata to know which schemas/tables exist, their columns and data types, and how to access the data. ([Docs.rs][2])

---

## 17.2 Default catalog and schema

Default config keys:

```text id="co5kek"
datafusion.catalog.create_default_catalog_and_schema = true
datafusion.catalog.default_catalog = datafusion
datafusion.catalog.default_schema = public
datafusion.catalog.information_schema = false
```

The configuration reference documents these defaults: DataFusion automatically creates the default catalog/schema by default; unqualified SQL uses default catalog `datafusion` and default schema `public`; `information_schema` virtual tables are disabled unless enabled. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### Configure defaults in Rust

```rust id="vqf1i7"
use datafusion::prelude::*;

let config = SessionConfig::new()
    .with_create_default_catalog_and_schema(true)
    .with_default_catalog_and_schema("prod", "analytics")
    .with_information_schema(true);

let ctx = SessionContext::new_with_config(config);
```

### Configure defaults through low-level keys

```rust id="q6hoae"
use datafusion::prelude::*;

let mut config = SessionConfig::new();

config.set_bool("datafusion.catalog.create_default_catalog_and_schema", true)?;
config.set_str("datafusion.catalog.default_catalog", "prod")?;
config.set_str("datafusion.catalog.default_schema", "analytics")?;
config.set_bool("datafusion.catalog.information_schema", true)?;

let ctx = SessionContext::new_with_config(config);
```

### SQL resolution examples

```sql id="gdb7w2"
-- resolves using default catalog + default schema
SELECT * FROM events;

-- explicit schema under default catalog
SELECT * FROM analytics.events;

-- explicit catalog + schema + table
SELECT * FROM prod.analytics.events;
```

Agent rules:

```text id="fdbm24"
Unqualified table name = default_catalog.default_schema.table.
Default names are config, not a universal database invariant.
Set defaults explicitly in services.
Use fully qualified names for generated SQL crossing tenant/schema boundaries.
```

---

## 17.3 Core traits and responsibilities

| Trait                 | Represents                 | Required / key operations                                          | Planning role                |
| --------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------- |
| `CatalogProviderList` | named catalog collection   | register catalog, list catalog names, get catalog                  | root lookup                  |
| `CatalogProvider`     | named schema collection    | list schemas, get schema, register/deregister schema               | catalog namespace            |
| `SchemaProvider`      | named table collection     | list tables, get table, table existence, register/deregister table | schema namespace             |
| `TableProvider`       | queryable/modifiable table | schema, table type, scan, filter pushdown, insert, statistics      | logical scan → physical plan |

The catalog guide describes the trait responsibilities: `CatalogProviderList` registers/gets/lists catalogs; `CatalogProvider` sets/gets/lists schemas; `SchemaProvider` sets/gets/lists/deregisters tables and checks table existence; `TableProvider` scans underlying data for use in DataFusion. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

---

## 17.4 `CatalogProviderList`

### Concept

```rust id="b21row"
pub trait CatalogProviderList: Debug + Sync + Send {
    fn register_catalog(
        &self,
        name: String,
        catalog: Arc<dyn CatalogProvider>,
    ) -> Option<Arc<dyn CatalogProvider>>;

    fn catalog_names(&self) -> Vec<String>;

    fn catalog(&self, name: &str) -> Option<Arc<dyn CatalogProvider>>;
}
```

`CatalogProviderList` represents a list of named `CatalogProvider`s; the docs.rs catalog module lists it as the root catalog collection trait. ([Docs.rs][4])

### Use cases

```text id="bqq6nv"
single app catalog list
multi-tenant catalog list
workspace catalog list
remote metastore snapshot
dynamic file catalog wrapper
```

### Agent rules

```text id="8lyxqu"
Implement CatalogProviderList only when you need to control catalog lookup globally.
Most apps can register catalogs on SessionContext instead.
Return deterministic catalog_names() for reproducible introspection.
Avoid network calls in catalog_names(); planning is latency-sensitive.
```

---

## 17.5 `CatalogProvider`

### Concept

```rust id="vg7vba"
pub trait CatalogProvider: Any + Debug + Sync + Send {
    fn schema_names(&self) -> Vec<String>;
    fn schema(&self, name: &str) -> Option<Arc<dyn SchemaProvider>>;

    fn register_schema(
        &self,
        name: &str,
        schema: Arc<dyn SchemaProvider>,
    ) -> Result<Option<Arc<dyn SchemaProvider>>> { ... }

    fn deregister_schema(
        &self,
        name: &str,
        cascade: bool,
    ) -> Result<Option<Arc<dyn SchemaProvider>>> { ... }
}
```

`CatalogProvider` represents a catalog containing named schemas; DataFusion’s docs describe `CatalogProvider` as “sometimes called a database in other systems,” but in DataFusion it is metadata, not a storage engine by itself. In DataFusion 54, `Any` is a supertrait (the `fn as_any` boilerplate was removed); downcast via `catalog.downcast_ref::<MyCatalog>()`. ([Docs.rs][2])

### In-memory catalog

```rust id="j2jnx4"
use std::sync::Arc;
use datafusion::catalog::{CatalogProvider, MemoryCatalogProvider, MemorySchemaProvider};
use datafusion::prelude::*;

let ctx = SessionContext::new();

let catalog = Arc::new(MemoryCatalogProvider::new());
catalog.register_schema(
    "analytics",
    Arc::new(MemorySchemaProvider::new()),
)?;

ctx.register_catalog("prod", catalog);
```

`MemoryCatalogProvider` is a simple in-memory catalog implementation; `new()` instantiates it with an empty collection of schemas. ([Docs.rs][5])

### Agent rules

```text id="jferao"
CatalogProvider = schema namespace, not table storage.
Use MemoryCatalogProvider for tests, session-local apps, examples.
Use custom CatalogProvider for durable/governed catalogs.
Implement deregister_schema only if schema deletion is product-supported.
```

---

## 17.6 `SchemaProvider`

### Concept

```rust id="55d5cb"
pub trait SchemaProvider: Any + Debug + Sync + Send {
    fn table_names(&self) -> Vec<String>;

    async fn table(
        &self,
        name: &str,
    ) -> Result<Option<Arc<dyn TableProvider>>>;

    fn table_exist(&self, name: &str) -> bool;

    fn register_table(
        &self,
        name: String,
        table: Arc<dyn TableProvider>,
    ) -> Result<Option<Arc<dyn TableProvider>>> { ... }

    fn deregister_table(
        &self,
        name: &str,
    ) -> Result<Option<Arc<dyn TableProvider>>> { ... }
}
```

`SchemaProvider` represents a schema containing named tables. Its `table(name)` method is async and returns `Option<Arc<dyn TableProvider>>`; `table_exist` returns whether a table exists; `table_names` lists available tables. In DataFusion 54, `Any` is a supertrait (no `fn as_any` method to implement). ([Docs.rs][6])

### In-memory schema

```rust id="3jmkqu"
use std::sync::Arc;
use datafusion::catalog::{MemorySchemaProvider, SchemaProvider, TableProvider};

let schema = MemorySchemaProvider::new();

schema.register_table(
    "events".to_string(),
    table_provider as Arc<dyn TableProvider>,
)?;

assert!(schema.table_exist("events"));
```

The catalog guide describes `MemorySchemaProvider` as a simple `SchemaProvider` implementation storing tables in a `DashMap`, which is useful as a minimal in-memory schema implementation. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

### Agent rules

```text id="94ty6n"
SchemaProvider = table namespace.
Use table_exist for cheap existence checks.
Use table(name).await for provider retrieval.
Do not put expensive remote scans in table_names().
If remote table details require IO, batch/cache metadata before planning.
```

---

## 17.7 `TableProvider`

### Concept

```rust id="2q64wz"
pub trait TableProvider: Any + Debug + Sync + Send {
    fn schema(&self) -> Arc<Schema>;

    fn table_type(&self) -> TableType;

    async fn scan(
        &self,
        state: &dyn Session,
        projection: Option<&Vec<usize>>,
        filters: &[Expr],
        limit: Option<usize>,
    ) -> Result<Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>>;
}
```

`TableProvider` represents a queryable/modifiable table. Implementations provide the table schema, filter-pushdown capabilities, and a `scan` method that returns an `ExecutionPlan` capable of producing Arrow `RecordBatch`es. In DataFusion 54, `Any` is a supertrait — implementations no longer write `fn as_any`, and callers downcast with `provider.downcast_ref::<MyTable>()` via trait upcasting. ([Docs.rs][7])

### Built-in provider examples

```text id="wo8hqc"
MemTable             -- in-memory Vec<RecordBatch>
ListingTable         -- local/remote file datasets
ViewTable / view     -- logical-plan-backed view
StreamingTable       -- streaming partitioned dataset
TableFunction        -- table-valued function
```

The `datafusion::catalog` module lists `MemTable`, `MemoryCatalogProvider`, `MemoryCatalogProviderList`, `MemorySchemaProvider`, stream/streaming providers, view provider support, table functions, dynamic file catalog/schema providers, and listing schema provider support. ([Docs.rs][4])

### Agent rules

```text id="1q2xpe"
TableProvider is the main custom data-source boundary.
schema() must be stable and cheap.
scan() may build an execution plan with projection/filter/limit pushdown.
supports_filters_pushdown and statistics improve optimization.
insert_into implements DML/write behavior when supported.
```

---

## 17.8 `SessionContext` catalog APIs

`SessionContext` is the user-facing engine object that creates DataFrames, registers data sources as SQL tables, registers custom data sources, and executes SQL queries. ([Docs.rs][8])

### Register table

```rust id="q8j97k"
use std::sync::Arc;
use datafusion::catalog::TableProvider;
use datafusion::prelude::*;

fn register_table(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    provider: Arc<dyn TableProvider>,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    ctx.register_table("events", provider)?;
    assert!(ctx.table_exist("events")?);
    Ok(())
}
```

### Deregister table

```rust id="2u7tzu"
let previous = ctx.deregister_table("events")?;
assert!(previous.is_some());
assert!(!ctx.table_exist("events")?);
```

### Retrieve table as DataFrame

```rust id="a1imcn"
let df = ctx.table("events").await?;
df.show().await?;
```

### Retrieve provider

```rust id="cs4dkb"
let provider = ctx.table_provider("events").await?;
let schema = provider.schema();
```

### Register catalog

```rust id="g9up8j"
use std::sync::Arc;
use datafusion::catalog::{CatalogProvider, MemoryCatalogProvider};
use datafusion::prelude::*;

let catalog: Arc<dyn CatalogProvider> = Arc::new(MemoryCatalogProvider::new());
ctx.register_catalog("prod", catalog);
```

Agent rules:

```text id="kyhfal"
Use ctx.register_table for custom providers.
Use ctx.register_csv/parquet/json/avro/arrow for built-in file providers.
Use ctx.table for DataFrame access to registered sources.
Use ctx.sql for SQL access.
Use table_exist in idempotent registration/migration code.
```

---

## 17.9 In-memory catalog stack

### Build complete in-memory catalog hierarchy

```rust id="qilczb"
use std::sync::Arc;

use datafusion::catalog::{
    CatalogProvider,
    MemoryCatalogProvider,
    MemorySchemaProvider,
    SchemaProvider,
};
use datafusion::prelude::*;

fn context_with_memory_catalog() -> datafusion::error::Result<SessionContext> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    let catalog = Arc::new(MemoryCatalogProvider::new());
    let schema = Arc::new(MemorySchemaProvider::new());

    catalog.register_schema("analytics", schema)?;
    ctx.register_catalog("prod", catalog);

    Ok(ctx)
}
```

### Add table into schema before registration

```rust id="lb7vw3"
use std::sync::Arc;

use datafusion::catalog::{MemorySchemaProvider, SchemaProvider, TableProvider};

let schema = Arc::new(MemorySchemaProvider::new());

schema.register_table(
    "events".to_string(),
    events_provider as Arc<dyn TableProvider>,
)?;
```

### Value case

```text id="fmr8mp"
tests
unit fixtures
session-local scratch schemas
temporary in-memory query apps
embedded demos
migration harnesses
catalog-trait prototyping
```

### Limits

```text id="nvcj59"
no persistence across process/session lifecycle
no durable transactions
no external authorization
no remote metastore sync
no built-in multi-node metadata coherence
```

DataFusion docs state that `MemoryCatalogProvider` is used by default, has no persistence, and DataFusion does not include a complex general-purpose catalog implementation because catalog management is a key design choice for most data systems. ([Docs.rs][2])

---

## 17.10 Custom catalog implementations

### When to implement custom catalogs

```text id="g3kzvc"
durable metadata
remote metastore
lakehouse table registry
tenant/workspace isolation
access-control-aware table discovery
catalog-backed schema evolution
external table lifecycle management
audited DDL
file/object-store-backed table discovery
database-backed metadata
```

### Implementation surface

```rust id="lqrrgj"

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct MyCatalog {
    // e.g. Arc<MetadataSnapshot>, DashMap<String, Arc<dyn SchemaProvider>>, etc.
}

impl CatalogProvider for MyCatalog {
    // DataFusion 54: no `fn as_any` — `Any` is a supertrait of CatalogProvider.

    fn schema_names(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        // return stable, cached schema names
        todo!()
    }

        // return cached schema provider
        todo!()

    fn register_schema(
        &self,
        name: &str,
        schema: Arc<dyn SchemaProvider>,
    ) -> Result<Option<Arc<dyn SchemaProvider>>> {

        todo!()
    }
```

### Remote catalog caveat

DataFusion’s planning APIs are not async, so network IO cannot be performed lazily for all catalog lookups during planning; the docs recommend providing an in-memory snapshot of required remote metadata, typically via caching or batched remote access, while noting that `SchemaProvider::table` is async to simplify cases where table details require non-trivial access. ([Docs.rs][2])

Agent rules:

```text id="bspzt5"
Remote catalog implementation:
  prefetch or cache schema/table names
  keep schema_names() and table_names() cheap
  batch remote metadata calls
  use async table(name) for table-detail resolution
  avoid per-expression / per-lookup network calls during planning
  design explicit cache invalidation
```

## 17.11 Custom schema implementation

### Skeleton

```rust id="zgsdl0"
use std::any::Any;
use std::sync::Arc;

use async_trait::async_trait;
use dashmap::DashMap;
use datafusion::catalog::{SchemaProvider, TableProvider};
use datafusion::error::Result;

#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct MySchema {
    tables: DashMap<String, Arc<dyn TableProvider>>,
}

#[async_trait]
impl SchemaProvider for MySchema {
    // DataFusion 54: no `fn as_any` — `Any` is a supertrait of SchemaProvider.

    fn table_names(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut names: Vec<_> = self.tables
            .iter()
            .map(|entry| entry.key().clone())
            .collect();
        names.sort();
        names
    }

    async fn table(&self, name: &str) -> Result<Option<Arc<dyn TableProvider>>> {
        Ok(self.tables.get(name).map(|entry| entry.value().clone()))
    }

    fn table_exist(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        self.tables.contains_key(name)
    }

    fn register_table(
        &self,
        name: String,
        table: Arc<dyn TableProvider>,
    ) -> Result<Option<Arc<dyn TableProvider>>> {
        Ok(self.tables.insert(name, table))
    }

    fn deregister_table(
        &self,
        name: &str,
    ) -> Result<Option<Arc<dyn TableProvider>>> {
        Ok(self.tables.remove(name).map(|(_, table)| table))
    }
}
```

The catalog guide’s example `MemorySchemaProvider` uses a `DashMap<String, Arc<dyn TableProvider>>` as the backing table store, matching the `SchemaProvider` trait’s table registration/listing/lookup responsibilities. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

### Agent rules

```text id="9vzuj1"
Return sorted table_names() for stable introspection.
Use Arc<dyn TableProvider> for provider sharing.
Make table_exist cheap.
Make register/deregister semantics explicit: replace? reject? audit?
Enforce ownership/authorization outside raw SchemaProvider unless provider includes policy.
```

---

## 17.12 Table existence and idempotent registration

### Pattern

```rust id="h01x1m"
async fn ensure_table(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    name: &str,
    provider: Arc<dyn datafusion::catalog::TableProvider>,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    if ctx.table_exist(name)? {
        return Ok(());
    }

    ctx.register_table(name, provider)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

### Replace pattern

```rust id="tv26vs"
fn replace_table(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    name: &str,
    provider: Arc<dyn datafusion::catalog::TableProvider>,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let _old = ctx.deregister_table(name)?;
    ctx.register_table(name, provider)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

### Safer replace with audit

```rust id="7937ae"
fn replace_table_with_audit(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    name: &str,
    provider: Arc<dyn datafusion::catalog::TableProvider>,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let existed = ctx.table_exist(name)?;

    if existed {
        let previous = ctx.deregister_table(name)?;
        tracing::info!(table = name, had_previous = previous.is_some(), "replacing table");
    }

    ctx.register_table(name, provider)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

Agent rules:

```text id="boiofp"
Use IF NOT EXISTS in SQL DDL when appropriate.
Use table_exist before idempotent Rust registration.
Use deregister_table + register_table only when replacement is intentional.
Log/audit table replacement in service code.
```

---

## 17.13 DDL integration

DataFusion supports DDL using the catalog API: `CREATE TABLE`, `CREATE SCHEMA`, `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE`, views, and related catalog-affecting statements register catalog/schema/table/view metadata through provider traits. The catalog guide explicitly connects DDL support to the catalog API. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

### SQL DDL examples

```sql id="2sv176"
CREATE DATABASE prod;

CREATE SCHEMA prod.analytics;

CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE prod.analytics.events
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://bucket/events/';

CREATE VIEW prod.analytics.active_events AS
SELECT *
FROM prod.analytics.events
WHERE active = true;

DROP TABLE prod.analytics.events;
```

### Read-only SQL safety

```rust id="tfgw63"
let options = SQLOptions::new()
    .with_allow_ddl(false)
    .with_allow_dml(false)
    .with_allow_statements(false);

let df = ctx.sql_with_options(user_sql, options).await?;
```

Agent rules:

```text id="nm7rzt"
DDL mutates catalog metadata.
Disable DDL for public/read-only SQL.
Custom catalogs must decide whether CREATE/DROP are supported.
DROP TABLE removes catalog binding; it does not necessarily delete remote data.
```

## 17.14 `information_schema`

### Enable

```rust id="2b11iv"
use datafusion::prelude::*;

let config = SessionConfig::new()
    .with_information_schema(true);

let ctx = SessionContext::new_with_config(config);
```

or:

```rust id="eob9o3"
let mut config = SessionConfig::new();
config.set_bool("datafusion.catalog.information_schema", true)?;

let ctx = SessionContext::new_with_config(config);
```

`datafusion.catalog.information_schema` controls whether DataFusion exposes `information_schema` virtual tables; it defaults to `false`. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### Show tables

```sql id="kghycr"
SHOW TABLES;

SELECT *
FROM information_schema.tables;
```

DataFusion supports metadata introspection through ISO SQL `information_schema` views and DataFusion-specific `SHOW TABLES` / `SHOW COLUMNS` commands. ([Apache DataFusion][9])

### Show columns

```sql id="dck59c"
SHOW COLUMNS FROM events;

SELECT
  table_catalog,
  table_schema,
  table_name,
  column_name,
  data_type,
  is_nullable
FROM information_schema.columns
WHERE table_name = 'events';
```

`SHOW COLUMNS` or `information_schema.columns` exposes table schema metadata including data type and nullability. ([Apache DataFusion][9])

### Show config

```sql id="n125zx"
SHOW ALL;

SELECT *
FROM information_schema.df_settings;
```

DataFusion documents `SHOW ALL` and `information_schema.df_settings` as ways to inspect current session configuration options. ([Apache DataFusion][9])

### Show functions

```sql id="ip0xb1"
SHOW FUNCTIONS LIKE '%date%';

SELECT *
FROM information_schema.routines
WHERE function_name LIKE '%date%';
```

DataFusion’s `SHOW FUNCTIONS` maps to `information_schema.routines` and `information_schema.parameters`, exposing function names, descriptions, parameters, and examples. ([Apache DataFusion][9])

### Agent rules

```text id="3h4te2"
Enable information_schema for debugging, admin tools, and self-service introspection.
Consider disabling/hiding it for strict multi-tenant or least-privilege SQL endpoints.
information_schema can reveal table names, columns, functions, and settings.
Use catalog-backed authorization if exposing metadata to users.
```

## 17.15 Governance patterns

### Pattern A — one catalog per tenant

```text id="5df9gk"
CatalogProviderList
  tenant_a -> CatalogProvider
  tenant_b -> CatalogProvider
  tenant_c -> CatalogProvider
```

Use when tenants require separate object-store credentials, table namespaces, metadata visibility, lifecycle, or billing.

### Pattern B — one schema per workspace

```text id="5sk7e6"
datafusion catalog
  workspace_alpha schema
  workspace_beta schema
  workspace_gamma schema
```

Use when catalog-level policy is shared but table namespaces differ.

### Pattern C — curated / raw / temp schemas

```text id="o31w55"
prod catalog
  raw
  staging
  curated
  temp
  information_schema
```

Use for lakehouse-style pipelines where schema namespace reflects data lifecycle.

### Pattern D — read-only registered tables only

```rust id="40qs8v"
let options = SQLOptions::new()
    .with_allow_ddl(false)
    .with_allow_dml(false)
    .with_allow_statements(false);

let df = ctx.sql_with_options(user_sql, options).await?;
```

Use for public SQL endpoints: register allowed tables in a governed catalog, deny DDL/DML/config statements, optionally deny `information_schema` or filter it.

### Pattern E — catalog-backed path allowlist

```text id="6gh2zr"
User SQL:
  SELECT ... FROM curated.events

Blocked:
  SELECT ... FROM 's3://arbitrary/path'
  CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE ... LOCATION 's3://unknown/path'
```

Use `CatalogProvider`/`SchemaProvider` as the only authorized path-to-table mechanism; do not enable arbitrary URL tables for untrusted SQL.

---

## 17.16 Custom catalog + remote metadata pattern

```text id="m4ly3p"
Startup / refresh loop:
  remote metastore / object store / DB
    → fetch table list, schemas, stats, locations
    → build immutable/cached metadata snapshot
    → expose CatalogProvider / SchemaProvider over snapshot

Planning:
  DataFusion calls schema_names(), table_names(), table(name).await
    → cheap local lookup
    → returns TableProvider

Execution:
  TableProvider::scan(...)
    → uses RuntimeEnv / ObjectStoreRegistry / provider metadata
```

DataFusion docs warn that lazy network IO during planning is not viable because planning APIs are not broadly async; remote catalogs should provide cached/in-memory snapshots or batch remote calls, with `SchemaProvider::table` async available for cases where table-detail loading is needed. ([Docs.rs][2])

Agent rules:

```text id="nrrq8u"
Remote catalog:
  separate metadata refresh from query planning
  use immutable snapshots for consistency
  batch remote calls
  expose cache version / refresh timestamp
  decide stale-read policy
  fail closed on auth metadata errors
```

---

## 17.17 Catalog-backed security controls

| Control                  | Catalog-layer enforcement idea                                             |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| table allowlist          | only register allowed providers                                            |
| column masking           | expose view/table provider with masked schema/scan                         |
| row policy               | expose provider that injects filters or views per tenant                   |
| path sandbox             | external tables only through catalog, not direct URL SQL                   |
| function restrictions    | custom `SessionState` function registry + plan validation                  |
| DDL authorization        | allow `register_schema` / `register_table` only through trusted admin path |
| metadata redaction       | filter `information_schema` or disable it                                  |
| object-store credentials | per-tenant `RuntimeEnv` / object-store registry                            |

Agent rule:

```text id="iggl56"
DataFusion catalog traits are metadata APIs, not a complete authorization system.
Authorization must be built around or inside catalog/table-provider implementations.
```

---

## 17.18 Information-schema leakage advisory

`information_schema.tables`, `information_schema.columns`, `information_schema.df_settings`, and function metadata are useful for agents and users, but they expose schema, function, and configuration information. DataFusion explicitly supports these views/commands for metadata introspection. ([Apache DataFusion][9])

Public service policy:

```text id="loj11e"
Option 1:
  disable information_schema
  expose curated metadata API instead

Option 2:
  enable information_schema only in admin contexts

Option 3:
  implement catalog/view filtering so users see only authorized objects
```

Agent-generated SQL policy:

```text id="dp8v2s"
Do not auto-query information_schema in a tenant/user context unless permitted.
Prefer server-provided schema manifests for LLM agents.
```

## 17.20 Catalog-backed custom table registration

### Register provider directly in default schema

```rust id="nozzy0"
use std::sync::Arc;
use datafusion::catalog::TableProvider;
use datafusion::prelude::*;

fn register_default_schema_table(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    table_name: &str,
    provider: Arc<dyn TableProvider>,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    ctx.register_table(table_name, provider)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

### Register provider in explicit catalog/schema

```rust id="j1x1eb"
use std::sync::Arc;

use datafusion::catalog::{CatalogProvider, MemoryCatalogProvider, MemorySchemaProvider, SchemaProvider, TableProvider};
use datafusion::prelude::*;

fn register_qualified_table(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    catalog_name: &str,
    schema_name: &str,
    table_name: &str,
    provider: Arc<dyn TableProvider>,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let catalog = Arc::new(MemoryCatalogProvider::new());
    let schema = Arc::new(MemorySchemaProvider::new());

    schema.register_table(table_name.to_string(), provider)?;
    catalog.register_schema(schema_name, schema)?;
    ctx.register_catalog(catalog_name, catalog);

    Ok(())
}
```

SQL access:

```sql id="5qdbt9"
SELECT *
FROM prod.analytics.events;
```

---

## 17.21 DDL and custom provider behavior

DDL statements are routed through catalog/schema/table provider APIs; custom catalogs decide how much mutation is supported. DataFusion’s catalog guide states that DDL queries use the catalog API, and `TableProvider` is where DML such as `INSERT INTO` becomes relevant. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

Design matrix:

| SQL                      | Required support                                   |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `CREATE DATABASE`        | catalog list / catalog creation policy             |
| `CREATE SCHEMA`          | `CatalogProvider::register_schema`                 |
| `DROP SCHEMA`-like API   | `CatalogProvider::deregister_schema` if supported  |
| `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE`  | schema table registration + file/provider factory  |
| `CREATE TABLE AS SELECT` | schema table registration + memory/custom provider |
| `DROP TABLE`             | `SchemaProvider::deregister_table`                 |
| `INSERT INTO`            | `TableProvider::insert_into`                       |
| `SELECT`                 | `TableProvider::scan`                              |

Agent rules:

```text id="8ty22v"
If custom catalog is read-only, reject register/deregister methods clearly.
If custom catalog supports DDL, define persistence and concurrency semantics.
If custom table supports DML, implement insert_into and count result contract.
```

---

## 17.22 TableProvider governance hooks

`TableProvider` includes more than `schema` and `scan`; it can expose filter-pushdown support, statistics, constraints, table type, and DML behavior. DataFusion’s docs call out `schema`, `supports_filters_pushdown`, and `scan` as important planning information. ([Docs.rs][7])

Governance patterns:

```text id="lgja33"
schema():
  hide unauthorized columns
  rename / normalize fields
  expose only stable contract

scan():
  inject required tenant filters
  enforce projection allowlist
  reject unsupported filters/limits
  return custom ExecutionPlan with audit

supports_filters_pushdown():
  advertise pushdown accurately
  avoid claiming exact pushdown if provider will re-check incorrectly

statistics():
  expose row counts / column stats for optimizer
  avoid leaking sensitive distribution info if metadata is protected

insert_into():
  enforce write permissions
  implement append/overwrite semantics safely
```

---

## 17.23 Catalog testing matrix

```text id="lr5gfy"
[ ] default catalog/schema names are expected
[ ] fully qualified table resolution works
[ ] unqualified table resolution uses configured defaults
[ ] register_table makes table visible to ctx.table and SQL
[ ] deregister_table removes table from SQL resolution
[ ] table_exist matches table lookup
[ ] catalog_names/schema_names/table_names sorted or stable enough for snapshots
[ ] information_schema.tables lists expected objects when enabled
[ ] information_schema.columns lists expected schema
[ ] SHOW TABLES / SHOW COLUMNS match information_schema results
[ ] DDL CREATE TABLE / DROP TABLE mutates expected schema
[ ] DDL disabled through SQLOptions for read-only contexts
[ ] custom catalog denies/permits register_schema as designed
[ ] custom schema denies/permits register_table as designed
[ ] remote catalog cache refresh behavior is deterministic
```

---

## 17.24 Production deployment advisory

```text id="s9wq76"
Small CLI / script:
  default SessionContext catalog is sufficient
  MemoryCatalogProvider is acceptable

Batch ETL:
  explicit catalog/schema names
  register external tables programmatically or through trusted DDL
  enable information_schema for diagnostics if safe

SQL service:
  disable DDL/DML for user SQL
  register only governed tables
  avoid direct URL table access
  disable or filter information_schema
  use custom catalogs for tenant isolation

Lakehouse engine:
  implement custom CatalogProvider / SchemaProvider over metastore
  TableProvider per table format
  cached remote metadata snapshot
  object-store registry per credential domain

Multi-tenant SaaS:
  separate catalogs or schemas per tenant
  per-tenant SessionContext / RuntimeEnv if credentials differ
  metadata visibility controlled at catalog/schema layer
```

---

## 17.25 Anti-pattern inventory

* Treating default `MemoryCatalogProvider` as durable metadata.
* Sharing one default catalog across tenants with different table visibility.
* Enabling `information_schema` in a public endpoint without metadata-access policy.
* Performing remote network calls inside every `schema_names()` / `table_names()` call.
* Returning unstable order from `table_names()` and snapshot-testing it.
* Implementing `table_exist` inconsistently with `table(name).await`.
* Claiming filter pushdown support in `TableProvider` but not enforcing/validating it.
* Registering arbitrary user-provided external locations into a shared catalog.
* Using unqualified SQL table names in generated multi-catalog/multi-tenant SQL.
* Replacing tables without audit.
* Assuming `DROP TABLE` deletes external data.
* Assuming `CREATE DATABASE` creates a durable DBMS database.
* Implementing a custom catalog with no cache invalidation/refresh strategy.
* Letting `information_schema.df_settings` expose runtime configuration to untrusted users.
* Using catalog metadata as authorization without a security review.

# DataFusion Advanced — 18) Custom `TableProvider`

Style target follows the uploaded advanced-reference pattern. 

## 18.0 Custom table provider mental model

```text id="vp8eul"
Catalog / SessionContext registration
  → Arc<dyn TableProvider>
      ├─ schema()                      -- logical table schema
      ├─ table_type()                  -- Base / View / Temporary / etc.
      ├─ supports_filters_pushdown()   -- predicate pushdown capability contract
      ├─ scan(...)                     -- planning-time: build ExecutionPlan
      ├─ statistics()                  -- table-level stats, if known
      ├─ constraints()                 -- table constraints, if supported
      └─ insert_into(...)              -- optional write path

scan(...)
  → Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>
      ├─ properties()                  -- partitioning / ordering / boundedness / emission
      ├─ children()
      ├─ with_new_children(...)
      └─ execute(partition, TaskContext)
            → SendableRecordBatchStream
                → poll()
                    → external API / DB / object store / generated data
                    → Arrow RecordBatch
```

DataFusion’s custom table provider guide identifies three collaborating layers: `TableProvider` describes the table and produces a physical plan, `ExecutionPlan` describes how to compute the result including partitioning and ordering, and `SendableRecordBatchStream` is the async stream that yields `RecordBatch` values one at a time during execution. The guide summarizes the call sequence: `TableProvider::scan()` is called once during planning, `ExecutionPlan::execute()` is called once per partition, and streams produce rows during execution. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

---

## 18.1 Value case: when a custom `TableProvider` is worth it

Use a custom provider when the data source is **not already best represented by built-in file readers, `MemTable`, `ListingTable`, or `StreamTable`**.

| Source shape                          | Prefer                                                             | Reason                                                         |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| already have `Vec<RecordBatch>`       | `MemTable`                                                         | no custom provider needed                                      |
| stream of batches                     | `StreamTable` / stream provider                                    | source already matches streaming model                         |
| SQL view / transformation             | `ViewTable` / logical plan                                         | no custom physical source                                      |
| standard Parquet/CSV/JSON/Avro files  | `ListingTable` / built-ins                                         | DataFusion already handles listing, partitioning, file pruning |
| custom file format                    | `ListingTable` + custom `FileFormat` / `FileSource` / `FileOpener` | reuse file-discovery and partition support                     |
| database/API/SaaS/index/custom source | `TableProvider + ExecutionPlan + stream`                           | complete source-specific pushdown/parallelism/auth/control     |

DataFusion’s guide explicitly recommends choosing the highest-level building block that fits: `MemTable` for in-memory batches, `StreamTable` for async streams, `ViewTable` for logical transformations, `ListingTable` plus file-format abstractions for file sources, and full `TableProvider + ExecutionPlan + stream` only when full control is needed. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

---

## 18.2 Trait import stance

Current released docs expose `TableProvider` through the DataFusion catalog/datasource surfaces; examples may use `datafusion::catalog::TableProvider`, while docs.rs pages are under `datafusion::datasource`. Use the path that compiles for your pinned version; keep all `datafusion-*` subcrates pinned to the same version if importing subcrate traits directly.

```rust id="qsm8uj"
// Common top-level imports in current examples/docs:
use datafusion::catalog::{Session, TableProvider};
use datafusion::datasource::TableType;

// Other core imports:
use datafusion::arrow::datatypes::{Schema, SchemaRef};
use datafusion::common::Result;
use datafusion::logical_expr::{Expr, TableProviderFilterPushDown};
use datafusion::physical_plan::ExecutionPlan;
```

The `TableProvider` docs describe the trait as a queryable/modifiable table source that provides Arrow `RecordBatch`es and communicates planning information such as schema, filter pushdown support, and a scan `ExecutionPlan`. ([Docs.rs][2])

---

## 18.3 Required `TableProvider` methods

### Minimal read-only provider shape

```rust id="adzn3m"
use std::{any::Any, sync::Arc};

use async_trait::async_trait;
use datafusion::arrow::datatypes::SchemaRef;
use datafusion::catalog::{Session, TableProvider};
use datafusion::common::Result;
use datafusion::datasource::TableType;
use datafusion::logical_expr::Expr;
use datafusion::physical_plan::ExecutionPlan;

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct MyTableProvider {
    schema: SchemaRef,
}

#[async_trait]
impl TableProvider for MyTableProvider {
    // DataFusion 54: no `fn as_any` — `Any` is a supertrait of TableProvider.

    fn schema(&self) -> SchemaRef {
        Arc::clone(&self.schema)
    }

    fn table_type(&self) -> TableType {
        TableType::Base
    }

    async fn scan(
        &self,
        state: &dyn Session,
        projection: Option<&Vec<usize>>,
        filters: &[Expr],
        limit: Option<usize>,
    ) -> Result<Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>> {
        Ok(Arc::new(MyExecPlan::new(
            Arc::clone(&self.schema),
            projection.cloned(),
            filters.to_vec(),
            limit,
        )))
    }
}
```

`scan` creates an `ExecutionPlan` for scanning the table with optional projection, filter, and limit hints; the plan is responsible for scanning source partitions in a streaming, parallelized fashion. Projection indices refer to fields in `schema()`, and DataFusion passes projection information so sources can avoid reading unused columns. ([Docs.rs][2])

---

## 18.4 `schema()`: contract and constraints

### Purpose

```text id="d7yc0p"
schema() -> Arc<Schema>
  = authoritative logical output schema for this table
  = column order used by projection indices
  = source of field names/types/nullability for SQL/DataFrame planning
  = schema all produced RecordBatches must conform to, after projection
```

### Schema construction

```rust id="b9ctvk"
use std::sync::Arc;

use datafusion::arrow::datatypes::{DataType, Field, Schema, SchemaRef};

let schema: SchemaRef = Arc::new(Schema::new(vec![
    Field::new("id", DataType::Int64, false),
    Field::new("region", DataType::Utf8, true),
    Field::new("amount", DataType::Float64, true),
]));
```

### Projected schema helper pattern

```rust id="8nhtah"
use datafusion::arrow::datatypes::SchemaRef;
use datafusion::common::Result;

fn project_schema(schema: &SchemaRef, projection: Option<&Vec<usize>>) -> Result<SchemaRef> {
    match projection {
        Some(indices) => Ok(Arc::new(schema.project(indices)?)),
        None => Ok(Arc::clone(schema)),
    }
}
```

### Agent rules

```text id="8ld1j1"
schema() must be cheap and stable.
schema() must not call remote APIs on every planning pass.
schema field order defines projection index semantics.
Every RecordBatch returned by the stream must match the output schema exactly.
If projection is pushed down, the ExecutionPlan stream schema should be projected.
If provider exposes dynamic schema, cache/snapshot it before planning.
```

`RecordBatchStream` implementors must guarantee every `RecordBatch` returned by the stream has the same schema returned from the stream’s `schema()` method. ([Docs.rs][3])

---

## 18.5 `scan(...)`: planning-time boundary

### Contract

```rust id="xbo37g"
async fn scan(
    &self,
    state: &dyn Session,
    projection: Option<&Vec<usize>>,
    filters: &[Expr],
    limit: Option<usize>,
) -> Result<Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>>;
```

`scan()` receives three key pushdown hints: `projection` for needed columns, `filters` for predicates the optimizer wants the provider to evaluate during scan, and `limit` for row-count caps. The custom provider guide stresses that `scan()` runs during planning, should return quickly, and should build metadata/plan objects—not perform I/O, network calls, or heavy computation. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

### Correct `scan` behavior

```text id="xfi3q0"
DO:
  clone config/metadata handles
  compute cheap partition selection from already-known metadata
  store projection/filter/limit in ExecutionPlan
  build PlanProperties
  return Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>

DO NOT:
  fetch remote data
  open long-lived network streams
  block on API calls
  decode records
  allocate huge buffers
  perform scan execution
```

The guide explains why heavy `scan()` work is harmful: it slows planning, runs single-threaded before execution parallelism, prevents optimizer reductions from helping, and bypasses DataFusion’s execution-time concurrency and memory management. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

---

## 18.6 `scan_with_args(...)`: structured scan arguments

`scan_with_args(state, ScanArgs)` is the structured newer scan variant. It returns `ScanResult` and can carry additional information such as ordering preferences that may not be available through the legacy scan method. Providers can override it when they need structured scan arguments beyond projection/filter/limit. ([Docs.rs][2])

```rust id="79u1uc"
async fn scan_with_args<'a>(
    &self,
    state: &dyn Session,
    args: ScanArgs<'a>,
) -> Result<ScanResult> {
    // optional advanced override; default delegates to scan(...)
    todo!()
}
```

Agent rules:

```text id="vc1czj"
Implement scan first.
Override scan_with_args only when structured args add required capability.
Keep scan_with_args lightweight for the same reason scan must be lightweight.
```

---

## 18.7 Projection pushdown

### Meaning

```text id="2hy4dn"
projection: Option<&Vec<usize>>
  None          => all columns requested
  Some(indices) => return only schema fields at these positions, in this order
```

DataFusion passes projection information to let table providers scan only columns actually used in the query, which can substantially improve performance for columnar or remote sources. ([Docs.rs][2])

### Implementation pattern

```rust id="41trp7"
#[derive(Debug)]
struct MyExecPlan {
    full_schema: SchemaRef,
    projected_schema: SchemaRef,
    projection: Option<Vec<usize>>,
}

impl MyExecPlan {
    fn new(
        full_schema: SchemaRef,
        projection: Option<Vec<usize>>,
    ) -> datafusion::common::Result<Self> {
        let projected_schema = match &projection {
            Some(p) => Arc::new(full_schema.project(p)?),
            None => Arc::clone(&full_schema),
        };

        Ok(Self {
            full_schema,
            projected_schema,
            projection,
        })
    }
}
```

### Remote API mapping

```text id="6bs78x"
projection indices:
  [0, 3, 4]

full schema:
  0 id
  1 region
  2 event_type
  3 amount
  4 event_ts

remote API selected fields:
  ["id", "amount", "event_ts"]
```

### Agent rules

```text id="praw9y"
Use projection to reduce remote SELECT columns, API fields, JSON keys, DB columns.
Maintain output column order exactly as projection order.
If filters require extra columns internally, do not expose them unless requested.
If remote API cannot project fields, still return projected RecordBatches to DataFusion.
Test projection permutations, empty projection if possible, and duplicate/invalid indices defensively.
```

## 18.8 Predicate pushdown

### Capability declaration

```rust id="mw3urb"
fn supports_filters_pushdown(
    &self,
    filters: &[&Expr],
) -> Result<Vec<TableProviderFilterPushDown>> {
    Ok(filters
        .iter()
        .map(|expr| {
            if Self::is_source_filterable(expr) {
                TableProviderFilterPushDown::Exact
            } else {
                TableProviderFilterPushDown::Unsupported
            }
        })
        .collect())
}
```

`supports_filters_pushdown` must return one element per input filter. Each result is `Exact`, `Inexact`, or `Unsupported`; by default, DataFusion assumes all filters are unsupported and does not pass them to `scan`. `Exact` means the source fully evaluates the predicate and no remaining `FilterExec` is needed for that predicate; `Inexact` means the source reduces data but DataFusion still applies a filter above the scan; `Unsupported` means DataFusion handles it entirely. ([Docs.rs][2])

### Practical classification

| Source ability                                             | Return        | Example                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| API can fully evaluate `region = 'us'` server-side         | `Exact`       | SQL DB predicate, indexed API filter         |
| source can skip partitions/files but not rows inside files | `Inexact`     | file stats, partition pruning, metadata skip |
| source cannot evaluate predicate better than DataFusion    | `Unsupported` | arbitrary regex on text, complex UDF         |

### Filter matching skeleton

```rust id="pvdht1"
use datafusion::logical_expr::{Expr, Operator, TableProviderFilterPushDown};

fn classify_filter(expr: &Expr) -> TableProviderFilterPushDown {
    match expr {
        Expr::BinaryExpr(binary)
            if binary.op == Operator::Eq && references_column(&binary.left, "region") =>
        {
            TableProviderFilterPushDown::Exact
        }

        Expr::Between(between)
            if between.expr.try_as_col().is_some_and(|c| c.name == "event_date") =>
        {
            TableProviderFilterPushDown::Inexact
        }

        _ => TableProviderFilterPushDown::Unsupported,
    }
}
```

### Agent rules

```text id="w0ugox"
Only claim Exact when no false rows can remain for that predicate.
Use Inexact for partition/file/stat pruning.
Use Unsupported when DataFusion's vectorized FilterExec is not worse.
Never push down a filter and silently change SQL null semantics.
Never claim Exact for approximate remote filters.
Return vector length exactly equal to filters.len().
```

The guide cautions that DataFusion’s in-memory `FilterExec` is optimized, so filter pushdown should be implemented only when the source can avoid I/O or work more effectively than DataFusion itself. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

---

## 18.9 Limit pushdown

`limit: Option<usize>` tells the provider a row cap the optimizer wants to push into the scan. If specified, the provider must produce **at least** this many rows but may produce more; if any inexact filters are pushed down, the limit cannot be pushed down because doing so can produce too few final rows after DataFusion applies the residual filter. ([Docs.rs][2])

### Implementation rule

```rust id="bi20dg"
let rows_to_fetch = match limit {
    Some(n) if no_inexact_filters => Some(n),
    _ => None,
};
```

### Agent rules

```text id="s5j388"
Limit pushdown is safe for exact filters or no filters.
Limit pushdown is unsafe with inexact filters unless provider compensates by over-fetching.
Remote APIs with page_size/limit should map this carefully.
Never use limit as a hard final-output guarantee inside provider.
DataFusion may still enforce final LIMIT above scan.
```

---

## 18.10 Statistics

### Trait method

```rust id="q82f91"
fn statistics(&self) -> Option<Statistics> {
    Some(self.statistics.clone())
}
```

The `TableProvider::statistics()` method returns table statistics when available; docs.rs notes it is not presently used in mainline DataFusion but can be used by downstream repositories with specialized optimizer rules, for example join reordering. ([Docs.rs][2])

### Useful statistics

```text id="66tpz1"
row count
total byte size
column null counts
column min/max
distinct count estimates
partition/file counts
remote source cardinality estimates
```

### Agent rules

```text id="v4aq9j"
Statistics should be cheap, cached, and conservative.
Unknown is better than wrong.
Stale high-level estimates are acceptable for planning if marked approximate.
Never expose sensitive distribution stats to untrusted metadata users without policy.
Use stats to support custom optimizer rules and join ordering.
```

## 18.11 Constraints

### Trait method

```rust id="xtobk9"
fn constraints(&self) -> Option<&Constraints> {
    Some(&self.constraints)
}
```

`constraints()` returns `None` when a table does not support constraints, and `Some(&Constraints::empty())` when the table supports constraints but has none. Constraints can describe table-level invariants useful for validation and optimization. ([Docs.rs][2])

### Constraint examples

```text id="6whnwe"
primary key / unique key
not-null columns
foreign-key-like relationship metadata
check-like constraints
provider-level guaranteed ordering or partitioning
```

### Agent rules

```text id="sxetjh"
Return None if constraints are unsupported or unknown.
Return empty constraints only when provider intentionally supports the concept.
Do not advertise constraints not enforced by the source.
Constraints are metadata contracts; stale/false constraints can break optimizations.
```

## 18.12 Table definition, logical plan, defaults

`TableProvider` also exposes optional metadata methods such as `get_table_definition()`, `get_logical_plan()`, and `get_column_default(column)`. Table definitions help introspection; logical plans are relevant for views; column defaults matter for inserts and DDL-like behavior. ([Docs.rs][2])

```rust id="0k46e7"
fn get_table_definition(&self) -> Option<&str> {
    self.create_sql.as_deref()
}

fn get_column_default(&self, column: &str) -> Option<&Expr> {
    self.defaults.get(column)
}
```

Agent rules:

```text id="55h84x"
Use get_table_definition for DDL/introspection fidelity.
Use get_logical_plan for view-like providers.
Use get_column_default only when insert/default semantics are supported.
```

## 18.13 Partitioning and `ExecutionPlan` properties

### Why properties matter

`ExecutionPlan` properties tell DataFusion about output partitioning, ordering, boundedness, and emission. The custom provider guide stresses that output partitioning determines parallelism, and output ordering lets the optimizer avoid unnecessary `SortExec` nodes when the source is naturally sorted. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

### PlanProperties construction pattern

```rust id="b8t3ub"
use std::sync::Arc;

use datafusion::physical_expr::EquivalenceProperties;
use datafusion::physical_plan::{
    execution_plan::{Boundedness, EmissionType},
    Partitioning, PlanProperties,
};

let properties = Arc::new(PlanProperties::new(
    EquivalenceProperties::new(Arc::clone(&schema)),
    Partitioning::UnknownPartitioning(num_partitions),
    EmissionType::Incremental,
    Boundedness::Bounded,
));
```

### Natural partitioning strategies

| Source             | Natural partition            |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------- |
| object-store files | file / object / row-group    |
| sharded DB         | shard                        |
| partitioned API    | region / tenant / date range |
| queue/stream       | topic partition              |
| indexed source     | key range                    |
| generated data     | partition id                 |

The guide recommends matching the provider’s partitioning to natural layout: files, shards, regions, or key ranges; `execute()` is called once per partition, and partitions become async tasks scheduled by the runtime. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

### Agent rules

```text id="mej3fe"
Do not report one partition if source can parallelize naturally.
Do not report many partitions if they all serialize through one locked resource.
Expose natural ordering only when guaranteed.
Incorrect ordering metadata can yield wrong results by removing needed sorts.
Incorrect partitioning metadata can cause wrong joins/aggregates.
```

---

## 18.14 Custom `ExecutionPlan`

### Required conceptual methods

```rust id="0mhk1f"
impl ExecutionPlan for MyExecPlan {
    fn apply_expressions(
        &self,
        _f: &mut dyn FnMut(
            &std::sync::Arc<dyn datafusion::physical_expr::PhysicalExpr>,
        ) -> datafusion::common::Result<datafusion::common::tree_node::TreeNodeRecursion>,
    ) -> datafusion::common::Result<datafusion::common::tree_node::TreeNodeRecursion> {
        // This illustrated node owns no PhysicalExpr roots.
        Ok(datafusion::common::tree_node::TreeNodeRecursion::Continue)
    }

    fn name(&self) -> &str { "MyExecPlan" }

    fn properties(&self) -> &Arc<PlanProperties> {
        &self.properties
    }

    fn children(&self) -> Vec<&Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>> {
        vec![]
    }

    fn with_new_children(
        self: Arc<Self>,
        children: Vec<Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>>,
    ) -> Result<Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>> {
        assert!(children.is_empty());
        Ok(self)
    }

    fn execute(
        &self,
        partition: usize,
        context: Arc<TaskContext>,
    ) -> Result<SendableRecordBatchStream> {
        // construct and return stream; do not fetch data here
        todo!()
    }
}
```

`ExecutionPlan` nodes represent physical-plan operators. `execute(partition, context)` returns an async `SendableRecordBatchStream` that incrementally computes a partition of the output. Methods such as `properties()` communicate optimizer-relevant output properties, and `children()` plus `replace_children()` are the preferred physical-optimizer rewrite contract in DataFusion 55; the deprecated required `with_new_children()` method should delegate to `replace_children`. ([Docs.rs][4])

### `execute()` boundary

```text id="2jamxp"
execute() SHOULD:
  validate partition id
  clone schema/config handles
  construct stream
  set up bounded channels if needed
  return quickly

execute() SHOULD NOT:
  block on async operations
  read all data
  call remote API synchronously
  allocate full output
```

The guide states that `execute()` should construct and return a stream without heavy work; data production happens when the stream is polled. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

## 18.15 Custom `RecordBatchStream`

### Type alias

```rust id="dtmobf"
pub type SendableRecordBatchStream =
    Pin<Box<dyn RecordBatchStream<Item = Result<RecordBatch, DataFusionError>> + Send>>;
```

`SendableRecordBatchStream` is a specialized async stream of `RecordBatch`es that can be passed between threads and knows its schema even if it has no data; after a stream returns an error, callers should not poll it again, and returning `Ready(None)` after error/end is recommended. ([Docs.rs][5])

### Easiest stream: `RecordBatchStreamAdapter`

```rust id="ki7wtr"
use datafusion::execution::SendableRecordBatchStream;
use datafusion::physical_plan::stream::RecordBatchStreamAdapter;
use futures::stream;

fn make_stream(schema: SchemaRef) -> SendableRecordBatchStream {
    let s = stream::iter(vec![
        Ok(make_batch_1(schema.clone())),
        Ok(make_batch_2(schema.clone())),
    ]);

    Box::pin(RecordBatchStreamAdapter::new(schema, s))
}
```

The custom provider guide recommends `RecordBatchStreamAdapter` as the easiest way to bridge any `futures::Stream<Item = Result<RecordBatch>>` into a `SendableRecordBatchStream`. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

### Async API stream pattern

```rust id="k3bwyy"
use async_stream::try_stream;
use datafusion::physical_plan::stream::RecordBatchStreamAdapter;

fn api_stream(
    schema: SchemaRef,
    client: Arc<MyApiClient>,
    request: MyRequest,
) -> SendableRecordBatchStream {
    let schema_for_stream = Arc::clone(&schema);

    let s = try_stream! {
        let mut cursor = None;

        loop {
            let page = client.fetch_page(&request, cursor.clone()).await?;
            if page.rows.is_empty() {
                break;
            }

            let batch = convert_api_rows_to_batch(Arc::clone(&schema_for_stream), page.rows)?;
            yield batch;

            cursor = page.next_cursor;
            if cursor.is_none() {
                break;
            }
        }
    };

    Box::pin(RecordBatchStreamAdapter::new(schema, s))
}
```

### Blocking source pattern

```rust id="zfdy6p"
use datafusion::physical_plan::stream::RecordBatchStreamAdapter;
use tokio_stream::wrappers::ReceiverStream;

fn blocking_stream(
    schema: SchemaRef,
    config: MyBlockingConfig,
) -> SendableRecordBatchStream {
    let (tx, rx) = tokio::sync::mpsc::channel(2);

    tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
        for result in blocking_read_batches(config) {
            if tx.blocking_send(result).is_err() {
                break; // receiver dropped: query cancelled
            }
        }
    });

    let stream = ReceiverStream::new(rx);
    Box::pin(RecordBatchStreamAdapter::new(schema, stream))
}
```

If stream work is blocking or CPU-bound for long periods, the custom provider guide says to avoid blocking the Tokio runtime; offload blocking work to a dedicated thread pool and send batches through a channel. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

### Agent rules

```text id="fgx7ct"
Stream poll is where I/O and computation belong.
Every yielded RecordBatch must match stream schema.
Use bounded channels for backpressure.
Stop producing when receiver is dropped.
Yield/await regularly; do not monopolize Tokio tasks.
Map source errors into DataFusionError.
```

---

## 18.16 Complete minimal generated table provider

```rust id="hytx1b"
use std::{any::Any, sync::Arc};

use async_trait::async_trait;
use datafusion::arrow::{
    array::{ArrayRef, Int64Array},
    datatypes::{DataType, Field, Schema, SchemaRef},
    record_batch::RecordBatch,
};
use datafusion::catalog::{Session, TableProvider};
use datafusion::common::Result;
use datafusion::datasource::TableType;
use datafusion::execution::{SendableRecordBatchStream, TaskContext};
use datafusion::logical_expr::Expr;
use datafusion::physical_expr::EquivalenceProperties;
use datafusion::physical_plan::{
    execution_plan::{Boundedness, EmissionType},
    stream::RecordBatchStreamAdapter,
    DisplayAs, DisplayFormatType, ExecutionPlan, Partitioning, PlanProperties,
};
use futures::stream;

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct CountingTable {
    schema: SchemaRef,
    num_partitions: usize,
    rows_per_partition: usize,
}

impl CountingTable {
    pub fn new(num_partitions: usize, rows_per_partition: usize) -> Self {
        let schema = Arc::new(Schema::new(vec![
            Field::new("partition", DataType::Int64, false),
            Field::new("value", DataType::Int64, false),
        ]));

        Self {
            schema,
            num_partitions,
            rows_per_partition,
        }
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl TableProvider for CountingTable {
    fn schema(&self) -> SchemaRef {
        Arc::clone(&self.schema)
    }

    fn table_type(&self) -> TableType {
        TableType::Base
    }

    async fn scan(
        &self,
        _state: &dyn Session,
        projection: Option<&Vec<usize>>,
        _filters: &[Expr],
        limit: Option<usize>,
    ) -> Result<Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>> {
        let projected_schema = match projection {
            Some(p) => Arc::new(self.schema.project(p)?),
            None => Arc::clone(&self.schema),
        };

        Ok(Arc::new(CountingExec {
            full_schema: Arc::clone(&self.schema),
            projected_schema,
            projection: projection.cloned(),
            num_partitions: self.num_partitions,
            rows_per_partition: limit
                .unwrap_or(self.rows_per_partition)
                .min(self.rows_per_partition),
            properties: Arc::new(PlanProperties::new(
                EquivalenceProperties::new(Arc::clone(&self.schema)),
                Partitioning::UnknownPartitioning(self.num_partitions),
                EmissionType::Incremental,
                Boundedness::Bounded,
            )),
        }))
    }
}

#[derive(Debug)]
struct CountingExec {
    full_schema: SchemaRef,
    projected_schema: SchemaRef,
    projection: Option<Vec<usize>>,
    num_partitions: usize,
    rows_per_partition: usize,
    properties: Arc<PlanProperties>,
}

impl DisplayAs for CountingExec {
    fn fmt_as(
        &self,
        _t: DisplayFormatType,
        f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>,
    ) -> std::fmt::Result {
        write!(
            f,
            "CountingExec: partitions={}, rows_per_partition={}, projection={:?}",
            self.num_partitions,
            self.rows_per_partition,
            self.projection,
        )
    }
}

impl ExecutionPlan for CountingExec {
    fn apply_expressions(
        &self,
        _f: &mut dyn FnMut(
            &std::sync::Arc<dyn datafusion::physical_expr::PhysicalExpr>,
        ) -> datafusion::common::Result<datafusion::common::tree_node::TreeNodeRecursion>,
    ) -> datafusion::common::Result<datafusion::common::tree_node::TreeNodeRecursion> {
        // This illustrated node owns no PhysicalExpr roots.
        Ok(datafusion::common::tree_node::TreeNodeRecursion::Continue)
    }

    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        "CountingExec"
    }

    fn properties(&self) -> &Arc<PlanProperties> {
        &self.properties
    }

    fn children(&self) -> Vec<&Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>> {
        vec![]
    }

    fn with_new_children(
        self: Arc<Self>,
        children: Vec<Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>>,
    ) -> Result<Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>> {
        assert!(children.is_empty());
        Ok(self)
    }

    fn execute(
        &self,
        partition: usize,
        _context: Arc<TaskContext>,
    ) -> Result<SendableRecordBatchStream> {
        let full_schema = Arc::clone(&self.full_schema);
        let out_schema = Arc::clone(&self.projected_schema);
        let projection = self.projection.clone();
        let rows = self.rows_per_partition;

        let batch_stream = stream::once(async move {
            let partition_values = Int64Array::from(vec![partition as i64; rows]);
            let values = Int64Array::from((0..rows as i64).collect::<Vec<_>>());

            let full_batch = RecordBatch::try_new(
                full_schema,
                vec![
                    Arc::new(partition_values) as ArrayRef,
                    Arc::new(values) as ArrayRef,
                ],
            )?;

            match projection {
                Some(indices) => Ok(full_batch.project(&indices)?),
                None => Ok(full_batch),
            }
        });

        Ok(Box::pin(RecordBatchStreamAdapter::new(
            out_schema,
            batch_stream,
        )))
    }
}
```

This follows the official guide’s minimal provider shape: `scan()` builds a plan with metadata, `ExecutionPlan::execute()` builds a stream, and heavy work happens inside the stream when polled. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

---

## 18.17 Registering and using the provider

```rust id="blld9q"
use std::sync::Arc;
use datafusion::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    let provider = CountingTable::new(4, 1_000);
    ctx.register_table("counting", Arc::new(provider))?;

    let df = ctx
        .sql(
            "SELECT partition, value
             FROM counting
             WHERE value < 10
             ORDER BY partition, value
             LIMIT 20",
        )
        .await?;

    df.show().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```

Once a `TableProvider` is registered with a `SessionContext`, it becomes queryable through SQL and DataFrame APIs; the guide shows registering `CountingTable` under the name `counting` and querying it with SQL. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

## 18.18 Remote API provider design

### Provider architecture

```text id="0449vu"
MyApiTableProvider
  schema: SchemaRef
  client: Arc<MyApiClient>
  table_config: MyTableConfig
  static_metadata: MyTableMetadata

scan(...)
  parse projection -> requested fields
  parse filters -> API filter request
  parse limit -> page cap / row cap
  create MyApiExec

MyApiExec::execute(partition)
  create request for partition/shard/range
  return stream

stream poll
  async fetch page
  convert rows -> Arrow arrays
  yield RecordBatch
  continue next cursor
```

### Remote API pushdown mapping

| DataFusion hint | API mapping                                                    |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| projection      | selected fields / sparse response / GraphQL field list         |
| exact filter    | API query parameter, SQL predicate, index search               |
| inexact filter  | partition selection, approximate search, server-side prefilter |
| limit           | page size / max rows / early stop                              |
| partition       | shard, region, tenant, key range, date range                   |
| ordering        | remote `ORDER BY` only if guaranteed stable                    |

### Agent rules

```text id="4023oy"
Remote API providers must be cancellation-aware.
Use bounded page sizes.
Respect DataFusion limit but do not over-claim final cardinality.
Map rate-limit errors into retryable/clear DataFusionError.
Use TaskContext / RuntimeEnv resources when applicable.
Avoid one HTTP call per row.
Batch rows into Arrow arrays before yielding.
```

---

## 18.19 Non-file source patterns

### SQL database federation

```text id="5q9me7"
filter pushdown:
  exact for SQL-translatable predicates

projection pushdown:
  SELECT only requested columns + filter columns

limit pushdown:
  LIMIT/OFFSET if exact filters or DB handles predicates

partitioning:
  key ranges / shards / partitioned SQL queries

execution:
  async DB client cursor -> batches
```

### Search/index provider

```text id="9v80tq"
filter pushdown:
  exact for indexed fields
  inexact for text/full-text/vector search candidate sets

projection pushdown:
  stored fields only

limit pushdown:
  top-k candidate cap, but preserve residual filter semantics

execution:
  query index -> candidate docs -> convert to Arrow
```

### SaaS REST provider

```text id="iqaz55"
filter pushdown:
  exact only for API-supported query parameters

projection pushdown:
  sparse fieldsets if API supports them

limit pushdown:
  page size and max pages

partitioning:
  endpoint partition, account, region, date ranges

execution:
  async paginated requests -> batches
```

### Message/streaming source

```text id="lw9aex"
provider:
  StreamTable or custom unbounded TableProvider

boundedness:
  Unbounded if stream never naturally ends

partitioning:
  topic partitions

execution:
  consumer stream -> RecordBatchStream
```

DataFusion’s catalog stream module describes `StreamProvider` as a generic interface for reading/writing streaming sources such as FIFO, WebSocket, Kafka, and similar sources. ([Docs.rs][6])

---

## 18.20 Pushdown correctness matrix

| Pushdown          | Correctness risk                          | Required tests                                      |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| projection        | wrong column order/type                   | all projection permutations; no projection          |
| exact filter      | false positives/negatives                 | compare provider output vs DataFusion filter output |
| inexact filter    | too few rows if combined with limit       | inexact + limit queries                             |
| limit             | final result too short                    | limit with filters/sorts/projections                |
| partition pruning | dropped partitions                        | partition filter boundary cases                     |
| ordering metadata | missing SortExec causes wrong top-N/order | `ORDER BY LIMIT` comparisons                        |
| statistics        | bad join/order planning                   | stats stale/wrong/unknown fallback                  |

## 18.21 EXPLAIN-driven validation

```sql id="kx9bbl"
EXPLAIN
SELECT *
FROM events
WHERE region = 'us-east-1'
  AND event_type = 'click';
```

Expected progression:

```text id="kg2ceb"
No pushdown:
  FilterExec: region = ... AND event_type = ...
    MyExec: partitions=50

Exact region pushdown:
  FilterExec: event_type = ...
    MyExec: partitions=5, filter=[region = ...]

Exact region + event_type pushdown:
  MyExec: partitions=5, filter=[region = ... AND event_type = ...]
```

The guide recommends `EXPLAIN` as the first diagnostic tool for custom providers because it shows whether DataFusion inserted `FilterExec`, `SortExec`, or `RepartitionExec` above the scan. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

Rust:

```rust id="dbem94"
let explain = ctx
    .sql(
        "EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM counting WHERE partition = 1 LIMIT 10",
    )
    .await?;

explain.show().await?;
```

## 18.22 Memory, cancellation, and resource management

### Rules

```text id="nyhlvz"
Use bounded channels for producer/consumer streams.
Stop background work when receiver drops.
Do not spawn untracked tasks that outlive the query.
Do not block Tokio worker threads.
Use dedicated blocking pool for blocking APIs.
Yield periodically in CPU-heavy stream code.
Use TaskContext runtime resources when available.
Avoid buffering full result sets.
```

The `ExecutionPlan` docs say `execute` returns a stream, any execution error is returned as an `Err` item, DataFusion execution should cancel additional work once an error occurs, and the returned stream must free allocated resources when dropped; it also warns that streams must not block the CPU indefinitely and should yield to the Tokio runtime regularly. ([Docs.rs][7])

---

## 18.23 Testing strategy

### Unit: schema and projection

```rust id="ldiqxb"
#[tokio::test]
async fn projection_schema_matches() -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let table = CountingTable::new(2, 10);

    let plan = table
        .scan(&session_state, Some(&vec![1]), &[], None)
        .await?;

    assert_eq!(plan.schema().fields()[0].name(), "value");
    Ok(())
}
```

### Integration: compare pushdown vs no pushdown

```text id="956y8t"
same table/provider data
  query A: provider pushdown enabled
  query B: provider pushdown disabled
  assert equal RecordBatches after sort
```

### Required tests

```text id="kp78z8"
[ ] schema() cheap and stable
[ ] scan() does not perform remote read
[ ] projection: all / subset / reordered columns
[ ] filters: exact / inexact / unsupported
[ ] limit with no filters
[ ] limit with exact filters
[ ] limit with inexact filters
[ ] partition count and partition IDs
[ ] empty partitions
[ ] remote API error becomes DataFusionError
[ ] stream cancellation stops background work
[ ] EXPLAIN plan shows expected pushdown
[ ] RecordBatch schemas match stream schemas
[ ] table registration + SQL query path works
```

---

## 18.24 Deployment advisory

### Remote APIs

```text id="mepg7z"
Cache schema/metadata.
Push projection into remote request.
Push only exact server-side filters as Exact.
Use Inexact for partition/stat/candidate pruning.
Batch remote pages into RecordBatches.
Respect rate limits.
Use bounded concurrency.
Implement timeout/retry/circuit-breaker policy.
```

### Databases

```text id="vp23we"
Translate pushdown filters to parameterized SQL.
Never concatenate untrusted literal SQL.
Use remote EXPLAIN or indexes for performance.
Partition by key ranges/shards for parallel scans.
Preserve DataFusion null and type semantics.
```

### Search/vector sources

```text id="4ahliw"
Treat vector/top-k retrieval as inexact unless final predicate semantics are guaranteed.
Return score columns explicitly.
Limit pushdown must not hide matches after residual filters.
```

### Object/non-file sources

```text id="vdwzty"
Use object-store registry if source is file-like.
Use TableProvider only when source is not representable as ListingTable/FileFormat.
```

---

## 18.25 Anti-pattern inventory

* Fetching data in `scan()`.
* Blocking on async work in `execute()`.
* Returning batches whose schema differs from stream schema.
* Claiming `Exact` filter pushdown for approximate remote predicates.
* Applying limit before inexact filters.
* Ignoring projection and returning full schema batches.
* Reporting natural ordering that is not guaranteed.
* Reporting one partition for a sharded/partitioned source.
* Spawning background tasks that continue after stream drop.
* Buffering all remote rows before yielding first batch.
* Performing one remote call per row.
* Hiding provider errors as empty result sets.
* Returning stale/wrong constraints.
* Advertising statistics as exact when approximate.
* Using direct `TableProvider` for file formats when `ListingTable` + `FileFormat` is enough.
* Failing to test with `EXPLAIN`.

---

## 18.26 Agent checklist

```text id="9yr5wl"
[ ] First decide if MemTable, StreamTable, ViewTable, or ListingTable is enough.
[ ] Implement full TableProvider only when complete custom source control is needed.
[ ] schema() returns Arc<Schema> cheaply.
[ ] table_type() returns correct table category.
[ ] scan() builds ExecutionPlan only; no heavy I/O.
[ ] projection maps to output schema and remote selected fields.
[ ] supports_filters_pushdown returns Exact/Inexact/Unsupported accurately.
[ ] scan() uses pushed filters only according to declared support.
[ ] limit pushdown is safe with exact/no filters; careful with inexact filters.
[ ] statistics() returns conservative cached stats or None.
[ ] constraints() returns None unless constraints are supported.
[ ] ExecutionPlan properties correctly describe partitioning/order/boundedness.
[ ] execute() constructs stream quickly.
[ ] stream polling performs I/O/computation and yields RecordBatches.
[ ] blocking work is offloaded and cancellation-aware.
[ ] custom provider is registered with SessionContext and query-tested.
[ ] EXPLAIN confirms pushdown, partitioning, and absence/presence of FilterExec/SortExec/RepartitionExec.
```
