# DataFusion Advanced — 38) Production deployment patterns in Rust

## 38.0 Production architecture mental model

```text
Rust application
  ├─ process-level resources
  │   ├─ Tokio runtime
  │   ├─ object-store clients / credentials
  │   ├─ memory pool
  │   ├─ spill/temp disk
  │   └─ observability/logging
  ├─ DataFusion engine boundary
  │   ├─ RuntimeEnv
  │   ├─ SessionConfig
  │   ├─ SessionState
  │   └─ SessionContext
  ├─ metadata boundary
  │   ├─ CatalogProvider
  │   ├─ SchemaProvider
  │   └─ TableProvider
  ├─ query boundary
  │   ├─ SQL endpoint
  │   ├─ DataFrame builder
  │   ├─ custom query compiler
  │   └─ plugin/UDF invocation
  └─ output boundary
      ├─ collect for bounded internal results
      ├─ execute_stream for services
      ├─ write_* for ETL
      └─ DataSink/custom writer
```

`SessionContext` is the primary high-level interface for executing DataFusion queries and maintains session/connection state; `SessionState` contains planning/execution state such as configuration, functions, and runtime environment; `RuntimeEnv` owns execution resources such as object stores, memory, disk, and cache managers. ([docs.rs][1])

---

## 38.1 Core production construction pattern

### Engine profile

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;

use datafusion::execution::{
    runtime_env::RuntimeEnvBuilder,
    session_state::SessionStateBuilder,
};
use datafusion::prelude::*;

pub struct EngineProfile {
    pub batch_size: usize,
    pub target_partitions: usize,
    pub memory_limit_bytes: usize,
    pub memory_fraction: f64,
    pub temp_dir: String,
    pub max_temp_dir_bytes: usize,
    pub timezone: String,
}

pub fn build_context(profile: &EngineProfile) -> datafusion::error::Result<SessionContext> {
    let config = SessionConfig::new()
        .with_batch_size(profile.batch_size)
        .with_target_partitions(profile.target_partitions)
        .set_str("datafusion.execution.time_zone", &profile.timezone)
        .set_bool("datafusion.execution.parquet.pruning", true)
        .set_bool("datafusion.execution.parquet.enable_page_index", true)
        .set_bool("datafusion.execution.parquet.bloom_filter_on_read", true)
        .set_bool("datafusion.optimizer.enable_dynamic_filter_pushdown", true)
        .set_str("datafusion.sql_parser.dialect", "generic");

    let runtime = RuntimeEnvBuilder::new()
        .with_memory_limit(profile.memory_limit_bytes, profile.memory_fraction)
        .with_temp_file_path(&profile.temp_dir)
        .with_max_temp_directory_size(profile.max_temp_dir_bytes)
        .build_arc()?;

    let state = SessionStateBuilder::new()
        .with_config(config)
        .with_runtime_env(runtime)
        .with_default_features()
        .build();

    Ok(SessionContext::from(state))
}
```

`SessionConfig` customizes a `SessionContext`, and DataFusion runtime configuration includes `datafusion.runtime.memory_limit`, `datafusion.runtime.temp_directory`, and cache/resource settings; programmatic construction should separate session/query settings from runtime resource settings. ([docs.rs][2])

### Safe SQL executor

```rust
use futures::StreamExt;
use datafusion::prelude::*;

pub async fn run_read_only_sql_streamed(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    sql: &str,
    mut sink: impl BatchSink,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let options = SQLOptions::new()
        .with_allow_ddl(false)
        .with_allow_dml(false)
        .with_allow_statements(false);

    let df = ctx.sql_with_options(sql, options).await?;

    let mut stream = df.execute_stream().await?;

    sink.write_schema(stream.schema()).await?;

    while let Some(batch) = stream.next().await {
        sink.write_batch(batch?).await?;
    }

    sink.finish().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```

`SessionContext::sql` and `sql_with_options` produce `DataFrame`s from SQL; `SQLOptions` controls which SQL statement classes are allowed, making it the critical boundary for read-only SQL endpoints. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

---

## 38.2 Shared vs per-request `SessionContext`

| Model                                                | Description                                | Best for                                           | Risks                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| process-global shared `SessionContext`               | one context reused for all requests        | static catalogs, internal services, CLI-style apps | session mutation, tenant leakage, DDL/SET side effects |
| per-request `SessionContext`                         | new context per request                    | public SQL endpoints, tenant isolation             | table registration overhead                            |
| per-tenant context pool                              | one or more contexts per tenant/profile    | SaaS analytics, credential isolation               | cache invalidation, lifecycle complexity               |
| shared `SessionState` template + per-request context | build context from immutable state/profile | controlled query services                          | must avoid mutable shared catalogs unless intended     |
| job-scoped context                                   | one context per batch/ETL job              | ETL/validation/feature generation                  | startup overhead acceptable                            |

Agent policy:

```text
Use shared context only when:
  users are trusted
  table registry is stable
  SQL SET/DDL/DML are disabled or controlled
  tenant/catalog visibility is identical

Use per-request/per-tenant context when:
  credentials differ
  table visibility differs
  memory/temp quotas differ
  user SQL can mutate session state
  lifecycle isolation matters
```

---

## 38.3 Table registration lifecycle

| Lifecycle                  | Registration strategy                                                |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| static built-in tables     | register during application startup                                  |
| tenant-specific tables     | register during tenant context construction                          |
| request-scoped temp tables | register into per-request context; drop with context                 |
| dynamic file query         | avoid direct path SQL in services; register governed external tables |
| plugin provider            | register provider at plugin load or tenant enablement                |
| ETL staging tables         | register per job; use temp dirs and explicit cleanup                 |
| catalog-backed production  | use custom `CatalogProvider` / `SchemaProvider`                      |

`SessionContext::register*` methods tell DataFusion how to read named data sources so SQL can refer to them as tables; custom `TableProvider`s can also be registered with `SessionContext` to make them queryable. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

Startup registration:

```rust
pub async fn register_static_tables(ctx: &SessionContext) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    ctx.register_parquet(
        "events",
        "s3://lake/events/",
        ParquetReadOptions::default(),
    )
    .await?;

    ctx.register_csv(
        "countries",
        "config/countries.csv",
        CsvReadOptions::new().has_header(true),
    )
    .await?;

    Ok(())
}
```

Custom provider registration:

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;
use datafusion::catalog::TableProvider;

pub fn register_provider(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    name: &str,
    provider: Arc<dyn TableProvider>,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    ctx.register_table(name, provider)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

---

## 38.4 Pattern A — embedded analytics inside a Rust service

```text
Service handlers
  → Rust request structs
  → DataFrame / Expr plans
  → execute_stream or bounded collect
  → API response
```

| Concern                    | Recommendation                                                                |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SessionContext` ownership | shared context or per-tenant context; no arbitrary user mutation              |
| per-request vs shared      | shared if catalog/function set is immutable; per-tenant if credentials differ |
| table lifecycle            | startup registration or custom catalog                                        |
| memory limits              | process/runtime-level `RuntimeEnv` memory limit                               |
| temp directory             | service-owned spill directory, quota-protected                                |
| concurrency                | app-level query semaphore + Tokio runtime                                     |
| security boundary          | callers provide structured filters, not raw SQL                               |
| SQL policy                 | no public SQL; internal SQL only                                              |
| observability              | query ID, plan hash, rows, elapsed, `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` in debug paths          |

### Handler style

```rust
use datafusion::prelude::*;

pub async fn customer_metrics(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    customer_id: i64,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<Vec<datafusion::arrow::record_batch::RecordBatch>> {
    ctx.table("orders")
        .await?
        .filter(col("customer_id").eq(lit(customer_id)))?
        .aggregate(
            vec![col("status")],
            vec![datafusion::functions_aggregate::expr_fn::sum(col("amount")).alias("total_amount")],
        )?
        .sort(vec![col("status").sort(true, true)])?
        .collect()
        .await
}
```

Agent rules:

```text
Prefer DataFrame/Expr over SQL string assembly.
Expose typed service parameters.
Use collect only for bounded internal result sets.
Stream large outputs.
Keep DDL/DML disabled because service code owns catalog lifecycle.
```

---

## 38.5 Pattern B — CLI tool using DataFusion

```text
main()
  → parse args
  → create SessionContext
  → register paths/tables
  → run SQL/DataFrame
  → print / write output
```

| Concern                    | Recommendation                                                      |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SessionContext` ownership | single job-scoped context                                           |
| per-request vs shared      | not relevant; one process invocation                                |
| table lifecycle            | command-line registration; direct paths acceptable for trusted user |
| memory limits              | CLI flags/env/config                                                |
| temp directory             | user-configurable                                                   |
| concurrency                | default target partitions; expose flag                              |
| security boundary          | local user trust boundary                                           |
| SQL policy                 | allow DDL/DML/SET if CLI is admin/debug tool                        |
| observability              | `--explain`, `--analyze`, verbose logs                              |

### Skeleton

```rust
use clap::Parser;
use datafusion::prelude::*;

#[derive(Parser)]
struct Args {
    #[arg(long)]
    sql: String,

    #[arg(long)]
    parquet: Vec<String>,

    #[arg(long, default_value_t = 8192)]
    batch_size: usize,
}

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let args = Args::parse();

    let config = SessionConfig::new().with_batch_size(args.batch_size);
    let ctx = SessionContext::new_with_config(config);

    for (idx, path) in args.parquet.iter().enumerate() {
        ctx.register_parquet(
            &format!("t{idx}"),
            path,
            ParquetReadOptions::default(),
        )
        .await?;
    }

    ctx.sql(&args.sql).await?.show().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```

Agent rules:

```text
CLI can be permissive because caller owns process.
Still redact credentials in logs.
Provide --memory-limit, --temp-dir, --target-partitions, --format.
Prefer command/file SQL for reproducibility.
```

---

## 38.6 Pattern C — REST/GraphQL service with SQL endpoint

```text
HTTP request
  → authenticate
  → authorize tables/functions
  → construct per-request or tenant context
  → sql_with_options(read_only)
  → logical-plan validation
  → execute_stream
  → encode Arrow/JSON/CSV response
```

| Concern                    | Recommendation                                                 |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SessionContext` ownership | per-request or per-tenant context                              |
| per-request vs shared      | per-request for untrusted SQL; per-tenant pool for performance |
| table lifecycle            | governed catalog only                                          |
| memory limits              | per-tenant/runtime class                                       |
| temp directory             | tenant/workload-isolated path                                  |
| concurrency                | semaphore per tenant + global admission control                |
| security boundary          | SQL text is untrusted input                                    |
| SQL policy                 | `allow_ddl=false`, `allow_dml=false`, `allow_statements=false` |
| observability              | query ID, SQL hash, auth subject, plan/metrics, error class    |

### Read-only SQL route

```rust
pub async fn sql_endpoint(
    tenant: Tenant,
    sql: String,
    registry: &TenantEngineRegistry,
    sink: impl BatchSink,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let ctx = registry.context_for(&tenant)?;

    let options = SQLOptions::new()
        .with_allow_ddl(false)
        .with_allow_dml(false)
        .with_allow_statements(false);

    let df = ctx.sql_with_options(&sql, options).await?;

    validate_logical_plan(df.logical_plan(), &tenant.policy)?;

    stream_response(df, sink).await
}
```

### Logical-plan policy hooks

```text
Reject:
  DDL / DML / SET / RESET
  direct path scans
  unauthorized tables
  unauthorized columns
  unauthorized functions
  unbounded CROSS JOIN
  too many joins/subqueries
  missing LIMIT for interactive endpoints
```

Agent rules:

```text
Never expose raw ctx.sql for public SQL.
Disable statements so users cannot change memory, dialect, timezone, or parser behavior.
Validate logical plans after SQL planning and before execution.
Stream results; do not collect arbitrary user output.
```

---

## 38.7 Pattern D — query service with tenant isolation

```text
TenantEngineRegistry
  tenant_id
    → SessionContext / RuntimeEnv / CatalogProvider / ObjectStoreRegistry
       → tenant tables
       → tenant memory quota
       → tenant temp dir
       → tenant UDF/function allowlist
```

| Concern                    | Recommendation                                                         |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SessionContext` ownership | tenant-scoped context or context pool                                  |
| per-request vs shared      | tenant shared context if immutable; per-request clone/build if mutable |
| table lifecycle            | tenant catalog/provider                                                |
| memory limits              | per-tenant `RuntimeEnv`                                                |
| temp directory             | per-tenant spill directory/quota                                       |
| concurrency                | per-tenant semaphore + global semaphore                                |
| security boundary          | catalog/object-store/function registry boundary                        |
| SQL policy                 | deny DDL/DML/SET for normal users; admin path separate                 |
| observability              | tenant ID, query ID, quota class, top memory consumers                 |

### Registry skeleton

```rust
use dashmap::DashMap;

pub struct TenantEngineRegistry {
    engines: DashMap<TenantId, Arc<TenantEngine>>,
}

pub struct TenantEngine {
    ctx: SessionContext,
    semaphore: tokio::sync::Semaphore,
}

impl TenantEngineRegistry {
    pub fn context_for(&self, tenant: &Tenant) -> datafusion::error::Result<SessionContext> {
        let engine = self.engines
            .get(&tenant.id)
            .ok_or_else(|| datafusion::error::DataFusionError::Plan(
                format!("tenant {} has no query engine", tenant.id)
            ))?;

        Ok(engine.ctx.clone())
    }
}
```

### Tenant runtime

```rust
pub fn build_tenant_context(tenant: &Tenant) -> datafusion::error::Result<SessionContext> {
    let runtime = RuntimeEnvBuilder::new()
        .with_memory_limit(tenant.memory_limit_bytes, 0.80)
        .with_temp_file_path(format!("/mnt/spill/tenant-{}", tenant.id))
        .with_max_temp_directory_size(tenant.max_temp_bytes)
        .build_arc()?;

    let config = SessionConfig::new()
        .with_target_partitions(tenant.target_partitions)
        .set_str("datafusion.execution.time_zone", "UTC");

    let state = SessionStateBuilder::new()
        .with_config(config)
        .with_runtime_env(runtime)
        .with_default_features()
        .build();

    let ctx = SessionContext::from(state);

    register_tenant_catalogs(&ctx, tenant)?;

    Ok(ctx)
}
```

Agent rules:

```text
Resource isolation requires RuntimeEnv isolation, not only SQL filters.
Credential isolation requires object-store registry isolation.
Metadata isolation requires catalog/schema filtering.
Do not share mutable default catalog across tenants unless access is identical.
```

---

## 38.8 Pattern E — batch ETL executable

```text
job config
  → job-scoped SessionContext
  → register raw sources
  → transform SQL/DataFrame
  → write Parquet/CSV/JSON/table
  → validate output
  → exit
```

| Concern                    | Recommendation                                                          |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SessionContext` ownership | job-scoped                                                              |
| per-request vs shared      | one context per job/run                                                 |
| table lifecycle            | register sources and staging tables per job                             |
| memory limits              | large but bounded                                                       |
| temp directory             | job-specific spill/staging directory                                    |
| concurrency                | batch-tuned target partitions                                           |
| security boundary          | job runner permissions; not public SQL                                  |
| SQL policy                 | allow DDL/DML/COPY for trusted ETL scripts                              |
| observability              | job ID, input/output rows, files written, EXPLAIN ANALYZE for slow jobs |

### Skeleton

```rust
use datafusion::dataframe::DataFrameWriteOptions;
use datafusion::prelude::*;

pub async fn run_etl(ctx: &SessionContext) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    ctx.register_parquet("raw_events", "s3://lake/raw/events/", ParquetReadOptions::default())
        .await?;

    let df = ctx.sql(
        "SELECT
           event_id,
           user_id,
           event_ts,
           event_date,
           region
         FROM raw_events
         WHERE event_id IS NOT NULL",
    ).await?;

    df.write_parquet(
        "s3://lake/curated/events/",
        DataFrameWriteOptions::new()
            .with_partition_by(vec!["event_date".to_string(), "region".to_string()]),
        None,
    )
    .await?;

    Ok(())
}
```

Agent rules:

```text
Use job-scoped temp directories.
Use staging output paths and atomic publish where possible.
Run validation queries after writes.
Capture row counts and file counts.
Allow write SQL only because ETL code is trusted.
```

---

## 38.9 Pattern F — data validation engine

```text
input dataset
  → DataFusion table
  → validation rules as SQL/DataFrame
  → violations table
  → pass/fail summary
```

| Concern                    | Recommendation                                              |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SessionContext` ownership | job/dataset-scoped                                          |
| per-request vs shared      | per validation run                                          |
| table lifecycle            | register dataset and reference tables                       |
| memory limits              | bounded; validation can be scan-heavy                       |
| temp directory             | validation-run spill dir                                    |
| concurrency                | target partitions based on input size                       |
| security boundary          | validation rule authors may be semi-trusted                 |
| SQL policy                 | no DDL/DML for rule SQL unless rule system needs temp views |
| observability              | rule ID, failed row count, sample violations, query metrics |

### Rule model

```rust
pub struct ValidationRule {
    pub id: String,
    pub sql: String, // returns violating rows
    pub max_examples: usize,
}

pub async fn run_rule(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    rule: &ValidationRule,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<ValidationResult> {
    let options = SQLOptions::new()
        .with_allow_ddl(false)
        .with_allow_dml(false)
        .with_allow_statements(false);

    let df = ctx.sql_with_options(&rule.sql, options).await?;

    validate_rule_plan(df.logical_plan())?;

    let violations = df.limit(0, Some(rule.max_examples))?.collect().await?;

    Ok(ValidationResult {
        rule_id: rule.id.clone(),
        example_batches: violations,
    })
}
```

Agent rules:

```text
Validation SQL should return bad rows, not good rows.
Always cap violation examples.
Run separate COUNT query or aggregate if full violation count is needed.
Store rule SQL, schema version, data snapshot, and config snapshot.
```

---

## 38.10 Pattern G — feature engineering engine

```text
raw feature sources
  → DataFusion transformations
  → point-in-time joins / windows / aggregations
  → feature table output
```

| Concern                    | Recommendation                                                            |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SessionContext` ownership | job-scoped or tenant/project-scoped                                       |
| per-request vs shared      | job-scoped for training batch; request-scoped for online feature previews |
| table lifecycle            | register feature sources/versioned snapshots                              |
| memory limits              | large; joins/windows/grouping heavy                                       |
| temp directory             | fast spill directory mandatory                                            |
| concurrency                | tune joins/aggregations; target partitions by workload                    |
| security boundary          | feature registry/catalog governance                                       |
| SQL policy                 | trusted feature definitions; review/validate plans                        |
| observability              | feature set ID, training window, row counts, join metrics                 |

### DataFrame-first pattern

```rust
pub async fn build_features(ctx: &SessionContext) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let events = ctx.table("events").await?;
    let users = ctx.table("users").await?;

    let features = events
        .join(
            users,
            datafusion::logical_expr::JoinType::Inner,
            &["user_id"],
            &["user_id"],
            None,
        )?
        .filter(col("event_ts").gt_eq(lit("2026-01-01")))?
        .aggregate(
            vec![col("user_id")],
            vec![
                datafusion::functions_aggregate::expr_fn::count(lit(1)).alias("event_count"),
                datafusion::functions_aggregate::expr_fn::max(col("event_ts")).alias("last_event_ts"),
            ],
        )?;

    features
        .write_parquet(
            "s3://feature-store/user_features/",
            datafusion::dataframe::DataFrameWriteOptions::new(),
            None,
        )
        .await?;

    Ok(())
}
```

Agent rules:

```text
Prefer DataFrame/Expr for generated feature definitions.
Use SQL for human-authored feature specs.
Require point-in-time correctness tests.
Test joins, nulls, late-arriving data, and deterministic ordering.
```

---

## 38.11 Pattern H — custom database/query layer

```text
client protocol
  → auth/session
  → catalog/schema/table metadata
  → SQL/DataFrame/logical-plan compiler
  → DataFusion optimizer/execution
  → Arrow/Flight/JSON result
```

| Concern                    | Recommendation                                                                 |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `SessionContext` ownership | connection/session-scoped or tenant-scoped                                     |
| per-request vs shared      | connection context if session state matters; request context for stateless API |
| table lifecycle            | custom catalog provider; DDL implementation policy                             |
| memory limits              | connection/tenant/workload class                                               |
| temp directory             | isolated by tenant/workload                                                    |
| concurrency                | scheduler/admission control                                                    |
| security boundary          | SQL authz, catalog authz, object-store authz                                   |
| SQL policy                 | product-specific; DDL/DML/admin paths separated                                |
| observability              | query ID, session ID, catalog version, plan/metrics, audit log                 |

### Database-layer boundary

```rust
pub async fn execute_query(
    session: &DbSession,
    sql: &str,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<QueryStream> {
    let options = session.sql_options();

    let df = session.ctx.sql_with_options(sql, options).await?;

    let plan = df.logical_plan();
    session.authorizer.validate(plan)?;

    let stream = df.execute_stream().await?;

    Ok(QueryStream::new(stream))
}
```

Agent rules:

```text
DataFusion is the execution engine, not the whole database contract.
You own:
  authentication
  authorization
  transaction semantics
  catalog durability
  DDL semantics
  audit logs
  quota/admission control
  client protocol
```

---

## 38.12 Pattern I — plugin architecture with UDFs/providers

```text
Plugin registry
  ├─ UDF plugins
  ├─ UDAF/UDWF plugins
  ├─ TableProvider plugins
  ├─ object-store plugins
  ├─ catalog plugins
  └─ optimizer/planner plugins
```

| Concern                    | Recommendation                                           |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SessionContext` ownership | rebuilt or extended during plugin activation             |
| per-request vs shared      | shared immutable registry; per-tenant enabled plugin set |
| table lifecycle            | provider plugins register into catalog/schema            |
| memory limits              | plugin operators use `TaskContext` reservations          |
| temp directory             | plugin operators must use runtime disk manager           |
| concurrency                | plugins must be Send + Sync and cancellation-safe        |
| security boundary          | plugins are trusted native code unless sandboxed         |
| SQL policy                 | function/table allowlist from plugin registry            |
| observability              | plugin name/version in metrics/errors/display            |

### Plugin traits

```rust
pub trait DataFusionPlugin: Send + Sync {
    fn name(&self) -> &'static str;
    fn version(&self) -> &'static str;

    fn register(
        &self,
        ctx: &SessionContext,
    ) -> datafusion::error::Result<()>;
}
```

### Registration

```rust
pub fn install_plugins(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    plugins: &[Arc<dyn DataFusionPlugin>],
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    for plugin in plugins {
        tracing::info!(
            plugin = plugin.name(),
            version = plugin.version(),
            "installing DataFusion plugin"
        );

        plugin.register(ctx)?;
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

### UDF plugin

```rust
pub struct TextFunctionsPlugin;

impl DataFusionPlugin for TextFunctionsPlugin {
    fn name(&self) -> &'static str { "text-functions" }
    fn version(&self) -> &'static str { "1.0.0" }

    fn register(&self, ctx: &SessionContext) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
        ctx.register_udf(make_slugify_udf());
        Ok(())
    }
}
```

### Provider plugin

```rust
pub struct CrmProviderPlugin {
    provider: Arc<dyn datafusion::catalog::TableProvider>,
}

impl DataFusionPlugin for CrmProviderPlugin {
    fn name(&self) -> &'static str { "crm-provider" }
    fn version(&self) -> &'static str { "2.1.0" }

    fn register(&self, ctx: &SessionContext) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
        ctx.register_table("crm_accounts", self.provider.clone())?;
        Ok(())
    }
}
```

Agent rules:

```text
Native plugins are trusted code.
Require plugin version metadata.
Require UDF signatures/docs.
Require provider schemas/pushdown contracts.
Require custom operators to expose metrics/display/memory reservations.
Do not dynamically load arbitrary untrusted native plugins without sandboxing.
```

---

## 38.13 Ownership models by pattern

| Pattern              | Context ownership               | Runtime ownership       | Catalog ownership         |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------- |
| embedded analytics   | app singleton or tenant         | app/tenant              | app/static                |
| CLI                  | process/job                     | process/job             | process/job               |
| REST SQL endpoint    | request or tenant               | tenant/workload         | governed catalog          |
| tenant query service | tenant engine                   | tenant                  | tenant catalog/provider   |
| batch ETL            | job                             | job                     | job + shared metastore    |
| validation engine    | validation run                  | run/job                 | dataset/reference catalog |
| feature engineering  | job/project                     | job/project             | feature registry          |
| custom DB layer      | session/tenant                  | session/tenant/workload | durable custom catalog    |
| plugin architecture  | app/tenant with plugin registry | app/tenant              | plugin/catalog registry   |

---

## 38.14 Concurrency model

```text
Tokio runtime:
  drives async execution and stream polling

DataFusion partitions:
  controlled by datafusion.execution.target_partitions

Application concurrency:
  number of simultaneous queries/jobs

Resource concurrency:
  memory pool
  temp disk
  object-store request concurrency
  remote API limits
```

`DataFusion` executes with partitioned physical plans and runtime resources; target partitions, batch size, memory limit, object-store writer buffers, metadata fetch concurrency, and runtime memory/temp settings are configured through `SessionConfig`, `ConfigOptions`, SQL `SET`, or `RuntimeEnvBuilder`. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

### Query semaphore

```rust
pub struct QueryGate {
    global: tokio::sync::Semaphore,
}

impl QueryGate {
    pub async fn run<T>(
        &self,
        fut: impl std::future::Future<Output = datafusion::error::Result<T>>,
    ) -> datafusion::error::Result<T> {
        let _permit = self.global
            .acquire()
            .await
            .map_err(|e| datafusion::error::DataFusionError::External(Box::new(e)))?;

        fut.await
    }
}
```

Agent rules:

```text
DataFusion target_partitions is not request admission control.
Always add app-level concurrency limits for services.
Separate:
  intra-query parallelism = target_partitions
  inter-query parallelism = service admission control
```

---

## 38.15 Security boundary matrix

| Boundary                | Required control                                        |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| SQL text                | `SQLOptions`, parser config, plan validation            |
| table access            | catalog/table allowlist                                 |
| column access           | projection/masking views or provider policy             |
| row access              | mandatory filters/views/provider-level enforcement      |
| file/object-store paths | no direct URL table access; registered governed sources |
| credentials             | object-store registry; no SQL secrets                   |
| functions               | UDF/function allowlist                                  |
| DDL/DML                 | admin-only path                                         |
| resource use            | memory/temp/query timeout/concurrency                   |
| output                  | row/byte caps, streaming cancellation                   |

Agent policy:

```text
User SQL is untrusted code.
Catalogs are security boundaries only if you implement authorization.
DataFusion does not replace application-level authn/authz.
```

---

## 38.16 SQL allow/deny policy profiles

### Internal service, no SQL endpoint

```text
allow SQL:
  no public SQL
  only static SQL strings or DataFrame plans

policy:
  no runtime SQL allowlist needed
  code review controls queries
```

### Read-only public SQL

```rust
let options = SQLOptions::new()
    .with_allow_ddl(false)
    .with_allow_dml(false)
    .with_allow_statements(false);
```

```text
allow:
  SELECT
  WITH
  read-only scalar/aggregate/window functions

deny:
  CREATE / DROP / ALTER
  INSERT / COPY writes
  SET / RESET
  direct file paths
  dangerous/high-cost functions if policy requires
```

### Admin SQL

```text
allow:
  DDL
  DML
  SET
  CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE

require:
  authenticated admin
  audit log
  path allowlist
  credential policy
  approval/rollback strategy
```

### ETL SQL

```text
allow:
  CREATE TEMP/STAGING TABLE
  INSERT/COPY/write paths
  SET workload config

require:
  job identity
  staging directories
  output validation
  cleanup policy
```

---

## 38.17 Observability hooks

| Hook                 | Implementation                                            |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| query ID             | generate before planning; attach to logs/errors           |
| SQL hash             | hash raw SQL; avoid logging full SQL by default           |
| plan snapshot        | `EXPLAIN FORMAT INDENT` in debug/profile mode             |
| runtime metrics      | `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` / `ExecutionPlan::metrics`              |
| streaming counters   | rows, batches, bytes written                              |
| error classification | map `DataFusionError::find_root()` to service error class |
| plugin metadata      | plugin name/version in logs                               |
| resource metrics     | memory pool reserved, spill dir usage, top consumers      |
| object-store metrics | request count, bytes, latency, errors                     |
| audit events         | DDL/DML/admin SQL/table access                            |

`ExecutionPlan::metrics()` returns a snapshot of operator metrics where available, and DataFusion’s metrics module provides counters, timers, pruning metrics, spill metrics, and metric builders for custom execution nodes. ([docs.rs][5])

### Query wrapper

```rust
pub async fn observed_query(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    query_id: &str,
    sql: &str,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<usize> {
    let started = std::time::Instant::now();

    tracing::info!(query_id, sql_hash = %hash_sql(sql), "planning query");

    let df = ctx.sql(sql)
        .await
        .map_err(|e| e.context(format!("planning query_id={query_id}")))?;

    tracing::info!(query_id, "executing query");

    let mut rows = 0usize;
    let mut stream = df.execute_stream().await?;

    while let Some(batch) = futures::StreamExt::next(&mut stream).await {
        rows += batch?.num_rows();
    }

    tracing::info!(
        query_id,
        rows,
        elapsed_ms = started.elapsed().as_millis(),
        "query complete"
    );

    Ok(rows)
}
```

---

## 38.18 Pattern-specific configuration defaults

| Pattern             |             `target_partitions` |    `batch_size` | memory        | temp dir             |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------: | --------------: | ------------- | -------------------- |
| embedded analytics  | core count or workload-specific |            8192 | process-level | shared service spill |
| CLI                 |                       user flag |       user flag | optional      | user flag            |
| REST SQL            |           tenant/workload class |       4096–8192 | mandatory     | tenant/workload      |
| tenant service      |                    tenant class |    tenant class | per tenant    | per tenant           |
| batch ETL           |                  high/CPU-count |           8192+ | mandatory     | job/workload         |
| validation          |                input-size based |       4096–8192 | bounded       | run-specific         |
| feature engineering |                  workload tuned |       4096–8192 | high + spill  | job/project          |
| custom DB           |          session/workload class | service default | mandatory     | tenant/session       |
| plugins             |                     host policy |     host policy | host-enforced | host-enforced        |

Agent rule:

```text
Resource profile is part of application architecture.
Do not let arbitrary user SQL choose resource profile unless admin-approved.
```

---

## 38.19 Deployment hardening checklist

```text
Engine construction:
  [ ] explicit SessionConfig
  [ ] explicit RuntimeEnv
  [ ] memory_limit set
  [ ] temp_directory set
  [ ] max_temp_directory_size set
  [ ] time_zone set
  [ ] parser dialect set
  [ ] object stores registered outside SQL

Catalog:
  [ ] no unintended default shared tables
  [ ] tenant/catalog isolation
  [ ] static registrations audited
  [ ] custom providers tested
  [ ] direct path access disabled unless trusted

SQL:
  [ ] SQLOptions selected per endpoint
  [ ] logical-plan authorization
  [ ] function allowlist
  [ ] DDL/DML/admin split
  [ ] SET/RESET policy

Runtime:
  [ ] query concurrency semaphore
  [ ] timeout/cancellation
  [ ] result row/byte caps
  [ ] stream output path
  [ ] spill disk monitoring

Observability:
  [ ] query ID
  [ ] SQL hash
  [ ] plan capture toggle
  [ ] EXPLAIN ANALYZE/profiling path
  [ ] metrics/logging
  [ ] error classification
  [ ] audit log
```

---

## 38.20 Anti-pattern inventory

* One global mutable `SessionContext` shared by all tenants and public SQL users.
* Public SQL endpoint using `ctx.sql(...)` with default allow-all SQL behavior.
* Allowing `SET` in untrusted SQL, letting users change memory, dialect, timezone, or optimizer behavior.
* Allowing arbitrary `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE LOCATION`.
* Using direct quoted path SQL as a public API.
* No memory limit in a shared service.
* Spill directory on a slow/full/unmonitored filesystem.
* `collect()` for arbitrary service responses.
* No query concurrency limit.
* Registering tenant tables in a shared default schema.
* Logging raw SQL with inline secrets.
* Plugins without versioning, metrics, or memory accounting.
* Custom providers claiming exact pushdown without tests.
* Treating DataFusion as complete database auth/transaction/catalog system without implementing those layers.

---

## 38.21 Agent checklist

```text
[ ] Select deployment pattern.
[ ] Decide SessionContext ownership: process / job / request / tenant / session.
[ ] Decide RuntimeEnv ownership: process / tenant / workload / job.
[ ] Decide catalog ownership and persistence.
[ ] Define table registration lifecycle.
[ ] Set memory limit, temp directory, max temp directory size.
[ ] Set concurrency limits outside DataFusion.
[ ] Define SQL allow/deny policy with SQLOptions.
[ ] Validate logical plans for authorization and complexity.
[ ] Disable direct path access for public services.
[ ] Register object stores and credentials outside SQL.
[ ] Use execute_stream for large/service outputs.
[ ] Use collect only for bounded internal results.
[ ] Add observability: query ID, SQL hash, plan, metrics, errors.
[ ] Add audit logging for DDL/DML/admin actions.
[ ] Test custom providers/UDFs/plugins under the same resource profile as production.
```

# DataFusion Advanced — 39) Security and governance

## 39.0 Threat model

```text
Untrusted user input
  ├─ SQL text
  ├─ table names / column names
  ├─ file/object-store locations
  ├─ function calls
  ├─ result-size requests
  ├─ config mutation via SET
  └─ resource-heavy query shapes

Security controls
  ├─ SQL class gating: SQLOptions
  ├─ catalog isolation
  ├─ object-store registry isolation
  ├─ logical-plan validation
  ├─ function allowlist
  ├─ memory/temp/query time limits
  ├─ result limits
  ├─ audit logs
  └─ tenant-scoped RuntimeEnv / SessionContext
```

DataFusion is an embeddable query engine, not a complete database security boundary by itself. `SessionContext` is the main interface for registering sources and executing SQL, and by default `SessionContext::sql` can execute DDL and DML such as `CREATE TABLE`, `CREATE VIEW`, and `INSERT INTO`; use `sql_with_options` and application-level plan validation for untrusted SQL. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 39.1 Security responsibility split

| Layer             | DataFusion provides                       | Application must provide                    |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| SQL parsing       | parser, dialect settings, recursion limit | query admission, authn/authz                |
| SQL class gating  | `SQLOptions` for DDL/DML/statements       | endpoint policy                             |
| catalog           | catalog/schema/table traits               | tenant isolation, ACLs, metadata governance |
| file/object store | URL/object-store integration              | credential isolation, path allowlists       |
| execution         | memory pool, temp dir, runtime configs    | quotas, timeouts, concurrency limits        |
| functions         | UDF registration                          | function allowlist, side-effect policy      |
| output            | `RecordBatch` streams                     | row/byte caps, serialization policy         |
| diagnostics       | errors, metrics, plans                    | audit logging, redaction, incident response |

Agent rule:

```text
Treat DataFusion as a query engine inside your trusted boundary.
Do not treat it as a full DBMS authorization, credential, sandbox, or tenant-isolation system unless you implement those layers.
```

---

## 39.2 Accepting user SQL safely

### Read-only SQL executor

```rust
use datafusion::prelude::*;
use futures::StreamExt;

pub async fn execute_read_only_sql(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    sql: &str,
    tenant_policy: &TenantPolicy,
    mut sink: impl BatchSink,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let options = SQLOptions::new()
        .with_allow_ddl(false)
        .with_allow_dml(false)
        .with_allow_statements(false);

    let df = ctx.sql_with_options(sql, options).await?;

    validate_logical_plan(df.logical_plan(), tenant_policy)?;

    let mut stream = df.execute_stream().await?;

    sink.write_schema(stream.schema()).await?;

    while let Some(batch) = stream.next().await {
        let batch = batch?;
        sink.write_batch(batch).await?;
    }

    sink.finish().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```

`SQLOptions` describes which SQL statements are allowed. DDL defaults to allowed, DML defaults to allowed, and statement/config SQL such as `SET` also defaults to allowed; therefore public SQL endpoints should explicitly disable all three unless those capabilities are product features. `SessionContext::sql_with_options` validates SQL against these options before returning a `DataFrame`. ([Docs.rs][2])

### Policy matrix

| Endpoint type            |           DDL |           DML | statements / `SET` |      direct paths | recommended                          |
| ------------------------ | ------------: | ------------: | -----------------: | ----------------: | ------------------------------------ |
| public analytics SELECT  |          deny |          deny |               deny |              deny | `sql_with_options` + plan validation |
| internal analyst console |    controlled |    controlled |         controlled |        controlled | authenticated/admin-only             |
| ETL runner               | allow trusted | allow trusted |      allow trusted | allow allowlisted | job identity + audit                 |
| admin migration tool     |         allow |         allow |              allow | allow allowlisted | strong auth + change log             |
| feature validation rule  |          deny |          deny |               deny |              deny | rule result caps                     |

### Agent rules

```text
Never expose ctx.sql(user_sql) directly in public services.
Use sql_with_options for all user SQL.
Disable DDL, DML, and statements for read-only endpoints.
Validate the logical plan after parsing and before execution.
Stream results; avoid collect() for arbitrary user queries.
```

---

## 39.3 DDL / DML governance

### Deny mutation

```rust
let options = SQLOptions::new()
    .with_allow_ddl(false)
    .with_allow_dml(false)
    .with_allow_statements(false);
```

### Admin-only mutation

```rust
pub async fn execute_admin_sql(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    principal: &Principal,
    sql: &str,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    require_admin(principal)?;

    let options = SQLOptions::new()
        .with_allow_ddl(true)
        .with_allow_dml(true)
        .with_allow_statements(true);

    let df = ctx.sql_with_options(sql, options).await?;

    audit_admin_sql(principal, sql, df.logical_plan())?;

    df.collect().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```

### DML / DDL risk inventory

```text
DDL risks:
  CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE over arbitrary path
  CREATE TABLE AS SELECT memory consumption
  CREATE VIEW exposing forbidden columns
  DROP TABLE / DROP VIEW removing shared metadata
  CREATE FUNCTION if function factory is enabled

DML/write risks:
  INSERT INTO target table/provider
  COPY query TO file/object-store path
  overwrite/append semantics by provider
  data exfiltration through writable sinks

Statements risks:
  SET memory limits / parser dialect / optimizer flags
  SET timezone / recursion limit
  RESET important service defaults
```

Agent rule:

```text
DDL/DML/admin SQL must have a separate authenticated path, audit trail, path policy, and rollback strategy.
```

---

## 39.4 Preventing arbitrary file reads

### Dangerous in public services

```rust
let ctx = SessionContext::new()
    .enable_url_table(); // do not enable for untrusted SQL
```

`enable_url_table()` permits local file access from SQL such as `SELECT * FROM 'my_file.parquet'`; the docs explicitly call it security-sensitive and say it should only be enabled for systems that intend to permit direct filesystem access from SQL. ([Docs.rs][1])

### Preferred public-service pattern

```rust
pub async fn build_tenant_context(
    tenant: &Tenant,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<SessionContext> {
    let ctx = SessionContext::new();

    // Register only governed, tenant-authorized tables.
    ctx.register_parquet(
        "events",
        tenant.allowed_events_path(),
        ParquetReadOptions::default(),
    )
    .await?;

    Ok(ctx)
}
```

### Direct-path denial policy

```text
Reject:
  SELECT * FROM 'file.parquet'
  SELECT * FROM 's3://arbitrary-bucket/path/'
  CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE ... LOCATION '/etc/passwd'
  CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE ... LOCATION 's3://unknown/path/'
```

### Agent rules

```text
Public SQL:
  do not enable_url_table()
  do not expose arbitrary CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE
  do not allow user-provided LOCATION unless allowlisted
  use registered tables and governed catalogs only

Trusted CLI / local admin:
  direct path SQL can be useful
```

---

## 39.5 Object-store credential handling

### Avoid inline secrets in SQL

```sql
-- Avoid in shared logs / public services
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE private_data
STORED AS PARQUET
OPTIONS (
  'aws.access_key_id' '...',
  'aws.secret_access_key' '...'
)
LOCATION 's3://bucket/path/';
```

DataFusion CLI docs support explicit S3 credentials in `OPTIONS`, environment/AWS SDK configuration, unsigned public-bucket access, GCS service-account options, and OSS/COS endpoint options; they also document S3 credential precedence as explicit `OPTIONS`, then standard AWS config/environment, then unsigned requests if no credentials are specified. ([datafusion.apache.org][3])

### Preferred Rust object-store registry pattern

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;
use datafusion::prelude::*;
use object_store::aws::AmazonS3Builder;
use url::Url;

pub fn register_tenant_s3(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    tenant: &Tenant,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let store = AmazonS3Builder::new()
        .with_region(tenant.aws_region())
        .with_bucket_name(tenant.bucket())
        .with_access_key_id(tenant.access_key_id())
        .with_secret_access_key(tenant.secret_access_key())
        .build()
        .map_err(|e| datafusion::error::DataFusionError::External(Box::new(e)))?;

    ctx.register_object_store(
        &Url::parse(&format!("s3://{}", tenant.bucket()))?,
        Arc::new(store),
    );

    Ok(())
}
```

### Credential policy

```text
Preferred:
  object-store registry
  runtime/env provider chain
  secret manager
  instance/workload identity
  short-lived credentials
  per-tenant RuntimeEnv/object-store registry

Avoid:
  SQL OPTIONS with long-lived secrets
  logging CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE statements containing credentials
  shared object-store registry across tenants with different credentials
  public endpoints that allow user-specified object-store OPTIONS
```

### Unsigned public bucket policy

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE public_dataset
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://public-bucket/path/'
OPTIONS ('aws.skip_signature' 'true');
```

Use unsigned requests only as an explicit public-data policy; do not rely on unsigned fallback for private-data access. The docs also show public S3 access via `aws.SKIP_SIGNATURE` / `aws.skip_signature`. ([datafusion.apache.org][3])

---

## 39.6 Query timeouts and cancellation

DataFusion execution is stream-based, so dropping the stream cancels remaining work. Application code should enforce wall-clock deadlines around planning and stream polling.

### Timeout wrapper

```rust
use futures::StreamExt;
use tokio::time::{timeout, Duration};

pub async fn execute_with_timeout(
    df: DataFrame,
    query_timeout: Duration,
    mut sink: impl BatchSink,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let mut stream = timeout(query_timeout, df.execute_stream())
        .await
        .map_err(|_| datafusion::error::DataFusionError::Execution(
            "query timed out before execution started".to_string(),
        ))??;

    sink.write_schema(stream.schema()).await?;

    loop {
        let next = timeout(query_timeout, stream.next())
            .await
            .map_err(|_| datafusion::error::DataFusionError::Execution(
                "query timed out while producing results".to_string(),
            ))?;

        match next {
            Some(Ok(batch)) => sink.write_batch(batch).await?,
            Some(Err(e)) => return Err(e),
            None => break,
        }
    }

    sink.finish().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```

### Timeout policy

```text
planning_timeout:
  protects parser/planner/optimizer/catalog latency

execution_timeout:
  protects long-running query runtime

idle_batch_timeout:
  protects stream stalls / remote object-store hangs

absolute_deadline:
  protects total request duration

client_disconnect:
  drop stream immediately
```

Agent rules:

```text
DataFusion does not replace application request deadlines.
Wrap planning and streaming in tokio timeouts.
Drop streams on timeout or client disconnect.
Use query_id in timeout errors and audit logs.
```

---

## 39.7 Memory limits and spill governance

### Rust runtime profile

```rust
use datafusion::execution::{
    runtime_env::RuntimeEnvBuilder,
    session_state::SessionStateBuilder,
};
use datafusion::prelude::*;

pub fn secure_runtime_context(
    tenant: &Tenant,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<SessionContext> {
    let runtime = RuntimeEnvBuilder::new()
        .with_memory_limit(tenant.memory_limit_bytes(), 0.80)
        .with_temp_file_path(tenant.spill_dir())
        .with_max_temp_directory_size(tenant.max_spill_bytes())
        .build_arc()?;

    let config = SessionConfig::new()
        .with_target_partitions(tenant.target_partitions())
        .with_batch_size(tenant.batch_size());

    let state = SessionStateBuilder::new()
        .with_runtime_env(runtime)
        .with_config(config)
        .with_default_features()
        .build();

    Ok(SessionContext::from(state))
}
```

Runtime settings can be set through SQL as well: `datafusion.runtime.memory_limit` controls maximum query execution memory, `datafusion.runtime.temp_directory` controls the temp directory path, and `datafusion.runtime.max_temp_directory_size` defaults to `100G` and controls the temporary-file directory size. ([datafusion.apache.org][4])

### Important shared-runtime caveat

```text
If every request creates a new independent RuntimeEnv:
  memory and disk limits are not shared across requests.

If all contexts share one RuntimeEnv:
  memory and disk limits are process-wide for those contexts.
```

The `SessionContext` docs state that by default each new context creates a new `RuntimeEnv`, so resource limits are not enforced across queries run in different contexts unless those contexts share the same `RuntimeEnv`. ([Docs.rs][1])

### Agent rules

```text
Set memory limits for shared services.
Set spill temp directory and max temp size.
Use tenant/workload RuntimeEnv isolation when quotas differ.
Use app-level query concurrency limits; memory pools are not admission control.
Monitor process RSS and spill disk externally too.
```

---

## 39.8 Result limits

### SQL-level cap wrapper

```rust
pub async fn execute_capped_sql(
    ctx: &SessionContext,
    sql: &str,
    max_rows: usize,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<Vec<RecordBatch>> {
    let options = SQLOptions::new()
        .with_allow_ddl(false)
        .with_allow_dml(false)
        .with_allow_statements(false);

    let df = ctx.sql_with_options(sql, options).await?;

    validate_logical_plan(df.logical_plan(), &Policy::default())?;

    df.limit(0, Some(max_rows))?
        .collect()
        .await
}
```

### Streaming cap

```rust
pub async fn stream_with_row_cap(
    mut stream: datafusion::execution::SendableRecordBatchStream,
    max_rows: usize,
    mut sink: impl BatchSink,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let mut emitted = 0usize;

    sink.write_schema(stream.schema()).await?;

    while let Some(batch) = futures::StreamExt::next(&mut stream).await {
        let batch = batch?;
        emitted += batch.num_rows();

        if emitted > max_rows {
            return Err(datafusion::error::DataFusionError::Execution(format!(
                "result row limit exceeded: max_rows={max_rows}"
            )));
        }

        sink.write_batch(batch).await?;
    }

    sink.finish().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```

### Policy table

| Endpoint          | Result policy                        |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| interactive UI    | mandatory `LIMIT` or server-side cap |
| API export        | async job + byte/row quota           |
| internal ETL      | job-level output expectations        |
| validation engine | cap examples, separate count         |
| public SQL        | hard row/byte/time cap               |

Agent rules:

```text
LIMIT in user SQL is not enough.
Also enforce server-side row/byte caps.
Do not collect arbitrary user outputs.
Prefer execute_stream for large results.
```

---

## 39.9 SQL parser dialect and recursion limits

### Secure parser profile

```rust
let config = SessionConfig::new()
    .set_str("datafusion.sql_parser.dialect", "generic")
    .set_usize("datafusion.sql_parser.recursion_limit", 50)
    .set_bool("datafusion.sql_parser.enable_ident_normalization", true);
```

```sql
SET datafusion.sql_parser.recursion_limit = '50';
```

DataFusion exposes parser settings including `datafusion.sql_parser.recursion_limit`, which defaults to `50` and limits recursion depth for complex SQL queries. The config docs also document parser settings such as dialect, identifier normalization, string-type mapping, and subquery sort elimination. ([datafusion.apache.org][4])

### Parser governance

```text
dialect:
  choose one product dialect
  document it
  do not let public users SET dialect unless intended

recursion_limit:
  keep bounded
  increase only for trusted workloads
  treat excessive nesting as query complexity risk

identifier normalization:
  keep default unless case-sensitive semantics are product requirement
```

Agent rules:

```text
Parser settings are part of security posture.
Disable SET for public SQL so users cannot alter parser behavior.
Validate query complexity after parsing as well as relying on recursion limits.
```

---

## 39.10 Function allowlists

### Function policy model

```rust
use datafusion::logical_expr::LogicalPlan;

pub struct FunctionPolicy {
    pub allowed_functions: std::collections::HashSet<String>,
    pub denied_functions: std::collections::HashSet<String>,
}

pub fn validate_functions(
    plan: &LogicalPlan,
    policy: &FunctionPolicy,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let mut violations = Vec::new();

    plan.apply_expressions(|expr| {
        for function_name in collect_function_names(expr) {
            let name = function_name.to_ascii_lowercase();

            if policy.denied_functions.contains(&name)
                || !policy.allowed_functions.contains(&name)
            {
                violations.push(name);
            }
        }

        Ok(datafusion::common::tree_node::TreeNodeRecursion::Continue)
    })?;

    if !violations.is_empty() {
        violations.sort();
        violations.dedup();

        return Err(datafusion::error::DataFusionError::Plan(format!(
            "function(s) not allowed: {}",
            violations.join(", ")
        )));
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

### High-risk function classes

```text
volatile:
  random, uuid, current time if deterministic output required

expensive:
  regex over huge text
  levenshtein over huge text
  vector distance cross joins
  unnest over large arrays

diagnostic:
  version
  metadata/cache introspection functions
  arrow_metadata / arrow_field if metadata exposure matters

external:
  async UDFs
  network-calling UDFs
  secret-reading UDFs
```

### Agent rules

```text
Function registration is not the same as function authorization.
Public SQL should have an allowlist.
Do not register side-effecting UDFs into contexts used by untrusted SQL.
Mark volatility correctly.
Audit UDF names, aliases, docs, and argument behavior.
```

---

## 39.11 Catalog isolation

### One catalog/schema per tenant

```text
CatalogProviderList
  ├─ tenant_a_catalog
  │   └─ public
  │       ├─ events
  │       └─ users
  └─ tenant_b_catalog
      └─ public
          ├─ events
          └─ users
```

### Tenant context construction

```rust
pub fn build_tenant_catalog_context(
    tenant: &Tenant,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<SessionContext> {
    let ctx = secure_runtime_context(tenant)?;

    let catalog = build_tenant_catalog(tenant)?;
    ctx.register_catalog(tenant.catalog_name(), catalog);

    Ok(ctx)
}
```

### Catalog policy

```text
CatalogProvider:
  controls schemas visible to tenant

SchemaProvider:
  controls table names visible to tenant

TableProvider:
  controls schema, scan, filter/projection pushdown, and data access

information_schema:
  expose only if metadata visibility is allowed
```

The DataFusion configuration docs show default catalog/schema settings and that `information_schema` is disabled by default; exposing information schema can reveal table, column, routine, and configuration metadata, so it should be governed per tenant/security policy. ([datafusion.apache.org][4])

### Agent rules

```text
Do not share one mutable MemoryCatalogProvider across tenants.
Do not rely on table-name prefixes as your only isolation layer.
Use separate catalogs/contexts/runtime envs when credentials or visibility differ.
Filter or disable information_schema for untrusted users.
```

---

## 39.12 Multi-tenant contexts

### Isolation levels

| Level                              | Isolation strength | Use                                     |
| ---------------------------------- | -----------------: | --------------------------------------- |
| shared context, row filters        |               weak | trusted internal users only             |
| shared runtime, per-tenant catalog |             medium | same credentials/resource pool          |
| per-tenant context, shared runtime |             medium | metadata isolation, shared memory limit |
| per-tenant context + runtime       |             strong | separate credentials and quotas         |
| separate process/container         |          strongest | high-risk tenants or strict isolation   |

### Strong tenant builder

```rust
pub async fn build_isolated_tenant_engine(
    tenant: &Tenant,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<SessionContext> {
    let ctx = secure_runtime_context(tenant)?;

    register_tenant_object_stores(&ctx, tenant)?;
    register_tenant_catalogs(&ctx, tenant).await?;
    register_tenant_udfs(&ctx, tenant)?;

    Ok(ctx)
}
```

### Agent rules

```text
If credentials differ:
  use separate object-store registries / RuntimeEnv.

If quotas differ:
  use separate RuntimeEnv.

If metadata visibility differs:
  use separate catalog/schema providers.

If user SQL is untrusted:
  use sql_with_options + plan validation per request.
```

---

## 39.13 Logical-plan authorization

### Validator skeleton

```rust
use datafusion::logical_expr::LogicalPlan;
use datafusion::common::tree_node::{TreeNodeRecursion, TreeNode};

pub fn validate_logical_plan(
    plan: &LogicalPlan,
    policy: &TenantPolicy,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    validate_tables(plan, policy)?;
    validate_columns(plan, policy)?;
    validate_functions(plan, policy)?;
    validate_complexity(plan, policy)?;
    validate_no_direct_paths(plan, policy)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

### Table validation

```rust
pub fn validate_tables(
    plan: &LogicalPlan,
    policy: &TenantPolicy,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let mut denied = Vec::new();

    plan.apply(|node| {
        if let LogicalPlan::TableScan(scan) = node {
            let table = scan.table_name.to_string();

            if !policy.allowed_tables.contains(&table) {
                denied.push(table);
            }
        }

        Ok(TreeNodeRecursion::Continue)
    })?;

    if !denied.is_empty() {
        denied.sort();
        denied.dedup();

        return Err(datafusion::error::DataFusionError::Plan(format!(
            "table access denied: {}",
            denied.join(", ")
        )));
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

### Complexity validation

```text
Reject or cap:
  too many joins
  cross joins
  nested lateral joins
  unbounded ORDER BY
  DISTINCT over wide data
  unbounded unnest
  too many subqueries / CTEs
  direct path scans
  disallowed functions
  missing LIMIT on interactive endpoint
```

Agent rules:

```text
SQLOptions prevents broad statement classes.
Plan validation enforces product-specific authz and complexity.
Run validation before execution.
Repeat validation after rewrites if your application injects/changes plans.
```

---

## 39.14 Row and column security

### Safer: view/provider-level masking

```sql
CREATE VIEW tenant_events AS
SELECT
  event_id,
  event_ts,
  user_id,
  -- omit secret columns
  region
FROM raw_events
WHERE tenant_id = 'tenant_a';
```

### Application-injected filter

```rust
pub fn apply_tenant_filter(
    df: DataFrame,
    tenant: &Tenant,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<DataFrame> {
    df.filter(col("tenant_id").eq(lit(tenant.id.as_str())))
}
```

### Provider-level enforcement

```text
Custom TableProvider::scan:
  always inject tenant predicate
  reject projection of forbidden columns
  expose schema without forbidden columns
  never rely only on user-supplied WHERE clause
```

Agent rules:

```text
Do not trust user SQL to include tenant filters.
Apply row security below or after parsing:
  custom views
  custom TableProvider
  DataFrame-enforced predicates
  logical-plan rewrite

Column security:
  hide columns in schema if possible.
  mask through views/providers if necessary.
```

---

## 39.15 Observability and audit

### Audit event schema

```rust
#[derive(Debug, serde::Serialize)]
pub struct QueryAuditEvent {
    pub query_id: String,
    pub principal_id: String,
    pub tenant_id: String,
    pub sql_hash: String,
    pub statement_class: String,
    pub tables: Vec<String>,
    pub functions: Vec<String>,
    pub started_at_ms: i64,
    pub elapsed_ms: Option<u128>,
    pub rows_returned: Option<usize>,
    pub error_class: Option<String>,
}
```

### Logging rules

```text
Log:
  query_id
  principal
  tenant
  SQL hash
  statement class
  authorized tables
  denied reason
  row count
  elapsed time
  error class
  memory/resource class

Do not log:
  inline credentials
  object-store tokens
  raw access keys
  full raw SQL by default
  sensitive row values
```

### Agent rules

```text
Every denied query should produce an audit event.
Every admin DDL/DML should produce an audit event.
Every resource exhaustion should include query_id and quota class.
Every public error should be sanitized and actionable.
```

---

## 39.16 Secure endpoint template

```rust
pub async fn secure_sql_endpoint(
    registry: &TenantEngineRegistry,
    request: SqlRequest,
    mut sink: impl BatchSink,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let principal = authenticate(&request)?;
    let tenant = authorize_tenant(&principal, &request.tenant_id)?;

    let ctx = registry.context_for(&tenant)?;

    let options = SQLOptions::new()
        .with_allow_ddl(false)
        .with_allow_dml(false)
        .with_allow_statements(false);

    let query_id = new_query_id();

    let df = ctx
        .sql_with_options(&request.sql, options)
        .await
        .map_err(|e| e.context(format!("planning query_id={query_id}")))?;

    validate_logical_plan(df.logical_plan(), &tenant.policy)
        .map_err(|e| e.context(format!("authorizing query_id={query_id}")))?;

    let df = enforce_result_limit(df, tenant.policy.max_rows)?;

    execute_with_timeout(
        df,
        tenant.policy.query_timeout,
        &mut sink,
    )
    .await
    .map_err(|e| e.context(format!("executing query_id={query_id}")))?;

    Ok(())
}
```

---

```text
SQL class gating:
  [ ] CREATE TABLE denied

  [ ] INSERT denied

  [ ] SET denied

File/object access:

Function policy:

Resources:

Plan validation:

  [ ] unbounded ORDER BY policy

  [ ] missing LIMIT policy
```

Context/runtime:
  [ ] per-tenant or shared RuntimeEnv chosen intentionally

---

## 39.19 Anti-pattern inventory

* Public SQL endpoint calling `ctx.sql(user_sql)` directly.
* Relying on `SQLOptions` alone for tenant/table/column authorization.
* Enabling `enable_url_table()` in a multi-tenant or public service.
* Allowing arbitrary `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE ... LOCATION`.
* Logging raw SQL containing cloud credentials.
* Putting long-lived S3/GCS credentials in SQL `OPTIONS`.
* Sharing one default in-memory catalog across tenants.
* Letting users run `SET datafusion.runtime.memory_limit`.
* Assuming memory limits apply across contexts that do not share `RuntimeEnv`.
* Enforcing row security only by asking users to include `WHERE tenant_id = ...`.
* Registering side-effecting UDFs in public SQL contexts.
* Returning raw internal errors/backtraces to users.
* Using `collect()` for unbounded public query results.
* No query timeout.
* No result limit.
* No audit log for denied queries.

---

## 39.20 Agent checklist

```text
[ ] Treat user SQL as untrusted input.
[ ] Use sql_with_options, not raw ctx.sql, for user SQL.
[ ] Disable DDL, DML, and statements for read-only endpoints.
[ ] Do not enable_url_table for public SQL.
[ ] Register only governed tables/catalogs.
[ ] Register object stores/credentials outside SQL.
[ ] Use per-tenant contexts/runtimes where credentials or quotas differ.
[ ] Validate logical plan for tables, columns, functions, and complexity.
[ ] Enforce row/column policy below user SQL.
[ ] Set parser dialect and recursion limit.
[ ] Use function allowlists.
[ ] Set memory limits, temp directories, and spill quotas.
[ ] Add query timeout and cancellation.
[ ] Add result row/byte limits.
[ ] Add concurrency/admission control.
[ ] Redact SQL/options in logs.
[ ] Audit every denied query and admin mutation.
[ ] Test security controls as first-class integration tests.
```
