# DataFusion Advanced — 40A) DataFusion 55 source-verified capability reconciliation

## 40A.0 Purpose and precedence

This chapter is the **version-sensitive precedence layer** for the rest of the reference. It was verified against the Apache DataFusion `55.0.0` source tag after comparing the broader reference with the specialized schema, planning, and calculation manuals.

```text
Precedence for deployable Rust code:
  1. Exact 55.0.0 tagged Rust source / version-pinned docs.rs signatures
  2. This 40A reconciliation chapter
  3. Detailed domain chapters in this document
  4. Historical notes explaining when a capability first appeared
```

A statement labeled “introduced in DataFusion 54” is historical provenance, not an instruction to use a 54-era signature.

## 40A.1 Session/planner contract in 55

DataFusion 55 moves planner-facing contracts toward `datafusion-session` and reduces dependence on the concrete `SessionState` type.

```rust
#[async_trait]
pub trait QueryPlanner: Any + Debug {
    async fn create_physical_plan(
        &self,
        logical_plan: &LogicalPlan,
        session: &dyn Session,
    ) -> Result<Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>>;
}

#[async_trait]
pub trait PhysicalPlanner: Send + Sync {
    async fn create_physical_plan(
        &self,
        logical_plan: &LogicalPlan,
        session: &dyn Session,
    ) -> Result<Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>>;

    fn create_physical_expr(
        &self,
        expr: &Expr,
        input_dfschema: &DFSchema,
        session: &dyn Session,
        planning_ctx: &PhysicalPlanningContext,
    ) -> Result<Arc<dyn PhysicalExpr>>;
}
```

`ExtensionPlanner::plan_extension` and `plan_table_scan` likewise receive both `&dyn Session` and `&PhysicalPlanningContext`. Extension planners must forward the context to `PhysicalPlanner::create_physical_expr` whenever they lower node-owned expressions.

## 40A.2 `PhysicalPlanningContext`: scalar subqueries and lambda scope

DataFusion 55 removes `subquery_indexes`, `subquery_results`, and `lambda_variable_qualifier` from `ExecutionProps`. Their subtree-scoped responsibilities now live in `PhysicalPlanningContext`:

```text
PhysicalPlanningContext
  ├─ indexes: Subquery -> SubqueryIndex
  ├─ results: ScalarSubqueryResults
  └─ lambda_variable_qualifier: name -> TableReference
```

This split matters because a physical planner recursively plans different subtrees with different scalar-subquery/lambda scope while sharing query-wide `ExecutionProps` such as query start time and alias generation.

Low-level physical-expression construction outside planner-owned lowering uses an empty context:

```rust
let physical = datafusion_physical_expr::create_physical_expr(
    &expr,
    &df_schema,
    &execution_props,
    &PhysicalPlanningContext::default(),
)?;
```

If such an expression actually contains an uncorrelated scalar subquery, an empty context is insufficient; normal planner-owned lowering supplies the populated context.

## 40A.3 `ExecutionPlan` expression traversal and child replacement

### Required `apply_expressions`

Every custom `ExecutionPlan` in 55 must expose the root physical expressions it owns and uses at execution time:

```rust
fn apply_expressions(
    &self,
    f: &mut dyn FnMut(&Arc<dyn PhysicalExpr>) -> Result<TreeNodeRecursion>,
) -> Result<TreeNodeRecursion> {
    apply_expression_roots([&self.predicate], f)
}
```

A node with no owned expressions returns `Ok(TreeNodeRecursion::Continue)`. Do **not** visit expressions merely because they appear in cached output ordering/equivalence metadata; expose expressions the node actually evaluates or dynamically updates.

### Preferred `replace_children`

DataFusion 55 prefers:

```rust
fn replace_children(
    self: Arc<Self>,
    children: Vec<Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>>,
    options: ReplaceChildrenOptions,
) -> Result<Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>>;
```

`with_new_children` remains required by the 55 trait but is deprecated. Implement it as a compatibility shim that delegates to `replace_children` with recomputation semantics. New optimizer code should use helpers such as `replace_children_if_necessary` / `replace_children` rather than encoding assumptions that rewritten children have identical properties.

### Richer distribution requirements

`required_input_distribution` is deprecated in 55 in favor of `input_distribution_requirements()`, whose `InputDistributionRequirements` can express richer policies such as co-partitioning requirements. Custom nodes that only need the old simple distribution vector can rely on the compatibility default, but new distribution-sensitive nodes should implement the richer contract.

## 40A.4 Bottom-up statistics: `StatisticsContext`, `ChildStats`, `StatisticsArgs`

This is the canonical statistics propagation model for new custom physical plans in 55:

```text
StatisticsContext::compute(plan, StatisticsArgs)
  -> plan.child_stats_requests(partition)
  -> recursively resolve requested child statistics
  -> plan.statistics_from_inputs(input_stats, args)
  -> memoize result for this walk
```

Core types:

```rust
pub struct StatisticsArgs {
    // None = overall plan statistics; Some(i) = partition i
    partition: Option<usize>,
}

pub enum ChildStats {
    At(Option<usize>),
    Skip,
}
```

Critical default: **`child_stats_requests` skips every child**. Therefore, a node that reads `input_stats` in `statistics_from_inputs` must also explicitly request those children.

```rust
fn child_stats_requests(&self, partition: Option<usize>) -> Vec<ChildStats> {
    vec![ChildStats::At(partition)]
}

fn statistics_from_inputs(
    &self,
    input_stats: &[Arc<Statistics>],
    args: &StatisticsArgs,
) -> Result<Arc<Statistics>> {
    let child = Arc::clone(&input_stats[0]);
    // transform child according to this operator's semantics
    Ok(child)
}
```

Use `ChildStats::At(None)` when an operator needs a child's whole-plan statistics even while computing a particular output partition—for example a coalescing/partition-merging operator or a broadcast build side. Use `ChildStats::Skip` when child statistics are irrelevant.

`StatisticsContext` memoizes by plan-node identity plus partition during one synchronous walk. If reusing a context after rewriting a plan tree, call `reset_cache()`.

The deprecated `partition_statistics` remains a compatibility fallback. The delegation is one-way: the default `statistics_from_inputs` can call the deprecated method, but callers of the deprecated method do not automatically reach a custom `statistics_from_inputs` implementation. New callers should use `StatisticsContext::compute`.

## 40A.5 Structured table scans and granular statistics requests

DataFusion 55 **retains** the required compatibility method:

```rust
async fn scan(
    &self,
    state: &dyn Session,
    projection: Option<&Vec<usize>>,
    filters: &[Expr],
    limit: Option<usize>,
) -> Result<Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>>;
```

and adds the structured path:

```text
TableProvider::scan_with_args(state, ScanArgs)
  -> ScanResult
```

`ScanArgs` carries:

```text
filters: Option<&[Expr]>
projection: Option<&[usize]>
limit: Option<usize>
statistics_requests: &[StatisticsRequest]
```

The default `scan_with_args` converts the slice projection to the legacy vector form and delegates to `scan`. Providers that need future structured scan options or granular statistics requests should override `scan_with_args`.

### `StatisticsRequest` flow

```text
custom optimizer rule
  -> annotates TableScan.statistics_requests
  -> physical planning
  -> ScanArgs.statistics_requests()
  -> custom TableProvider cheaply answers what it already knows
```

This is intentionally a **request**, not an instruction to perform expensive metadata I/O. If a provider cannot answer a requested statistic cheaply from cached/catalog metadata, it can ignore it.

## 40A.6 Range partitioning

DataFusion 55 adds first-class logical and physical range partitioning.

```text
logical Partitioning::Range
  -> create_physical_partitioning
  -> physical RangePartitioning
       ├─ LexOrdering
       └─ ordered SplitPoint values
  -> physical Partitioning::Range
```

Physical lowering requires non-empty ordering. Split-point scalar values are normalized to the ordering expression types only when the conversion is exactly representable; otherwise planning fails rather than silently moving the advertised boundary.

Use range partitioning when explicit ordered key ranges are semantically meaningful and compatible operators can preserve/exploit those ranges. DataFusion 55 also adds serialization/FFI support and support for co-partitioned range inner equi joins.

Agent rules:

```text
Do not treat range partitioning as "hash partitioning with sorted partitions".
Split points are ordered semantic boundaries.
Ordering expressions and split-point value types must agree exactly.
Test empty/duplicate/out-of-order boundaries as negative cases.
When joining range-partitioned inputs, verify compatible boundaries and key semantics.
```

## 40A.7 `EnsureRequirements`: distribution + sorting as one physical rule

DataFusion 55 replaces the old conceptual two-rule `EnforceDistribution` then `EnforceSorting` pipeline with the unified `EnsureRequirements` physical optimizer rule.

```text
EnsureRequirements
  Phase 1: top-down join-key reordering
  Phase 2: bottom-up, per child
           1. satisfy distribution
           2. satisfy ordering with distribution now known
  Phase 3: parallelize sorts / order-preserving variants /
           sort pushdown / partial-sort refinements
```

Why it matters: the old independent rules could invalidate one another—especially when sort pushdown changed partition-preservation choices. The combined rule is designed to be idempotent and makes distribution decisions before sorting decisions for each child.

This is the physical-planning context for `input_distribution_requirements`, `required_input_ordering`, `PlanProperties`, range/hash partitioning, repartitions, `SortExec`, and `SortPreservingMergeExec`.

## 40A.8 `MERGE INTO`: generic engine hooks vs table transaction semantics

DataFusion 55 adds generic logical/planner/provider support for `MERGE INTO`.

`WriteOp` is non-exhaustive and includes:

```rust
WriteOp::MergeInto(Box<MergeIntoOp>)
```

`MergeIntoOp` owns:

```text
on: Expr
clauses: Vec<MergeIntoClause>
```

A clause contains a clause kind, optional predicate, and action. Actions include update assignments, insert columns/values, and delete. `MergeIntoOp::exprs()` exposes the owned expressions in stable order, and `with_new_exprs` rebuilds the operation after rewrites.

Provider execution hook:

```rust
async fn merge_into(
    &self,
    state: &dyn Session,
    source: Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>,
    merge_schema: DFSchemaRef,
    on: Expr,
    clauses: Vec<MergeIntoClause>,
) -> Result<Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>>;
```

**Boundary rule:** DataFusion defines relational semantics and the provider hook. It does not make an arbitrary provider transactional. Delta Lake, databases, and other providers must implement their own concurrency, atomicity, conflict handling, file rewrites, commit protocol, and constraints.

## 40A.9 `file_row_index()`: source-dependent virtual row identity

DataFusion 55's `file_row_index()` is a nullary, volatile scalar UDF returning `Int64`, but its logical function is a **placeholder for a file-source-provided physical expression**.

```sql
SELECT file_row_index() FROM parquet_table;
```

Semantics:

```text
value = zero-based row offset within the source file
scope = one file
same index may occur in different files
```

Direct evaluation outside a supported file scan errors because there is no file context. Its expression placement moves it toward leaf nodes so file sources such as Parquet can rewrite it into virtual-column/read-plan machinery.

Use cases:
- row provenance inside a file;
- joining externally supplied row-selection/index metadata with scan output;
- diagnostics and deletion-vector/index workflows when paired with file identity.

Do **not** treat `file_row_index()` alone as a globally unique row identifier. Pair it with stable file identity when global uniqueness matters.

## 40A.10 UNNEST null/empty semantics in 55

DataFusion 55 represents list-UNNEST null behavior explicitly:

```rust
pub enum NullHandling {
    Drop,
    Preserve,               // default
    PreserveAndExpandEmpty,
}
```

| Mode | NULL list | empty list `[]` |
|---|---|---|
| `Drop` | 0 rows | 0 rows |
| `Preserve` | one NULL row | 0 rows |
| `PreserveAndExpandEmpty` | one NULL row | one NULL row |

`UnnestOptions::with_preserve_nulls(bool)` remains as a compatibility setter (`true -> Preserve`, `false -> Drop`). Use `with_null_handling(NullHandling::PreserveAndExpandEmpty)` when outer-like empty-list preservation is required.

This is a cardinality contract. Tests must distinguish a NULL list, an empty list, a list containing NULL, and a non-empty list.

## 40A.11 Scalar UDF strictness

DataFusion 55 exposes:

```rust
fn is_strict(&self) -> bool {
    false
}
```

on `ScalarUDFImpl`. A strict function **always returns NULL whenever any argument is NULL**. DataFusion can use this declaration when reasoning about expression nullability and null-rejecting predicates, including outer-join simplification.

Only return `true` if the property holds for every supported signature and every argument position.

```text
strictness != immutability
strictness != determinism
strictness != "usually propagates nulls"
```

Required tests for a strict N-argument function:
- each argument NULL independently;
- multiple NULL arguments;
- scalar and array execution paths;
- all supported overloads/coercions;
- nested/dictionary inputs if supported.

False-positive strictness can make optimizer reasoning unsound. The conservative default is `false`.

## 40A.12 Dictionary-preserving typed coercion

DataFusion 55 typed `Coercion` can opt into dictionary encoding preservation. Without preservation, typed coercions generally materialize dictionary inputs to the coerced value type. With:

```rust
Coercion::new_exact(TypeSignatureClass::Native(logical_string()))
    .with_encoding_preservation(EncodingPreservation::dictionary())
```

an input `Dictionary(key_type, value_type)` can remain a dictionary whose values are coerced while retaining the key encoding. This changes the post-coercion type seen by the UDF implementation and can also change return-type inference when output types derive from input types.

Use dictionary preservation for low-cardinality transforms that can operate efficiently without materialization; explicitly test dictionary and plain-array paths for identical semantics.

## 40A.13 `GroupsAccumulator` contract in DataFusion 55

The vectorized all-groups interface is:

```rust
pub trait GroupsAccumulator: Send + Any {
    fn update_batch(
        &mut self,
        values: &[ArrayRef],
        group_indices: &[usize],
        opt_filter: Option<&BooleanArray>,
        total_num_groups: usize,
    ) -> Result<()>;

    fn evaluate(&mut self, emit_to: EmitTo) -> Result<ArrayRef>;
    fn state(&mut self, emit_to: EmitTo) -> Result<Vec<ArrayRef>>;

    // No opt_filter in 55: filtering already happened during partial update.
    fn merge_batch(
        &mut self,
        values: &[ArrayRef],
        group_indices: &[usize],
        total_num_groups: usize,
    ) -> Result<()>;

    // Required in 55.
    fn convert_to_state(
        &self,
        values: &[ArrayRef],
        opt_filter: Option<&BooleanArray>,
    ) -> Result<Vec<ArrayRef>>;

    fn size(&self) -> usize;
}
```

`convert_to_state` enables hash aggregation to bypass costly partial pre-aggregation when cardinality reduction is poor, converting each input row directly into intermediate state for the next phase. `supports_convert_to_state` no longer exists. FFI providers and consumers must be rebuilt together because the 55 FFI layout changed.

## 40A.14 Higher-order UDF authoring contract

Higher-order functions are not merely scalar UDFs with an `Expr` argument. `HigherOrderUDFImpl` has a dedicated multi-stage type/binding/evaluation contract:

```text
HigherOrderSignature
  -> distinguish Value vs Lambda positions
  -> coerce ordinary value arguments
  -> lambda_parameters(step, fields)
       -> Partial / Complete parameter Fields
  -> plan/type-check lambda bodies
  -> optional coerce_values_for_lambdas
  -> return_field_from_args
  -> physical LambdaArgument construction
  -> invoke_with_args(HigherOrderFunctionArgs)
```

Required authoring methods include `name`, `signature`, `lambda_parameters`, `return_field_from_args`, and `invoke_with_args`. `lambda_parameters_max_iterations` defaults to 256 to guard an implementation that never finishes multi-step parameter inference.

`LambdaArgument::evaluate` evaluates only parameters actually referenced by the lambda body and supports captured outer columns. For list transforms, the function is responsible for spreading one captured value per outer row to the flattened element-level evaluation batch before reassembling the output list offsets/null structure.

Lambda variable scope during physical lowering is now carried by `PhysicalPlanningContext`, while SQL/binder-time lambda parameter scope is tracked in `PlannerContext`.

## 40A.15 `PlannerContext`: binder scope is a first-class planning artifact

`PlannerContext` in DataFusion 55 tracks SQL-planning scope including:

```text
PREPARE parameter FieldRef types
CTE name -> LogicalPlan bindings
outer query schema stack for correlated subqueries
outer FROM schema for LATERAL planning
CREATE TABLE schema context
left-most set-expression schema
lambda parameter name -> FieldRef
```

This is query-planning scope—not application-global state. Clone behavior intentionally gives nested queries inherited CTEs while allowing private nested CTE definitions. Generated/custom SQL-planning code should preserve the context rather than manually reproducing CTE, correlation, parameter, set-operation, or lambda scope.

## 40A.16 Schema / constraints / functional-dependency / statistics contract

Treat the provider/planner metadata stack as one contract:

```text
Arrow Field / Schema
  -> physical names, types, nullability, metadata
DFSchema
  -> qualifiers + logical resolution + functional dependencies
TableProvider
  -> schema + constraints + defaults + statistics + pushdown + write hooks
LogicalPlan
  -> derived schema + relational semantics
ExecutionPlan / PlanProperties
  -> physical partitioning, ordering, boundedness, emission, equivalences
StatisticsContext
  -> bottom-up physical statistics propagation
```

Functional dependencies and constraints are only useful when true. False ordering/partitioning/FD declarations can permit invalid optimizer rewrites; unknown metadata is safer than fabricated precision.


## 40A.17 Physical-plan self-serialization hooks

DataFusion 55 begins moving physical-plan protobuf encoding closer to the plan types themselves. `ExecutionPlan` has the feature-gated hook:

```rust
#[cfg(feature = "proto")]
fn try_to_proto(
    &self,
    ctx: &ExecutionPlanEncodeCtx<'_>,
) -> Result<Option<PhysicalPlanNode>> {
    Ok(None)
}
```

`Ok(None)` means "this node does not self-serialize" and lets `datafusion-proto` fall back to its central downcast chain. `Ok(Some(node))` means the node fully encoded itself and fallback must not run. Only self-contained plans should override this; session-dependent reconstruction still belongs at the codec/session boundary.

Migration implication: custom serialization code should not assume every built-in node remains permanently encoded in one central match statement. Round-trip tests should validate both legacy fallback and self-serialization paths under the exact pinned version.

## 40A.18 Lambda serialization

DataFusion 55 adds native protobuf and Substrait support for higher-order/lambda expressions. A system that serializes logical plans must therefore treat `Expr::HigherOrderFunction`, `Expr::Lambda`, and `Expr::LambdaVariable` as serializable semantic nodes rather than flattening lambdas into strings.

Agent rule:

```text
Do not serialize lambda bodies as SQL text when native plan serialization is available.
Preserve parameter order, lambda-local identity, captures, function identity, and types.
Round-trip nested lambdas and captured outer columns.
```

## 40A.19 Dynamic-filter tracking

DataFusion 55 adds `DynamicFilterTracker` / `DynamicFilterTracking` for cheap detection of changes to dynamic physical filters. A `DynamicFilterPhysicalExpr` has stable logical identity but an inner expression that may update as a build side or Top-K threshold becomes known.

Important contracts:
- leaf/column children must be known up front even if the initial predicate is a placeholder;
- generation changes allow consumers to avoid expensive full-expression comparisons;
- derived expressions created through child remapping retain the same underlying dynamic-filter identity;
- plans holding mutable dynamic filters should review `ExecutionPlan::reset_state` so recursive/reused plans do not retain stale runtime state;
- dynamic filters may be used by Parquet row filtering / early stopping and join/Top-K optimization.

Do not use the deprecated `is_dynamic_physical_expr` helper as the primary detection API in new 55 code.

## 40A.20 Scan-time physical-expression adaptation and virtual-column rewriting

DataFusion's datasource/Parquet stack uses `datafusion-physical-expr-adapter` to reconcile table-level physical expressions with per-file physical schemas. This supports schema evolution and source-specific rewrites such as `file_row_index` projection rewriting.

```text
table-level predicate/projection
  -> physical expression adapter
  -> file-specific schema mapping
  -> virtual/source-dependent expression rewrite
  -> Parquet read projection / row filter
```

This is preferable to hand-rebuilding predicates for every file schema. Custom file/source implementations should first evaluate whether `PhysicalExprAdapterFactory` / the rewrite utilities cover the needed source-schema adaptation before inventing a second expression-rewrite subsystem.

## 40A.21 Nested group-key execution coverage

DataFusion 55 broadens grouped-aggregation support for nested/group-value representations. This improves the set of Arrow logical types that can participate efficiently as group keys rather than falling back to less-specialized paths.

For custom calculation design, distinguish:

```text
custom aggregate state (UDAF / GroupsAccumulator)
  from
built-in grouping-key representation (GroupValuesColumn / row-backed group values)
```

Do not create a custom UDAF merely because the **group key** is nested. First verify that the built-in grouping engine handles the key type and reserve UDAFs for custom aggregate state/semantics.

## 40A.22 Pluggable spill storage

DataFusion 55 replaces the assumption of one concrete temporary-file type with the `SpillFile` abstraction and custom temporary-file factories. `DiskManager::create_tmp_file` returns `Arc<dyn SpillFile>`; spilling code writes through the spill-file writer interface and can inspect the resulting size.

Value case:
- alternative local spill storage implementations;
- controlled/custom temp-file allocation;
- testing spill behavior without coupling operators to one concrete file type.

Do not bypass DataFusion's memory reservation and spill-management surfaces by writing untracked temporary files directly from a custom operator.

## 40A.23 Sort pushdown, Top-K, and Parquet early stopping

DataFusion 55 deepens physical sort pushdown and Parquet intra-file early stopping. For `ORDER BY ... LIMIT k`, the optimized path can combine:

```text
known source ordering / min-max statistics
  + Top-K threshold
  + dynamic filter updates
  + row-group/page/row pruning
  -> read likely winners first
  -> skip ranges that cannot beat threshold
  -> avoid or reduce sort/decoding/I/O work
```

This is plan- and layout-dependent. Agents should inspect optimized physical plans and `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` metrics, and benchmark on representative file ordering/statistics rather than hard-coding expectations about a particular operator tree.

## 40A.24 `ScanArgs`, statistics requests, virtual columns, and source rewrites as one source contract

The 55 source-planning model is increasingly structured:

```text
TableProvider metadata
  -> TableScan annotations
  -> ScanArgs
       projection
       filters
       limit
       statistics_requests
  -> source-specific physical plan
  -> physical expression adaptation
  -> source virtual columns / file-row index
  -> runtime pruning + streaming
```

For new custom sources, treat `scan_with_args` as the extensible integration surface while maintaining compatibility with required `scan`. Keep schema/projection mapping, statistics answering, predicate pushdown, and virtual-column generation under one provider/source authority so each contract has one implementation owner.

## 40A.25 `EnsureRequirements` / range partitioning / statistics / scans as one design fabric

The major 55 planning changes reinforce a common design principle:

```text
provider declares source facts
  -> planner binds schema/functions/scopes
  -> logical optimizer derives semantic plan
  -> physical planner lowers with explicit subtree context
  -> physical nodes expose expressions + properties + statistics dependencies
  -> EnsureRequirements jointly satisfies distribution and ordering
  -> runtime streams Arrow batches under memory/spill policy
```

When implementing an extension, participate in these contracts rather than reproducing optimizer/planner logic inside a custom node.


# DataFusion Advanced — 40) Best practices and anti-patterns

## 40.0 Practical rule map

```text
Best practice classes
  ├─ dependency/version hygiene
  ├─ query interface choice
  ├─ table/source registration
  ├─ file/object-store layout
  ├─ Parquet optimization
  ├─ runtime/resource safety
  ├─ optimizer/rewrite correctness
  ├─ testing and baselines
  ├─ UDF/provider/operator extension safety
  └─ security/governance
```

DataFusion’s top-level crate is the normal entry point for Rust applications: it exposes the high-level APIs and re-exports public dependency types such as Arrow and ObjectStore; the SQL user guide frames `SessionContext` as the high-level SQL entry point after registering data sources as tables. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## 40.1 Dependency and type hygiene

### Rule: use `datafusion::arrow` re-exports by default

```rust
use datafusion::arrow::{
    array::{ArrayRef, Int64Array, StringArray},
    datatypes::{DataType, Field, Schema},
    record_batch::RecordBatch,
};
```

Why:

```text
Arrow types are part of DataFusion's public API.
Rust type identity includes crate version.
Two different Arrow versions can produce incompatible RecordBatch/Array/DataType types.
```

The top-level DataFusion crate re-exports Arrow, ObjectStore, and feature-gated Parquet because these types are part of its public API surface; using those re-exports avoids accidental Arrow type mismatches. ([Docs.rs][1])

### Anti-pattern

```rust
// Risky if this `arrow` version differs from DataFusion's Arrow version.
use arrow::record_batch::RecordBatch;
```

### Direct dependency policy

```toml
[dependencies]
datafusion = "=55.0.0"

# Only add if necessary and match DataFusion's Arrow family.
arrow = "=59.2.0"
parquet = "=59.2.0"
```

### Agent checklist

```text
[ ] Prefer datafusion::arrow imports.
[ ] Prefer datafusion::prelude for normal app code.
[ ] Pin datafusion exactly in production.
[ ] If using datafusion-* subcrates directly, align all versions.
[ ] Run cargo tree -d after upgrades.
```

---

## 40.2 Query interface choice

### Rule: prefer DataFrame/Expr API for generated queries

```rust
use datafusion::prelude::*;

let df = ctx
    .table("orders")
    .await?
    .filter(
        col("customer_id")
            .eq(lit(customer_id))
            .and(col("amount").gt(lit(0.0))),
    )?
    .select(vec![
        col("order_id"),
        col("amount"),
        (col("amount") * lit(1.08)).alias("amount_with_tax"),
    ])?;
```

DataFrame methods such as `select` and `filter` accept logical `Expr` values, and the expression API is designed for fluent, programmatic expression construction. ([datafusion.apache.org][2])

### Rule: prefer SQL for user-facing query interfaces

```rust
let options = SQLOptions::new()
    .with_allow_ddl(false)
    .with_allow_dml(false)
    .with_allow_statements(false);

let df = ctx.sql_with_options(user_sql, options).await?;
```

DataFusion has a full SQL API via `SessionContext`; using SQL is appropriate when query text is the product interface, while lower-level options such as `sql_with_options` are needed for governed endpoints. ([datafusion.apache.org][3])

### Decision table

| Situation                        | Prefer                                     |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| programmatic service filters     | DataFrame + `Expr`                         |
| trusted internal query templates | SQL or DataFrame                           |
| human query authoring            | SQL                                        |
| public SQL endpoint              | SQL + `sql_with_options` + plan validation |
| custom query compiler            | `LogicalPlanBuilder`                       |
| custom runtime source            | `TableProvider`                            |

### Anti-patterns

```text
String-concatenating user literals into SQL.
Using SQL snippets where Expr builders are safer.
Using DataFrame API to emulate complex human-authored SQL when SQL is the product.
Using ctx.sql(user_sql) directly in public endpoints.
```

---

## 40.3 Table registration and schema stability

### Rule: register tables explicitly for stable schemas

```rust
ctx.register_parquet(
    "events",
    "s3://lake/events/",
    ParquetReadOptions::default(),
)
.await?;

let df = ctx.sql("SELECT event_id, event_ts FROM events").await?;
```

`SessionContext` supports creating DataFrames from sources, registering CSV/Parquet/custom data sources as named SQL tables, and executing SQL; explicit registration gives stable names and schema contracts for SQL and DataFrame paths. ([Docs.rs][4])

### Prefer

```text
register_parquet / register_csv / register_json / register_avro / register_arrow
custom TableProvider registration
custom CatalogProvider / SchemaProvider
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE only through trusted/admin paths
```

### Avoid in services

```sql
SELECT * FROM 's3://arbitrary/path/';
SELECT * FROM '/etc/passwd';
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE x STORED AS PARQUET LOCATION 's3://unknown/path/';
```

### Agent checklist

```text
[ ] Register governed tables by name.
[ ] Use stable aliases and schemas.
[ ] Avoid public direct-path SQL.
[ ] Use custom catalogs for tenant/workspace table governance.
[ ] Validate schemas after registration with DESCRIBE / df.schema().
```

---

## 40.4 File and object-store paths

### Rule: avoid wildcards; use directory roots

```sql
-- Preferred
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE t
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://bucket/table_root/';

-- Avoid
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE t
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://bucket/*.parquet';
```

DataFusion’s datasource docs state wildcards are not supported in file paths and recommend specifying directory roots so DataFusion reads all compatible files under the directory; the same docs show Hive-style partition discovery for paths such as `a=1/b=100/file.parquet`. ([datafusion.apache.org][5])

### Rule: use Hive-style partitions deliberately

```text
s3://lake/events/event_date=2026-05-22/region=us/part-000.parquet
s3://lake/events/event_date=2026-05-22/region=eu/part-001.parquet
```

```sql
SELECT COUNT(*)
FROM events
WHERE event_date = DATE '2026-05-22'
  AND region = 'us';
```

### Anti-patterns

```text
Wildcard paths.
Directory path intended but no trailing `/` where source treats it as file.
Millions of tiny files.
High-cardinality partition directories.
Mixed schemas in one directory table.
User-supplied arbitrary LOCATION in public SQL.
```

---

## 40.5 Parquet layout and statistics

### Rule: use Parquet for repeated analytics

```text
CSV / JSON:
  ingestion, interchange, debugging

Parquet:
  repeated analytics, lake tables, nested typed data, pruning, compression
```

### Rule: write statistics and partition for future reads

```sql
COPY (
  SELECT *
  FROM clean_events
)
TO 's3://lake/curated/events/'
STORED AS PARQUET
PARTITIONED BY (event_date, region)
OPTIONS (
  'compression' 'zstd(3)',
  'statistics_enabled' 'page',
  'max_row_group_size' '1048576',
  'bloom_filter_enabled::event_id' 'true'
);
```

Parquet tuning knobs include page index, row-group pruning, bloom-filter reads, filter pushdown, compression, row-group size, statistics, writer version, and parallel writer settings; the configuration docs describe these read/write controls and their memory/performance tradeoffs. ([datafusion.apache.org][6])

### Agent rules

```text
Use low/moderate-cardinality partition columns.
Write page statistics for selective scans.
Use bloom filters for high-value equality keys, not low-cardinality booleans.
Tune row group size with workload and memory constraints.
Use zstd for storage/I/O efficiency; snappy for broad compatibility.
```

---

## 40.6 Runtime resource safety

### Rule: set memory and temp directory limits in services

```rust
let runtime = RuntimeEnvBuilder::new()
    .with_memory_limit(8 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024, 0.80)
    .with_temp_file_path("/mnt/nvme/datafusion-spill")
    .with_max_temp_directory_size(200 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024)
    .build_arc()?;
```

The configuration docs expose runtime memory, temp-directory, and max-temp-directory settings; they also recommend smaller `target_partitions` and `batch_size` under tight memory because spilling reads batches back at the configured batch size and memory is divided among partitions. ([datafusion.apache.org][6])

### SQL equivalent

```sql
SET datafusion.runtime.memory_limit = '8G';
SET datafusion.runtime.temp_directory = '/mnt/nvme/datafusion-spill';
SET datafusion.runtime.max_temp_directory_size = '200G';
SET datafusion.execution.target_partitions = '4';
SET datafusion.execution.batch_size = '1024';
```

### Anti-patterns

```text
Unbounded memory pool in multi-tenant service.
No temp directory for spill-capable workloads.
Spill directory on slow/unmonitored filesystem.
High target_partitions under tight memory.
collect() for arbitrary public query results.
No query concurrency limit.
```

---

## 40.7 Tune `target_partitions` for workload size

### Small queries

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.target_partitions = '1';
```

For very small datasets, the configuration guide recommends `target_partitions = 1` to avoid repartitioning overhead. ([datafusion.apache.org][7])

### Large scans

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.target_partitions = '0'; -- CPU-derived default
```

### Memory-limited workloads

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.target_partitions = '4';
SET datafusion.execution.batch_size = '1024';
```

### Rule table

| Workload                     | `target_partitions` stance                               |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| tiny data / short query      | `1`                                                      |
| large local Parquet scan     | CPU/core-derived default or measured value               |
| cloud object-store scan      | enough to overlap I/O; avoid tiny task explosion         |
| memory-tight group/join/sort | lower partitions                                         |
| high concurrency service     | lower per-query partitions + app-level admission control |
| batch ETL                    | higher partitions if memory/disk allows                  |

### Anti-pattern

```text
Assuming more partitions always improves performance.
It can increase scheduling, repartition, memory fragmentation, and spill pressure.
```

---

## 40.8 Explainability and regression baselines

### Rule: add `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` baselines for important workloads

```sql
EXPLAIN FORMAT INDENT
SELECT ...;

EXPLAIN ANALYZE
SELECT ...;
```

`EXPLAIN` shows the logical and physical plans without running the query, while `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` executes it and includes runtime metrics collected by operators; DataFusion metrics expose where time is spent and how rows/bytes flow through the pipeline. ([datafusion.apache.org][8])

### Baseline inventory

```text
Correctness:
  result rows
  schema
  nullability
  deterministic order

Plan:
  DataSourceExec
  FilterExec residuals
  RepartitionExec count
  join algorithm
  SortExec / TopK
  AggregateExec partial/final

Metrics:
  elapsed_compute
  output_rows
  output_batches
  output_bytes
  spill bytes
  files/row groups pruned
```

### Agent rules

```text
Use EXPLAIN before tuning.
Use EXPLAIN ANALYZE before declaring a bottleneck.
Pin DataFusion version for exact plan snapshots.
Use semantic plan assertions where possible.
Compare result + plan + metrics, not timing alone.
```

---

## 40.9 Optimizer rewrites

### Rule: preserve expression names in optimizer rewrites

```rust
// Conceptual rewrite
// old output expression: 1 + 2
// simplified value:      3
// output name must remain compatible:
lit(3i64).alias("Int64(1) + Int64(2)");
```

DataFusion identifies columns using string names, so optimizer rewrites must preserve expression names; the optimizer guide explicitly says rewritten expressions should typically be aliased back to the original display name. ([datafusion.apache.org][9])

### Custom optimizer checklist

```text
[ ] Same results.
[ ] Same output schema.
[ ] Same output expression names.
[ ] Aliases preserved.
[ ] Volatile expressions not duplicated/reordered.
[ ] Transformed::no returned for no-op.
[ ] plan.check_invariants() passes.
```

### Anti-patterns

```text
Changing output field names during simplification.
Dropping aliases.
Matching functions only by string name when UDFs can override names.
Duplicating volatile/random/time expressions.
Returning "changed" when rule did nothing.
```

---

## 40.10 UDF extension safety

### Rule: test UDFs with Arrow nulls, empty arrays, and type coercion cases

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;
use datafusion::arrow::array::{ArrayRef, Int64Array};
use datafusion::logical_expr::ColumnarValue;

let input = ColumnarValue::Array(
    Arc::new(Int64Array::from(vec![Some(1), None, Some(3)])) as ArrayRef
);
```

DataFusion’s UDF guide covers scalar, window, aggregate, table, and async scalar UDFs; scalar UDFs are vectorized over Arrow arrays, and Arrow arrays can contain null values represented naturally from `Option<T>` values. ([datafusion.apache.org][10])

### Required UDF test matrix

```text
Scalar UDF:
  [ ] ColumnarValue::Array
  [ ] ColumnarValue::Scalar
  [ ] empty arrays
  [ ] null inputs
  [ ] all-null inputs
  [ ] wrong arity
  [ ] wrong datatype
  [ ] return type inference
  [ ] SQL invocation
  [ ] DataFrame invocation

UDAF:
  [ ] update_batch
  [ ] state
  [ ] merge_batch
  [ ] evaluate empty/all-null input

UDTF:
  [ ] bad argument count/type
  [ ] schema stability
  [ ] pushdown over returned provider
```

### Anti-patterns

```text
panic!/unwrap! in UDFs.
Ignoring ColumnarValue::Scalar.
Returning arrays with wrong length.
Wrong volatility.
Not testing null propagation.
Doing blocking network I/O in sync scalar UDFs.
```

---

## 40.11 SQL vs DataFrame anti-injection policy

### Safer generated filter

```rust
df.filter(
    col("customer_id").eq(lit(customer_id))
)?;
```

### Risky SQL concatenation

```rust
let sql = format!("SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id = {customer_id}");
```

### Better SQL endpoint boundary

```rust
let options = SQLOptions::new()
    .with_allow_ddl(false)
    .with_allow_dml(false)
    .with_allow_statements(false);

let df = ctx.sql_with_options(user_sql, options).await?;
validate_logical_plan(df.logical_plan(), &policy)?;
```

Agent rules:

```text
Generated application logic:
  DataFrame/Expr.

Human-authored SQL:
  SQL + sql_with_options + logical-plan validation.

Never:
  SQL-concatenate untrusted identifiers/literals.
  Expose direct path SQL to untrusted users.
```

---

## 40.12 Catalog and governance

### Rule: isolate tenants with catalogs/contexts/runtimes when visibility or credentials differ

```text
Tenant A:
  SessionContext
    RuntimeEnv A
    ObjectStoreRegistry A
    CatalogProvider A

Tenant B:
  SessionContext
    RuntimeEnv B
    ObjectStoreRegistry B
    CatalogProvider B
```

### Agent rules

```text
Shared context is acceptable only when:
  users are trusted
  catalogs are immutable
  all users have same visibility
  statements/DDL/DML are disabled or controlled

Per-tenant context/runtime is required when:
  credentials differ
  quotas differ
  table visibility differs
  function allowlists differ
```

### Anti-patterns

```text
One mutable MemoryCatalogProvider for all tenants.
Row security only by asking users to include WHERE tenant_id = ...
Information_schema exposed without metadata policy.
Object-store credentials embedded in SQL.
```

---

## 40.13 Result and execution safety

### Rule: stream large results

```rust
use futures::StreamExt;

let mut stream = df.execute_stream().await?;

while let Some(batch) = stream.next().await {
    let batch = batch?;
    sink.write_batch(batch).await?;
}
```

### Rule: collect only bounded results

```rust
let batches = df
    .limit(0, Some(1000))?
    .collect()
    .await?;
```

### Safety controls

```text
[ ] query timeout
[ ] row cap
[ ] byte cap
[ ] memory limit
[ ] spill directory quota
[ ] concurrency semaphore
[ ] cancellation on disconnect
```

### Anti-patterns

```text
collect() on arbitrary public SQL.
No LIMIT or server-side cap in interactive endpoints.
No timeout.
No admission control.
```

---

## 40.14 Object-store and remote-data practices

### Good

```text
s3://lake/events/event_date=2026-05-22/region=us/part-000.parquet
```

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE events
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://lake/events/';
```

### Bad

```text
s3://lake/events/*.parquet
s3://lake/events/user_id=<millions>/...
s3://lake/events/mixed_schema_files/
```

### Remote profile

```sql
SET datafusion.runtime.metadata_cache_limit = '512M';
SET datafusion.runtime.list_files_cache_limit = '128M';
SET datafusion.runtime.list_files_cache_ttl = '5m';
SET datafusion.execution.meta_fetch_concurrency = '32';
```

DataFusion’s CLI-specific cache functions document that listing table file lists are cached in `ListFilesCache`, and subsequent queries against the same table can reuse cached file-listing information instead of relisting files. ([datafusion.apache.org][11])

### Anti-patterns

```text
Treating cloud-object latency as a CPU problem.
No metadata/listing cache for stable remote prefixes.
Huge number of tiny objects.
High-cardinality partition directories.
Raw secrets in SQL OPTIONS.
```

---

## 40.15 Testing practices

### Rule: use exact vs unordered assertions intentionally

```rust
// Deterministic order required.
assert_batches_eq!(expected, &batches);

// Order-independent comparison.
assert_batches_sorted_eq!(expected, &batches);
```

### Rule: add `ORDER BY` for exact row-order tests

```sql
SELECT id, score
FROM scored
ORDER BY score DESC, id ASC
LIMIT 10;
```

### Rule: use typed assertions for floats/nested/nullability

```rust
let field = batch.schema().field_with_name("amount")?;
assert_eq!(field.data_type(), &DataType::Float64);
assert!(field.is_nullable());
```

### Anti-patterns

```text
Exact row-order assertions without ORDER BY.
Pretty-table equality for floats.
No schema/nullability checks.
Only testing success paths.
No SQLLogicTests for public SQL surfaces.
No EXPLAIN baseline for performance-critical queries.
```

---

## 40.16 Custom provider/operator practices

### Rule: choose the highest-level extension that works

```text
Need custom row-wise function:
  UDF

Need table-like data source:
  TableProvider

Need file-like source:
  FileFormat/FileSource/ListingTable path

Need custom relational semantics:
  LogicalPlan::Extension + physical planner

Need custom runtime algorithm:
  ExecutionPlan
```

### Custom `TableProvider` rules

```text
schema():
  cheap, stable, correct

scan():
  planning only; no heavy I/O

supports_filters_pushdown():
  Exact only if exact
  Inexact for pruning/candidate reduction
  Unsupported when not handled

RecordBatchStream:
  every batch matches schema
  stream cancellation safe
```

### Custom `ExecutionPlan` rules

```text
PlanProperties truthful.
DisplayAs implemented.
ExecutionPlan::metrics implemented.
MemoryReservation used for buffered state.
execute() returns stream quickly.
stream polling does the work.
```

### Anti-patterns

```text
Fetching remote data in TableProvider::scan.
Blocking Tokio worker threads in stream poll.
Claiming exact pushdown for approximate filters.
Reporting ordering/partitioning that is not guaranteed.
No metrics/display for production custom operators.
```

---

## 40.17 Configuration practices

### Service baseline

```rust
let config = SessionConfig::new()
    .with_batch_size(8192)
    .with_target_partitions(num_cpus::get())
    .set_str("datafusion.execution.time_zone", "UTC")
    .set_str("datafusion.sql_parser.dialect", "generic")
    .set_usize("datafusion.sql_parser.recursion_limit", 50);
```

The `SessionConfig` docs state it customizes `SessionContext` and accepts namespaced keys such as `datafusion.execution.batch_size` and other built-in `datafusion.*` options. ([Docs.rs][12])

### Rule table

| Setting             | Best practice                                       |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `time_zone`         | set explicitly, usually UTC                         |
| `target_partitions` | tune by workload                                    |
| `batch_size`        | default for throughput; lower under memory pressure |
| parser dialect      | set explicitly for product SQL                      |
| parser recursion    | keep bounded for public SQL                         |
| memory limit        | set in services                                     |
| temp dir            | set in services                                     |
| explain settings    | enable schema/statistics in debug profiles          |

### Anti-patterns

```text
Letting public users run SET.
Relying on default timezone.
Using one config profile for tiny interactive queries and batch ETL.
No SHOW ALL/config capture in regression baselines.
```

---

## 40.18 Security practices

### Rule: public SQL requires layered controls

```text
Layer 1:
  sql_with_options disables DDL/DML/statements

Layer 2:
  logical-plan validation checks tables, columns, functions, complexity

Layer 3:
  runtime limits: memory/temp/time/result/concurrency

Layer 4:
  catalog/object-store/function isolation

Layer 5:
  audit logs and sanitized errors
```

### Minimum public SQL endpoint

```rust
let options = SQLOptions::new()
    .with_allow_ddl(false)
    .with_allow_dml(false)
    .with_allow_statements(false);

let df = ctx.sql_with_options(user_sql, options).await?;
validate_logical_plan(df.logical_plan(), &tenant_policy)?;
```

### Anti-patterns

```text
Public ctx.sql(user_sql).
enable_url_table in public service.
DDL/DML allowed by default.
Function registry includes side-effecting UDFs.
No tenant-specific catalog/object-store isolation.
No row/byte/time cap.
```

---

## 40.19 Deployment practices

### CLI / local tool

```text
Allow:
  direct paths
  DDL/DML/SET
  rich EXPLAIN
  local configs

Require:
  version capture
  input/output paths explicit
```

### Public service

```text
Deny:
  direct paths
  DDL
  DML
  SET
  arbitrary LOCATION
  unapproved functions

Require:
  per-tenant policy
  memory/temp/time/result/concurrency caps
  streaming output
  audit
```

### Batch ETL

```text
Allow:
  trusted DDL/DML/COPY
  large memory/spill profile
  job-scoped staging paths

Require:
  output validation
  row/file counts
  staging + publish
  retry/idempotency policy
```

---

## 40.20 Final anti-pattern inventory

```text
Dependency:
  importing mismatched arrow crate types
  mixing datafusion-* versions

Query building:
  SQL string concatenation for untrusted values
  using SQL where Expr builders are safer
  using DataFrame API where user SQL is the product

Sources:
  arbitrary direct path SQL in public services
  object-store wildcards
  mixed schemas in table directory
  CSV/JSON as repeated analytics storage

Parquet:
  no stats/page index for selective workloads
  high-cardinality partitions
  many tiny files
  bloom filters on low-value columns

Runtime:
  no memory limit
  no spill directory
  no query timeout
  no result cap
  high partitions under tight memory
  collect() on unbounded results

Optimizer/extensions:
  changed expression names in rewrites
  unsafe volatile expression rewrites
  exact pushdown lies
  custom exec without metrics/display/memory accounting

Testing:
  no null tests
  no empty-array UDF tests
  no schema/nullability assertions
  exact row-order tests without ORDER BY
  no EXPLAIN ANALYZE baselines

Security:
  ctx.sql(user_sql) in public endpoint
  SET allowed to untrusted users
  raw credentials in SQL OPTIONS/logs
  shared tenant catalog/runtime with different visibility/credentials
```

---

## 40.21 Final agent checklist

```text
[ ] Use datafusion::arrow re-exports.
[ ] Pin DataFusion version in production.
[ ] Prefer DataFrame/Expr for generated plans.
[ ] Prefer SQL for user-facing query interfaces.
[ ] Use sql_with_options for user SQL.
[ ] Register tables explicitly.
[ ] Use governed catalogs for services.
[ ] Avoid public direct-path SQL.
[ ] Use directory roots, not wildcards.
[ ] Prefer Parquet for repeated analytics.
[ ] Write/read Parquet statistics deliberately.
[ ] Partition by bounded-cardinality, frequently filtered columns.
[ ] Tune target_partitions by workload.
[ ] Set memory limit, temp dir, and max temp dir in services.
[ ] Stream large outputs with execute_stream.
[ ] Use collect only for bounded results.
[ ] Add EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN ANALYZE baselines.
[ ] Preserve expression names in optimizer rewrites.
[ ] Test UDFs with nulls, empty arrays, scalars, arrays, wrong types, and type coercion.
[ ] Test custom providers for projection/filter/limit pushdown.
[ ] Add metrics/display/memory accounting to custom ExecutionPlan nodes.
[ ] Enforce timeouts, result limits, concurrency limits, and function allowlists.
[ ] Capture config/version/data layout in regression reports.
```

### SMARTREF Planning And Runtime Boundary

`smartref_planning` is the non-executing compiler for SQL, PlanSpecV2, logical
plan imports, and Delta write handoffs. `smartref_runtime` owns sessions,
runtime environment, provider registry, plan cache, streams, and handoff
execution. Boundary layers must call the compiler/runtime instead of invoking
DataFusion planning or execution APIs as independent authority.

# Part II — Integrated schema, planning, and calculation deep dives

## Integration policy

The following chapters incorporate the previously separate schema, planning, and calculation manuals into this single canonical reference. They retain their deeper lifecycle/governance/agent-oriented treatment, while the version-sensitive contracts are reconciled to DataFusion 55 and Arrow 59.

```text
Library capability vs recommended architecture:
  "DataFusion provides / API / trait / function"
    -> engine capability.

  CalculationSpec / SchemaContract / PlanningArtifactBundle / catalog manifest /
  security policy / package layout
    -> recommended application architecture built on DataFusion, not a claim that
       DataFusion ships those application-level objects.
```

Historical headings that say a capability was “introduced in DataFusion 54” are retained to explain provenance. The deployable API target throughout this integrated release is DataFusion 55.0.0 / Arrow 59.2.0.


# Part II-A — Schema-first architecture and capability deep dives

# DataFusion Advanced — S1) Schema lifecycle and invariants across DataFusion

## S1.0 Objective

Treat schema as a **compiled contract** that crosses every DataFusion layer:

```text
external data / declared SQL / in-memory Arrow
  → Arrow Schema
  → catalog/table provider contract
  → DFSchema for logical planning
  → LogicalPlan output schema
  → optimized LogicalPlan output schema
  → ExecutionPlan output schema
  → RecordBatch runtime schema
  → sink/output schema
  → introspection + tests + diagnostics
```

The attached document already covers the main ingredients: Arrow `Schema` / `Field` / `DataType`, `RecordBatch`, `DFSchema`, schema qualifiers, catalog/provider hierarchy, and provider output requirements. This chapter’s added value is the **end-to-end invariant system**: where schemas originate, who owns them, where they are validated, how they are normalized, when metadata is preserved or discarded, and where drift must be rejected.  

This integrated reference is pinned to `datafusion 55.0.0`, uses Apache Arrow as the in-memory format, exposes SQL/DataFrame APIs, and allows customization across data sources, functions, operators, query languages, and planning/execution layers. ([Docs.rs][1])

---

## S1.1 Schema vocabulary: object taxonomy

```text
Arrow Schema
  = physical / interchange / runtime batch schema

DFSchema
  = logical planning schema
  = Arrow fields + optional qualifiers + logical resolution helpers

TableProvider::schema()
  = authoritative table/source contract exposed to planner

LogicalPlan::schema()
  = operator-derived logical output schema

ExecutionPlan::schema()
  = physical operator output schema communicated to physical optimizer/executor

RecordBatch::schema()
  = concrete runtime batch schema paired with actual Arrow arrays

Sink/output schema
  = persisted / serialized / API result schema after execution
```

Arrow `Schema` is metadata for an ordered sequence of field types and is not part of the physical memory layout; Arrow `Field` describes one column with name, data type, nullability, and custom metadata. ([Docs.rs][2]) ([Docs.rs][3])

`DFSchema` wraps Arrow schema information and adds relation/table qualification; it can contain qualified and unqualified fields, supports qualified schema creation, and can convert back to Arrow schema, at which point qualifier information is not retained as Arrow table/catalog metadata. ([Docs.rs][4])

`RecordBatch` is the runtime unit: a two-dimensional columnar dataset whose arrays must match the schema’s field count, field order, field data types, and equal column lengths. ([Docs.rs][5])

---

The catalog hierarchy is explicitly `CatalogProviderList → CatalogProvider → SchemaProvider → TableProvider`, and DataFusion’s catalog guide states that DDL such as `CREATE TABLE` is supported through this catalog API. ([Apache DataFusion][6])

## S1.3 Schema surfaces matrix

| Layer               | Schema object                           |                                         Owner |                             Mutability | Primary validation                 | Failure mode                                                |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------: | -------------------------------------: | ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| SQL DDL             | SQL column list                         |                      user / migration / agent |                    mutable through DDL | SQL planner + Arrow type mapping   | unsupported type, invalid nullability, duplicate column     |
| File source         | inferred Arrow `Schema`                 | file format / object store / listing provider |                       source-dependent | file metadata / inference / merge  | incompatible files, bad inference, partition conflict       |
| Rust in-memory data | `Arc<Schema>` + arrays                  |                              application code |           immutable after construction | `RecordBatch::try_new`             | field count/type/length/nullability mismatch                |
| Catalog             | schema/table namespace                  |          `CatalogProvider` / `SchemaProvider` |                       provider-defined | registration policy                | duplicate table, stale schema, unauthorized schema exposure |
| Table provider      | `TableProvider::schema()`               |                       provider implementation | should be stable per planning snapshot | provider tests + scan output tests | projected output mismatch                                   |
| Logical planner     | `DFSchema`                              |                            DataFusion planner |                                derived | binder/analyzer/type coercion      | missing/ambiguous column, type coercion failure             |
| Logical plan        | `LogicalPlan::schema()` / `DFSchemaRef` |                  DataFusion logical operators |                     immutable per plan | plan construction                  | invalid operator output schema                              |
| Physical plan       | `ExecutionPlan::schema()`               |                     physical planner/operator |                immutable per plan node | physical planning + invariants     | logical/physical mismatch                                   |
| Runtime stream      | `RecordBatch::schema()`                 |                     execution operator/stream |                  batch-level immutable | Arrow constructor + adapter checks | bad batch emitted                                           |
| Sink                | sink schema / output files              |                          writer/sink/provider |                           sink-defined | sink compatibility check           | persisted schema drift                                      |

DataFusion’s custom table-provider guide describes three cooperating layers: `TableProvider` describes the table and produces a plan, `ExecutionPlan` describes how to compute results, and `SendableRecordBatchStream` yields `RecordBatch` values during execution. ([Apache DataFusion][7])

---

## S1.4 Source-origin schemas

### S1.4.1 Declared SQL schema

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE refinery_streams (
    stream_id       VARCHAR NOT NULL,
    case_id         VARCHAR NOT NULL,
    unit_id         VARCHAR NOT NULL,
    component       VARCHAR NOT NULL,
    mass_flow_kg_h  DOUBLE  NOT NULL,
    sulfur_wt_pct   DOUBLE,
    event_ts        TIMESTAMP
)
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION 's3://lake/refinery/streams/';
```

SQL type declarations are mapped into Arrow data types during `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE` and `CAST`; string declarations map to `Utf8View` by default unless `datafusion.sql_parser.map_string_types_to_utf8view` is set to false. ([Apache DataFusion][8])

Agent rules:

```text
DDL schema = public contract.
Use explicit aliases / lowercase names.
Reject unsupported source dialect types before SQL planning.
Attach source metadata outside SQL where possible.
Snapshot DESCRIBE output after registration.
```

### S1.4.2 Inferred file schema

```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE taxi
STORED AS PARQUET
LOCATION '/mnt/nyctaxi/tripdata.parquet';

CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE raw_csv
STORED AS CSV
LOCATION '/path/to/raw.csv'
OPTIONS ('has_header' 'true');
```

Parquet external tables do not require an explicit schema because schema information is obtained from file metadata, while CSV tables infer schema by scanning a subset of the file unless a schema is supplied. DataFusion also incorporates Hive partition columns into schema/data when directory paths use Hive-compliant `key=value` partitioning. ([Apache DataFusion][9])

Agent rules:

```text
Parquet/Arrow/Avro:
  infer from embedded schema, then validate.

CSV/JSON:
  declare explicit schema for production.
  use inference for exploration only.
  route dirty input through staging schema + arrow_try_cast.

Directories:
  validate all files are schema-compatible.
  validate partition columns are expected.
  reject mixed schemas unless a deliberate merge/coercion policy exists.
```

### S1.4.3 Explicit Arrow schema

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;

use datafusion::arrow::datatypes::{DataType, Field, Schema, TimeUnit};

pub fn stream_schema() -> Arc<Schema> {
    Arc::new(Schema::new(vec![
        Field::new("stream_id", DataType::Utf8, false),
        Field::new("case_id", DataType::Utf8, false),
        Field::new("unit_id", DataType::Utf8, false),
        Field::new("mass_flow_kg_h", DataType::Float64, false),
        Field::new("sulfur_wt_pct", DataType::Float64, true),
        Field::new(
            "event_ts",
            DataType::Timestamp(TimeUnit::Nanosecond, Some("UTC".into())),
            true,
        ),
    ]))
}
```

Use explicit Arrow schemas for in-memory tests, generated data, custom providers, UDF outputs, adapter boundaries, and sink contracts. Use `datafusion::arrow` re-exports to prevent Arrow version bifurcation across DataFusion and application code; the attached document highlights this as a repeated invariant. 

---

## S1.5 Catalog and provider binding

```text
CatalogProviderList
  └─ CatalogProvider
      └─ SchemaProvider
          └─ TableProvider
              ├─ schema()      -> Arc<Schema>
              ├─ constraints() -> optional constraint metadata
              ├─ statistics()  -> optional planning metadata
              └─ scan(...)     -> Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>
```

`TableProvider` represents a source of Arrow `RecordBatch`es; its documented planning information includes `schema`, filter-pushdown support, and `scan`, with `schema()` returning the columns and types of the table. ([Docs.rs][10])

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;
use datafusion::catalog::{Session, TableProvider};
use datafusion::datasource::TableType;
use datafusion::arrow::datatypes::{Schema, SchemaRef};
use datafusion::logical_expr::Expr;
use datafusion::physical_plan::ExecutionPlan;
use datafusion::error::Result;

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ContractTable {
    schema: SchemaRef,
}

#[async_trait::async_trait]
impl TableProvider for ContractTable {
    fn schema(&self) -> SchemaRef {
        self.schema.clone()
    }

    fn table_type(&self) -> TableType {
        TableType::Base
    }

    async fn scan(
        &self,
        state: &dyn Session,
        projection: Option<&Vec<usize>>,
        filters: &[Expr],
        limit: Option<usize>,
    ) -> Result<Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>> {
        // projection indices are against self.schema()
        // filters are logical Exprs already bound against this table contract
        // returned ExecutionPlan::schema() must match requested projection
        todo!()
    }
}
```

DataFusion 54 removed the `fn as_any(&self)` boilerplate from the catalog traits: `TableProvider`, `SchemaProvider`, `CatalogProvider`, and `CatalogProviderList` now declare `Any` as a supertrait (e.g. `TableProvider: Any + Debug + Sync + Send`), so implementations no longer write an `as_any` method. Downcasting uses the inherent helpers on the trait object via trait upcasting: `provider.downcast_ref::<ContractTable>()` and `provider.is::<ContractTable>()` work directly on `&dyn TableProvider` and on `Arc<dyn TableProvider>` via auto-deref.

Hard provider invariant:

```text
TableProvider::schema()
  = full unprojected table schema

scan(projection = Some(indices))
  = ExecutionPlan with schema = schema.project(indices)

every emitted RecordBatch
  = exactly ExecutionPlan::schema()
```

The planning-time `TableSource` trait exists to expose a subset of `TableProvider` information such as schema and filter-pushdown capability without depending on the execution engine; this separation is useful when building logical-plan-only systems or alternate execution engines. ([Docs.rs][11])

---

## S1.6 Logical schema: `DFSchema`

### Role

```text
Arrow Schema
  = physical ordered fields

DFSchema
  = physical fields
  + optional table/relation qualifiers
  + logical column resolution
  + ambiguity detection
  + functional-dependency space
```

```rust
use datafusion::arrow::datatypes::{DataType, Field, Schema};
use datafusion::common::{Column, DFSchema};

let arrow_schema = Schema::new(vec![
    Field::new("id", DataType::Int64, false),
    Field::new("amount", DataType::Float64, true),
]);

let df_schema = DFSchema::try_from_qualified_schema("orders", &arrow_schema)?;

assert!(df_schema.has_column(&Column::from_qualified_name("orders.id")));
assert!(df_schema.has_column(&Column::from_qualified_name("id"))); // if unambiguous
```

`DFSchema` is the correct object for binding and validating expressions, not raw Arrow `Schema`, because logical expressions can reference qualified table columns. The attached document correctly frames `DFSchema` as the planning schema and Arrow `Schema` as the physical/runtime schema. 

### Qualifier-loss invariant

```rust
let arrow_only = df_schema.as_arrow();
// arrow_only contains fields + metadata
// arrow_only does not encode catalog/schema/table qualifiers as planner qualifiers
```

Hard invariant:

```text
DFSchema qualifiers are logical planner state.
Arrow Schema has no native DataFusion catalog/table qualifier semantics.
Converting DFSchema → Arrow Schema is a boundary crossing.
Do not expect qualifiers to survive RecordBatch / Parquet / Arrow IPC output.
```

---

## S1.7 Logical plan schema propagation

```text
Scan
  input: TableProvider::schema()
  output: DFSchema qualified by table/reference

Projection
  input: child DFSchema
  output: selected Expr::to_field results
  contract: aliases determine durable output names

Filter
  input: child DFSchema
  output: child DFSchema unchanged
  contract: predicate type must coerce to Boolean

Aggregate
  input: child DFSchema
  output: grouping fields + aggregate fields
  contract: aggregate aliases define stable schema

Join
  input: left DFSchema + right DFSchema
  output: combined DFSchema
  contract: duplicate names require qualification or aliasing

Union
  input: two compatible schemas
  output: coerced/merged schema
  contract: position or name semantics depend on API/operator

Sort / Limit
  input: child DFSchema
  output: child DFSchema unchanged

Window
  input: child DFSchema
  output: child fields + window expression fields
  contract: window expression aliases required for stable names

Unnest
  input: list/struct/map fields
  output: cardinality/field-shape transformed schema
  contract: output names must be explicit in stable APIs
```

`DataFrame::schema()` returns the `DFSchema` describing the output of a DataFrame, including name, data type, and nullability; `logical_plan()` returns the unoptimized logical plan, while `into_unoptimized_plan` / `into_optimized_plan` are documented as testing-oriented because they lose the attached `SessionState` snapshot. ([Docs.rs][12])

Agent rules:

```text
Validate after each schema-changing operation:
  select
  with_column
  aggregate
  join
  union
  unnest
  cast
  view creation
  CTAS
  sink write

Do not validate only after execution.
Most schema errors are planning-time errors and should be caught before collect().
```

---

## S1.8 Physical plan schema

```rust
use datafusion::prelude::*;
use datafusion::physical_plan::ExecutionPlan;

async fn inspect_physical_schema(ctx: &SessionContext) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    let df = ctx.sql("SELECT 1 AS x").await?;
    let physical = df.create_physical_plan().await?;
    let schema = physical.schema();

    for field in schema.fields() {
        println!("{}: {:?}, nullable={}", field.name(), field.data_type(), field.is_nullable());
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

`ExecutionPlan::execute(partition, context)` returns an async stream of `RecordBatch`es, and `ExecutionPlan::schema()` communicates the output schema of that physical node to the optimizer/executor. Execution should be streaming: most plans should not perform heavy work before the first batch is requested. ([Docs.rs][13])

Hard invariant:

```text
physical_plan.schema()
  == schema of every RecordBatch yielded by physical_plan.execute(...)
```

Recommended physical validation:

```rust
use datafusion::physical_plan::{ExecutionPlan, InvariantLevel};

fn validate_physical_plan(plan: &dyn ExecutionPlan) -> datafusion::error::Result<()> {
    plan.check_invariants(InvariantLevel::Always)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

Use `ExecutionPlan::check_invariants` in custom physical operators and regression tests when available in the pinned version. The exact invariant levels and method availability must be verified against the version-pinned docs.rs API. ([Docs.rs][13])

---

## S1.9 Runtime `RecordBatch` schema invariants

`RecordBatch::try_new(schema, columns)` expects non-empty columns, field count equal to column count, each field data type equal to the corresponding array data type, and all columns having equal length. ([Docs.rs][5])

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;
use datafusion::arrow::{
    array::{ArrayRef, Int64Array, StringArray},
    datatypes::{DataType, Field, Schema},
    record_batch::RecordBatch,
};

let schema = Arc::new(Schema::new(vec![
    Field::new("id", DataType::Int64, false),
    Field::new("name", DataType::Utf8, true),
]));

let columns: Vec<ArrayRef> = vec![
    Arc::new(Int64Array::from(vec![1, 2, 3])),
    Arc::new(StringArray::from(vec![Some("a"), None, Some("c")])),
];

let batch = RecordBatch::try_new(schema.clone(), columns)?;
assert_eq!(batch.schema(), schema);
```

Runtime contract:

```text
RecordBatch.schema().fields()[i].data_type() == RecordBatch.column(i).data_type()
RecordBatch.schema().fields().len() == RecordBatch.num_columns()
RecordBatch.column(i).len() == RecordBatch.num_rows()
RecordBatch.schema().fields()[i].is_nullable() == false implies no nulls in column i
RecordBatch column order is semantic
```

Do not use `RecordBatch::new_unchecked` in application/provider code unless a narrow, proven, internally audited hot path justifies skipping validation.

---

## S1.10 Sink and output schema

```text
Output paths:
  collect()
    -> Vec<RecordBatch>
    -> same schema for each batch

  execute_stream()
    -> SendableRecordBatchStream
    -> stream schema + every yielded batch schema

  write_parquet()
    -> Parquet schema / physical file schema

  write_csv()
    -> header / serialized scalar field names

  write_json()
    -> serialized field names/types inferred from Arrow values

  write_table()
    -> TableProvider::insert_into target schema contract

  DataSink
    -> sink.schema()
    -> write_all(stream, task_context)
```

Sink schema policy:

```text
Sink-owned schema must be explicit before write.
Never infer output schema from first batch only.
Empty result sets still require schema.
File writers should use plan/schema contract, not sampled runtime rows.
Partition columns require explicit policy:
  kept in payload
  removed from payload
  duplicated in path + payload
```

For service APIs, the output schema is an API contract:

```json
{
  "schema_fingerprint": "sha256:...",
  "fields": [
    {"name": "stream_id", "data_type": "Utf8", "nullable": false},
    {"name": "mass_flow_kg_h", "data_type": "Float64", "nullable": false}
  ],
  "qualifiers": "stripped",
  "source_plan_hash": "..."
}
```

---

## S1.11 Hard invariants

### Invariant 1 — Provider schema must match execution output

```text
TableProvider::schema()
  → scan(projection)
  → ExecutionPlan::schema()
  → RecordBatchStream::schema()
  → every RecordBatch::schema()
```

Violation examples:

```text
provider schema says [id:Int64, name:Utf8]
scan(projection=[0]) emits [name:Utf8]
stream schema says [id:Int64] but batch emits [id:Int32]
projection index maps against backend order instead of TableProvider::schema order
```

Required test:

```rust
fn assert_batch_schema_eq(expected: &Schema, batch: &RecordBatch) {
    assert_eq!(expected.fields(), batch.schema().fields());
}
```

### Invariant 2 — Logical qualifiers do not survive Arrow conversion

```text
DFSchema:
  orders.id
  customers.id

Arrow Schema:
  id
  id
```

Required policy:

```text
Before Arrow boundary:
  preserve qualifiers for binding/ambiguity checks.

At output boundary:
  alias/rename columns into deterministic unique names.

After Arrow boundary:
  do not attempt to recover qualifiers unless stored explicitly in custom metadata.
```

### Invariant 3 — Output field names must be deterministic

Bad:

```sql
SELECT SUM(amount), amount * 1.08, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (...)
FROM t
GROUP BY amount;
```

Good:

```sql
SELECT
  SUM(amount) AS total_amount,
  amount * 1.08 AS amount_with_tax,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY amount DESC) AS amount_rank
FROM t
GROUP BY amount
ORDER BY amount_rank;
```

Agent rule:

```text
Every computed expression must have an alias:
  arithmetic
  cast
  aggregate
  window
  case
  scalar function
  nested extraction
  unnest
  generated expression
```

### Invariant 4 — `RecordBatch` array order/type/nullability must match schema

```text
Schema fields are ordered.
Column vectors are ordered.
Names do not remap runtime arrays.
```

Bad:

```rust
Schema:  [id:Int64, name:Utf8]
Columns: [StringArray(name), Int64Array(id)]
```

Good:

```rust
Schema:  [id:Int64, name:Utf8]
Columns: [Int64Array(id), StringArray(name)]
```

### Invariant 5 — Planning schema is not execution proof

```text
df.schema()
  proves planner output contract

collect().await?
  proves execution succeeded for this run

RecordBatch::try_new tests
  prove provider/adaptor emitted valid batches

physical_plan.check_invariants()
  proves some physical plan structural invariants
```

Agent rule:

```text
Validate at planning boundary and runtime boundary.
Do not treat one as replacement for the other.
```

---

## S1.12 Schema ownership model

| Ownership class       | Owns                                 | Examples                                                          | Authority               | Drift policy                       |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| Source-owned schema   | physical storage contract            | Parquet footer, Avro schema, Arrow IPC schema, remote DB metadata | storage/source          | reject or adapt at ingestion       |
| Catalog-owned schema  | namespace binding and table identity | `prod.analytics.events` table schema                              | catalog/metastore       | version, cache, refresh            |
| Provider-owned schema | DataFusion scan contract             | `TableProvider::schema()`                                         | provider implementation | freeze per query planning snapshot |
| Query-derived schema  | operator output                      | projection/aggregate/join/window/union                            | planner/analyzer        | deterministic derivation           |
| Sink-owned schema     | persisted/API output                 | Parquet file, JSON API, target table insert schema                | writer/target provider  | enforce compatibility before write |

### Source-owned schema

```text
Schema source:
  Parquet footer
  Avro file schema
  Arrow IPC schema
  CSV inferred header + sampled data
  remote database INFORMATION_SCHEMA
```

Policy:

```text
Do not mutate source schema in place.
Create normalized DataFusion-facing schema.
Record source fingerprint.
Reject incompatible changes unless migration policy exists.
```

### Catalog-owned schema

```text
catalog.schema.table → TableProvider
```

Policy:

```text
Catalog controls visibility, naming, tenancy, persistence, refresh.
Catalog should not perform heavy scans during listing.
Catalog should expose stable TableProvider snapshot per query.
```

### Provider-owned schema

```text
TableProvider::schema() = contract exposed to DataFusion.
```

Policy:

```text
Cheap clone of Arc<Schema>.
No surprise network calls in schema().
No per-batch shape drift.
Projection indices are interpreted against this schema.
```

### Query-derived schema

```text
SELECT a AS x, b + c AS y FROM t
  → [x:type(a), y:type(b+c)]
```

Policy:

```text
Aliases stabilize field names.
Casts stabilize field types.
Qualifiers stabilize resolution before output.
```

### Sink-owned schema

```text
write_parquet(path)
  → final Parquet schema

write_table(target)
  → target TableProvider insert contract

execute_stream()
  → stream schema contract
```

Policy:

```text
Validate before write.
Treat empty output schema as meaningful.
Snapshot output schema in CI.
```

---

## S1.13 Validation checkpoints

```text
Checkpoint 0 — schema construction
  Rust: Schema::new, Field::new
  SQL: CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE explicit columns
  File: DESCRIBE / schema inference audit

Checkpoint 1 — registration
  catalog.table_exist()
  table_provider.schema()
  information_schema.columns

Checkpoint 2 — expression binding
  ExprSchemable::get_type(df_schema)
  ExprSchemable::nullable(df_schema)
  missing/ambiguous column rejection

Checkpoint 3 — logical plan
  df.schema()
  df.logical_plan().schema()
  optimized plan schema snapshot

Checkpoint 4 — physical plan
  df.create_physical_plan().await?.schema()
  ExecutionPlan::check_invariants(...)

Checkpoint 5 — runtime batch
  RecordBatch::try_new(...)
  stream schema vs batch schema
  all batches same schema

Checkpoint 6 — sink
  writer schema
  target TableProvider insert compatibility
  Parquet/Arrow metadata inspection
```

### Minimal Rust validation harness

```rust
use datafusion::arrow::datatypes::SchemaRef;
use datafusion::arrow::record_batch::RecordBatch;
use datafusion::common::DFSchema;
use datafusion::prelude::*;

pub fn assert_arrow_schema_eq(expected: &SchemaRef, actual: &SchemaRef) {
    assert_eq!(expected.fields(), actual.fields(), "field mismatch");
    assert_eq!(expected.metadata(), actual.metadata(), "schema metadata mismatch");
}

pub fn assert_batch_schema_eq(expected: &SchemaRef, batch: &RecordBatch) {
    assert_arrow_schema_eq(expected, &batch.schema());
}

pub fn assert_df_schema_has_unique_names(df_schema: &DFSchema) {
    let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();

    for (_qualifier, field) in df_schema.iter() {
        let inserted = seen.insert(field.name().to_string());
        assert!(inserted, "duplicate output field name: {}", field.name());
    }
}

pub async fn validate_dataframe_schema(df: DataFrame) -> datafusion::error::Result<Vec<RecordBatch>> {
    let logical_schema = df.schema().clone();

    assert_df_schema_has_unique_names(&logical_schema);

    let batches = df.collect().await?;

    if let Some(first) = batches.first() {
        let output_schema = first.schema();
        for batch in &batches {
            assert_batch_schema_eq(&output_schema, batch);
        }
    }

    Ok(batches)
}
```
